News.title: Joiner wore woman’s bras and underwear while in home to carry out work but forgot to take them off after plumber arrived
News.content:
'I'VE BEEN STUPID' Joiner wore woman’s bras and underwear while in home to carry out work but forgot to take them off after plumber arrived

A JOINER wore a woman’s bras and underwear while working in her home but forgot to take them off after a plumber arrived.

Neil Wilson, 46, was carrying out work at the home in Ingol, a suburb in northwest Preston, Lancashire, in early July when he was caught on a security camera going in and out of the upstairs bedrooms.

The work he had been hired to do involved only working downstairs.



He started to go through the drawers, picking out various bras and underwear before trying them on and stopping to sniff them.



When he left, he also took a pair of underwear.

He found the camera at one point and moved it out of the way so he was no longer visible.

When the victims returned home, they made a report and Wilson was arrested.



Wilson told the cops: “I’ve done something stupid”.

He then took the officers to see the other items he had stolen – a pair of underwear in his works van.

Wilson, of Chorley, admitted to trying on the underwear when interviewed, but said he didn’t mean to steal them.

He claimed he had been disrupted by the arrival of a plumber and had to get changed to answer the door, leaving them on under his work clothes.



He pleaded guilty to burglary and theft from a dwelling at Preston Magistrates Court and was sentenced to 12 months in prison, suspended for 12 months, and was ordered to pay compensation and costs.

DS Ben Barnes of South Residential Burglary Team said: “Wilson entered an area of a property that he didn’t have access to, whilst alone and trusted to complete the work he was hired for. He betrayed that trust.

“I hope he now has time to reflect on his actions, and the victim feels some sense of justice now criminal proceedings have been completed.”

News.title: Pubs’ hope for VAT cut dashed after minister’s cost warning – despite Burnham supporting tax slash before entering No10
News.content:
POUR CHOICES Pubs’ hope for VAT cut dashed after minister’s cost warning – despite Burnham supporting tax slash before entering No10

PUBS hoping for a VAT cut were dealt a blow yesterday after a Treasury minister warned slashing the tax would cost “a lot of money”.

James Murray cooled hopes of cutting hospitality VAT from 20 to 10 per cent despite Andy Burnham backing the move before becoming PM.



The Financial Secretary to the Treasury said any cut would have to be “fully funded” and offer taxpayers value for money.

He told The Sun: “We want to support hospitality, but let’s be upfront about this. “If you’re having a big cut in VAT, it costs a lot of money, and anything that we announce, we want to make sure it’s fully funded, and we explain exactly how we’re going to do that.



“So, when the Prime Minister announced 20 per cent cut off business rates last month, we said exactly how we were going to pay for that.”

Mr Murray insisted he would “not get ahead of anything that might be announced at the Budget”, adding: “But we need to keep looking at how we can support high streets and particularly pubs because they’re so important to everyone right across the country.”

Mr Burnham backed calls for a 10 per cent hospitality VAT rate before entering No10, arguing the sector needed more help.

Top chefs including Tom Kerridge threw their weight behind his stance at the time.

But the Government has so far focused its latest support on business rates, announcing a further 20 per cent reduction for pubs from April 2027.

The Treasury has also launched a review into the way pubs and hotels are valued for business rates after sharp increases at the 2026 revaluation.



UKHospitality boss Kate Nicholls said: “As the Prime Minister acknowledged earlier this year – and as we have seen this summer – cutting VAT is the fastest way to tackle the cost of living, make everyday treats for families more affordable and bear down on inflation.

It boosts consumer confidence, generates economic growth and much needed tax revenues and has the quickest payback in terms of jobs.

“If the PM is serious about delivering growth in every postcode, a high street renaissance and tackling the NEETs crisis this is the lever to pull.”

News.title: Airport worker hit and killed on tarmac by taxiing passenger plane in ‘unfortunate incident’ as probe launched
News.content:
PLANE HORROR Airport worker hit and killed on tarmac by taxiing passenger plane in ‘unfortunate incident’ as probe launched

A RUNWAY marshal has died after he was allegedly struck by a taxiing plane at one of Canada’s busiest airports.

The employee was hit by the French bee budget airliner as it reversed in front of horrified passengers at Montreal airport, police said.



The victim, said to be in his forties, was rushed to hospital but later succumbed to his injuries.

Recalling the horrific incident, one witness told Radio-Canada that “many passengers were screaming.”



She said that she saw the man pass under the plane while it was moving before the fatal hit occurred.

Montreal airport mourned the loss of the worker, describing the incident as an “unfortunate and tragic workplace accident”.

Airport president and CEO Yves Beauchamp said: “The loss of a member of our airport community affects us all deeply.

“During this difficult time, our thoughts are with the employee’s family, loved ones and colleagues, to whom we extend our heartfelt sympathy and sincere condolences.”

The airport refused to comment further “out of respect for the victim and their loved ones”.

The plane involved was scheduled to take-off bound for Paris at 6pm on Monday, with emergency measures being deployed at 7.30pm.



It had reportedly been scheduled to leave the day before, but was postponed due to a technical problem.

Police have ruled out a criminal investigation into the tragedy but two probes have been launched into the incident.

French bee said that it is cooperating with investigators.

The airline added: “[Our] immediate priority is caring for those affected by the incident and supporting its passengers and crew.”

The tragedy comes a month after an aircraft engineer died after he was crushed to death inside a Boeing 787 fuel tank.



Machinery suddenly fell on popular aircraft technician Georgie Buxton at Heathrow Airport.

Buxton, 23, was rushed to hospital after the horrifying accident, which happened as he was carrying out maintenance tests inside a hangar on June 11.

His family later took the heartbreaking decision to switch off his life support.

The plane he was working on has been taken out of service since the accident while experts try to understand how the tragedy occurred.

A source told The Sun: “Georgie was a young and very loved member of the team. Everyone at Virgin is in shock.

News.title: Controversial TikTok & Netflix Inside the Manosphere streamer Ed Matthews is jailed over ‘paedophile’ assault
News.content:
CONTROVERSIAL “Manosphere” streamer Ed Matthews has been jailed for 12 weeks over an alleged paedophile sting.

Matthews, who appeared in Louis Theroux’s Inside the Manosphere doc, live-streamed himself assaulting an alleged paedophile alongside a group of “paedophile hunters”.



The 24-year-old, who is a close friend of streamer HSTikkyTokky, was handed a community order over the assault in June 2024.

He was fined £264 and told to complete 150 hours of unpaid work and rehabilitation activity days as part of his sentence.



However, due to his failure to comply with the order he was jailed for 12 weeks at Basildon Magistrates Court on August 19.

Matthews’ streamer pals have since shared their outrage over his sentence in online posts.



HSTikkyTokky posted about Matthews’ arrest and branded his sentencing as “absolutely ridiculous”.

Matthews was convicted of assault by beating and using threatening and abusive language or behaviour likely to cause harassment, alarm or distress at Willesden Magistrates’ Court last year.



The man Matthews was convicted of beating is due to stand trial in 2028 for attempting to meet a child after grooming them.

In the streamer’s filmed ambush of the alleged paedophile, he tells him to eat an extremely spicy Hot Chip or be arrested by the police.

Matthews wrestles the man to the ground and then holds him down in the video.

In an update, Matthews has now shared a recorded phone call message for his fans from prison.

In a video shared on his Instagram page, he says “I’m on a peak bang up right now, 23 hours a day because I’m high profile. All alone in my cell.



“But guess what I’m grateful still, something I was preaching in Africa. I love you man. I’m good.

“I’m going to go so much f***ing harder when I come out with these streams.

“I’m so motivated.

“I’m getting treated like a f***ing murderer and that predator is walking free. The system is f****d.”

He told his followers to turn up to his next court date in September.

News.title: Mystery over colourful sea slug discovered by diver exploring shipwreck off UK coast as experts think it’s a new species
News.content:
SEA RIDDLE Mystery over colourful sea slug discovered by diver exploring shipwreck off UK coast as experts think it’s a new species

A TINY brightly-coloured sea slug discovered by a diver exploring a shipwreck off the British coast could be a brand new species, experts say.

Diver Maggs Ashton discovered the striking orange, purple and white nudibranch off Lundy, Devon.



Measuring just 0.6 inches long, the mysterious creature was found around 65ft underwater among the wreckage of the MV Robert, which sank in 1975.

Marine naturalist Bernard Picton said the discovery was significant and believes the sea critter is likely to be a species never formally identified before.



Maggs said the colourful sea slug immediately caught her eye despite its tiny size.

She said: “I was just swimming along and not really looking that carefully when I suddenly saw it.

“It just stood out, and I’d never seen anything like it before in my 29 or 30 years of diving – it was really special.”

Maggs sent snaps of her unusual find to marine biologists, who told her it appeared to be a species that had not previously been documented.



She has since returned to the wreck in the hope of finding it again, but so far has had no luck.

“I’ve actually been back to the wreck to try and see it again, but I can’t find it,” she said.

“Hopefully it is just hiding and hasn’t been eaten by a fish.”

Picton believes the creature could be an undescribed species belonging to Lomanotus, a genus of sea slug.

He said: “I think it is likely to be an undescribed Lomanotus species.



“In scientific terms, this is significant – an ‘undescribed species’ is one that has never been formally identified, named and documented in the scientific literature.”

The association has now urged divers, rockpoolers, sailors and fishers to keep their eyes peeled for similar creatures and submit any photographs to its data archive centre, DASSH.

A spokesperson said the records help scientists build a clearer picture of how Britain’s coasts and seas are changing as waters warm, including sightings of “unusual visitors and shifting species ranges”.

The association added: “The discovery is another reminder that the marine life around Britain is ever-changing.”

It comes after young rockpoolers taking part in the monthly Rock Pool Project Bioblitz discovered a rare depilatory sea hare on Mount Batten beach in Plymouth in 2025.

News.title: Moment hero passerby catches toddler, 2, as youngster plummets from 20ft-high ledge she was clinging to
News.content:
THIS is the startling moment a heroic passerby caught a two-year-old toddler after she fell from a 20ft-high ledge she had been clinging to.

Footage shows the youngster lowering her legs over the side of the 6m-high ledge.



A passer-by spots her after being alerted by someone shouting, then runs over to the pavement and stretches out his arms beneath her.

The girl lowers herself from the ledge and plunges towards the ground, with the man partially catching her before she slips from his grip and lands on the pavement.



The dramatic incident unfolded in Bozhou, China, on August 21.

Thanks to the quick actions of passer-by Chu Liang, the girl emerged from the ordeal with nothing more serious than a fractured ankle.

The girl had ended up on the ledge after apparently climbing out of a window.

Her mother, Ms Wang, told local media she had been tidying up at home when her daughter somehow locked the front door.



Worried that something might happen to her, Wang tried to kick the door open but was unable to do so.

As she was looking for the key, she heard people shouting downstairs.

When she went outside, she discovered that her daughter had fallen from the building but had fortunately been caught by someone.

Chu, 39, believes he absorbed most of the force from the fall.

Wang tried to give him money as a thank-you, but he refused, also declining to give her his name or phone number.



She only learned his name later from local media.

She said: “Chu Liang saved my child, so of course I have to thank him. Otherwise, I would feel terrible.”

The girl has been recovering in bed following a visit to the doctor.

The impact left Chu unable to raise his arm for a day, while his leg and lower back remained sore.

He told local media that he felt guilty because he had not managed to catch the girl completely.

He said: “If I had managed to catch the child, she wouldn’t have been injured.”

However, he felt relieved after learning that she had not suffered any serious injuries.

News.title: Cruise ship worker, 38, admits having sex with underage girl in his cabin twice as he’s arrested on return to port
News.content:
CRUISE CREEP Cruise ship worker, 38, admits having sex with underage girl in his cabin twice as he’s arrested on return to port

A CREEPY cruise ship lifeguard has admitted to having sex twice with an underage girl in his cabin, police said.

Guatemalan lifeguard Rafael Cayetano Blanco, 38, was cuffed as the MSC World America liner docked at port in Miami.

The accused pervert is now being held on an immigration detainer.



Blanco told cops that he exchanged numbers with a 17-year-old passenger on August 16 – the first day of the cruise.



He admitted that the pair then returned to his cabin to have sex, according to a police report.

She returned to his cabin again three days later and they had sex once again, cops said.

After confessing to both incidents, Blanco was charged with unlawful sexual activity with a minor.

The 38-year-old remains locked up on an immigration hold.

The mega cruise ship can carry more than 6,700 passengers and 2,100 crew.

It set sail from Miami on August 15 before making scheduled stops in Honduras, Mexico and the Bahamas, according to Cruisemapper.

MSC said in a statement: “On discovery of a breach of conduct by a crew member and an alleged criminal act, we immediately contacted the relevant law enforcement authorities.



“We fully supported the investigation and provided every assistance to the guest.

“The crew member concerned has been dismissed.”

It comes after a 25-year-old creep allegedly tried to take pictures up a 13-year-old girl’s dress on a a Royal Caribbean liner.

Matthew Stilwell, 25, from Illinois is accused of trying to take the pervy pictures in a gift shop on the ship.

The teenage girl noticed Stilwell “standing unusually close behind her with the camera application on his cellphone”, according to a police report seen by WPLG.



She told cops he tried to snap a picture at least three times before she ran over to her mum.

Authorities boarded the ‘Allure of the Seas’ when it returned to Port Everglades in Florida, and checked CCTV.

Cops said they found security footage corroborating the young girl’s version of events.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Stilwell allegedly confessed to investigators, but his admission was redacted in the report.

He has since been charged with voyeurism and is currently being held at the Paul Rein Detention Facility in Pompano Beach.

News.title: How Harry’s return can spark dramatic redemption. Hear me out – but the Royal Family NEED pariah prince back in fold
News.content:
SO, the wanderers return. Yes, Harry and Meghan are blighty-bound after the Californian dream imploded and their situation turned as sticky as one of the Duchess’s unsold jams.

Surprise, surprise as soon the pairs drip feed of Royal disses dried up so too did America’s interest – dumped by Netflix and deserted by many of their A-list cronies.



But if America is bored, the UK is rightly aggrieved over the couple’s Megxit U-turn especially when it comes to hapless Harry.

Unlike Meghan, he and the British public have history. In short we once cared which is why his recent betrayals have felt so personal.

Airing the family secrets to the highest bidder during the ailing Queen’s final years squandered his popularity and will be hard to forgive.



Yet, despite this, the stage could still be set for his redemption.

Hear me out. Harry has many flaws but also some key attributes. He has charisma and a natural connection with the public reminiscent of his late mother Diana, a common touch amid the polish and privilege.

Having grown out of the more rebellious excesses of his youth he retains the boyish charm that made him a crowd favourite.

It’s this endearing side that established the goodwill towards him for so long and can still be clawed back if he chooses a more productive return to public life.

And this would be long overdue.



You see, it’s ironic that the title of the duke’s infamous tell-all memoir – Spare – (available in every good charity shop) could in fact have been more accurately applied to his life in LA.

Treading water for six years as Meghan’s plus-one, the fifth in line to the throne so often seemed reduced to a spare part on the sidelines of many tacky stunts and projects.

Remember the 40-year-old’s awkward expression as his wife blabbed to Netflix about her first meeting with late Queen Elizabeth in the 2022 docu-series, Harry & Meghan and reenacted a mocking theatrical curtsy?



Not to mention his toe- curling cameos in her Netflix lifestyle series, With Love.

Ostensibly it was to applaud her brunch-making skills but as always, he seemed he was simply on hand to ramp up the royal connection.

Throughout the sorry mess of Megxit, only Harry’s work with the Invictus Games felt like a rare injection of purpose and positivity – a reminder of where his talents lie and why he can’t be written off yet.

Winning back the hearts of the British people won’t be easy.

The first step will be unlocking his arm from Meghan’s tight grip and forging a more independent path that plays to his strengths.



A greater focus on charity work and building on Diana’s legacy through his support of landmine clearance charity The Halo Trust is an obvious starting point.

Meanwhile, the rumour mill suggests Meghan will find plenty to fill her days, whether that’s a return to the small screen or establishing her own court among other celebrity American expats in the Cotswolds.

No doubt it will involve too many meet-and-greets – the mainstay duty of royal life. From the outset the former Suits star always seemed to be cos-playing at the gig keen to be a Diana 2.0 but with an eye more on the commercial than compassion.

Harry at least appears more authentic and for all the rows and recriminations his absence has been felt.

In the wake of the scandal surrounding Andrew Mountbatten Windsor’s links with convicted paedophile Jeffery Epstein, the Royal family has taken a heavy reputational knock.



Yes, a hardworking King and Queen and a stoic and dedicated William and Kate have successfully steadied the ship but at times it still feels depleted offering.

The line-up would benefit from the different dimension that Harry – ideally freed up from his all consuming legal battles with the press and some of the tedious self-pity – can still offer.

The big question remains just what form this could take.

News.title: Barcelona fire LIVE: 'Explosion' heard as blaze burns 25 hectares and residents told 'stay indoors'
News.content:
A huge fire has broken out in Barcelona, with smoke visible from a Ryanair flight amid unconfirmed reports of an explosion

A large fire is burning in Barcelona, with around 35 hectares of land affected and residents in two neighbourhoods told to stay indoors.

Mobile phone alerts have been sent to people in Torre Baró and Ciutat Meridiana, warning them to close their doors and windows and not go outside due to the vegetation fire.

People posting on X have reported hearing an explosion, while a high-voltage tower in the area is believed to have been damaged. The explosion report has not yet been confirmed by authorities.

Spain’s 112 emergency service has received 1,074 calls about the blaze, while firefighters continue to tackle the flames.

The emergency warning tells residents: “Close doors and windows and do not go out on the street. In case of emergency, call 112.”

News.title: Dolly Parton's life in photos from young country star to glam icon before death at 80
News.content:
Country music legend Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80.

Her nephew, Bryan Seaver, confirmed the sad news in a video shared with the star's 8.7 million Instagram followers, announcing she had been welcomed by "the arms of Jesus".

"This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago, before I fully absorbed it as a future reality," Seaver said. "As her head of security for more than two decades, a role my father Larry held before me, I have imagined the heaviness of this moment, but haven't truly felt it until now."

Seaver, the son of Dolly's sister Cassie Parton, said his aunt is now "in the arms of Jesus, surely met by her late husband Carl and her parents" in the heavens. He said Dolly had "opened doors for generations of singers, songwriters, musicians, and dreamers from every walk of life and across every continent."

The announcement comes after Dolly pulled out of an event at Dollywood due to poor health. In a new interview just this month, she said: "I am dealing with some health issues that I just didn't pay attention to when I was watching over Carl.

"It's not like I haven't been through hard times with my health. But I think because we live in a 24/7 world with social media, everything gets magnified in ways it wasn’t years ago."

Here is Dolly Parton's remarkable life in pictures - from the young girl with big dreams to her rise as country music royalty and the beloved icon in her later years.

News.title: A66 crash that killed seven 'sparked by turf war' after home of teen victim's dad 'ram raided' in early hours
News.content:
A66 crash that killed seven 'sparked by turf war' after home of teen victim's dad 'ram raided' in early hours

Five more arrests have been made in connection with the A66 crash near Middlesborough. A 16-year-old boy and two men, aged 18 and 21, were arrested on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group.

A66 crash: Police cordon remains in place on Teeside

Five more people were arrested today amid claims the A66 crash was sparked by a feud between rival crime gangs.

‌



A 16-year-old boy and two men, aged 18 and 21, were arrested on suspicion of participating in an organised crime group. A 55-year-old man was also held on suspicion of assisting an offender. A 23-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of making threats to kill. All five remained in custody, Cleveland Police said.

‌



The update from police of the further arrests came as the fundraisers for the families of PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, neared the £1m mark. More than £900,000 has been pledged to two separate Gofundme appeals. PC Clough and PC Blades died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, and Cole Robert Worthy, both 17.

‌



View 7 Images From left to right: Makai Saddington, Theo Rae, Cole Robert Worthy, Michael Robert Cahill, Jakub Matusiak

Fundraiser for Cleveland police officers killed in A66 crash exceeds £750k READ MORE :

All seven were killed when a Volkswagen Passat, going the wrong way down the A66 at South Bank, hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle heading in the opposite direction at 3.39am on Saturday. The home of Cole Worthy's father was allegedly ram-raided at 3am on Saturday, just 40 minutes before the devastating crash.

It is alleged that a Volvo XC60 was used, and that vehicle is now central to the police investigation into the tragedy. The house is believed to belong to Gye Worthy, Cole's father. A vehicle deliberately reversed into the front window twice, causing extensive damage, according to those living close to the scene.

‌



View 7 Images Tribute to Cole Worthy who died in the A66 crash

Within minutes, a VW Passat containing his son Cole and four friends was racing around Middlesbrough, pursuing the Volvo allegedly involved in the attack. The Passat was later spotted by a police patrol, resulting in the horrific crash that killed PC Clough and PC Blades. There is no suggestion Gye Worthy, 39, a company director, was involved in any criminal activity. But the attack on his home appeared to be the flashpoint for the chase between rival gangs.

The chain of events that led to the tragedy began in Acklam, Middlesbrough. One neighbour of the Worthys said Cole's father had lived at the address for around ten years and led 'a normal life'. Another heard a 'loud bang' and looked out to see the damage.

‌



View 7 Images PC Tom Clough, one of two Cleveland Police officers killed in a car crash on the A66 near Middlesbrough (Image: ncjMedia Ltd)

Cleveland Police confirmed both the Volvo and VW Passat were part of their enquiries in the early hours of August 22. But they declined to comment on claims that rival gangs were involved in the police chase that led to the crash.

Mr Worthy's home was rammed at around 3am. By 3.36am, the VW Passat was caught on CCTV racing at between 80 and 100mph down Lime Road in Teesville, pursued by three police vehicles. At 3.39am, it turned the wrong way onto the A66 dual carriageway, at which point the pursuing police vehicles stopped. Just ten seconds later, it smashed head-on into the armed response vehicle carrying PCs Clough and Blades.

‌



View 7 Images PC Matthew Blades, who died when a car going in the wrong direction hit a police car on the A66 near Middlesbrough (Image: Cleveland Police/PA Wire)

Cleveland Police said two of the 12 people previously arrested in connection with the A66 collision have now appeared in court. The further arrests brings the total held in connection to the investigation to 17.

Kai Beattie, 19, of Foxrush Court, Redcar, appeared at Teesside Magistrates' Court charged with possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life, according to the police. Cameron George, 26, of Micklow Close, Redcar, was remanded in custody to appear at Teesside Crown Court on September 21 charged with drugs offences and possession of criminal property, it said. A spokesman for Cleveland Police said: "On the morning of Saturday 22 August, Cleveland Police received several reports of two vehicles being driven dangerously. The first vehicle, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was witnessed ramming properties in the Middlesbrough area. The second vehicle, a Volkswagen Passat, is believed to have been associated with the activities of the Volvo XC60."

‌



View 7 Images Flares lit during a balloon release in memory of Jakub Matusiak, 23, who died in the A66 crash (Image: North News & Pictures Ltd)

Youths wearing balaclavas set off flares and fireworks in a noisy tribute to the five dead youths following the crash. Friends of Jakub Matusiak, 23, gathered at a field in South Bank, Middlesbrough, close to the scene of Saturday's catastrophic collision.

A gang of around 20 masked youths on motorbikes and quad bikes roared around the field in honour of Mr Matusiak, who had convictions for motoring offences. The scenes sparked fury on social media.

‌



One commentator wrote: "I get it that their families and friends will be devastated and grieving, but surely in circumstances where they have killed two innocent men who were simply out doing their jobs, you grieve in private?" Writing on Facebook, a woman accused the mourners of showing "disrespect of the highest level for the two murdered policemen" and said a quiet vigil would have been more appropriate.

View 7 Images Flares light up the skies during a balloon release in memory of Jakub Matusiak, 23, (Image: North News & Pictures Ltd)

Paul Williams, acting deputy national chairman for the Police Federation of England and Wales, told BBC Breakfast: "Every day we can identify now numerous examples of young people sensationalising dangerous driving. Not just dangerous driving, but baiting police officers who are out there to protect the public.

‌



"It's a real problem. It's causing officers concern. They shouldn't have to be going out and worrying about whether they're going to return home from their shift or not. But on top of that, wondering if they’re going to be plastered all over social media. It's absolutely unacceptable and social media platforms need to take some action."

Offers of support have come in from as far afield as Australia. Officers from other forces contacted Cleveland Police to cover shifts for the distressed colleagues of the fallen officers. The number of donations on a police federation page has reached almost 30,000.

View 7 Images The crash scene on the A66 in South Bank, near Middlesbrough (Image: Owen Humphreys/PA Wire)

‌



The extraordinary show of support for their families came as the Government also called upon social media companies to remove videos of drivers recording police pursuits. Matt Storey, police and crime commissioner for Cleveland, called on the community to reach out to police officers. "Reach out and put your arm around them," he said. "They are people behind the uniforms."

He told the Mirror that filming behind the wheel was becoming an "incredibly dangerous and idiotic" trend. He added: "Parents have a responsibility to tell their children what they should be doing on the road. But also have to demand more from TikTok and social media platforms to remove content. They have a responsibility regarding public safety to get this taken off their platforms. They have to be careful about what is on their site.

"We need to tighten the legislation. It is like the wild west. I have met with many young people about misinformation and exploitation. They understand social media is dangerous; their reaction was that it must be regulated more tightly."

Article continues below

Lauren Somerville, chairwoman of Cleveland Police Federation, said: “It’s so hard to describe how this grief feels and how it will feel. Policing is so unique, so unique. We are injected into the darkest moments in people’s lives, whether that be arresting somebody or you know, saving a life.

"Whatever it is, officers forge relationships that might happen in a moment or over a full career together, and you cannot describe the grief."

News.title: Brits stranded in Tunisia for almost three days after easyJet flight cancelled
News.content:
Brits stranded in Tunisia for almost three days after easyJet flight cancelled

Passengers who were left stranded at Tunisia's Enfidha airport after their flight to Belfast was cancelled are finally due to return home

View 3 Images Passengers were left stranded at Tunisia's Enfidha airport after their flight to Belfast was cancelled (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Around 150 easyJet passengers have been left stranded in Tunisia for almost three days after their flight to Belfast was cancelled.

‌



Passengers due to fly with the low-cost carrier from Tunisia's Enfidha airport on Saturday night were already waiting at the gate when they were told their flight to Belfast was not going to take off. Parents, children, pregnant women and the elderly were all reportedly among those affected, facing uncertainty about when they might return home.

‌



Flight EZY3072 was cancelled after experiencing a technical issue, with alternative services, including with other carriers, “very limited” due to the large number of people travelling at this time of year. Passenger Gina Dochartaigh expressed her frustration on social media, saying she was stranded on her own with her six children after her husband had to cut his holiday short due to a family emergency.

‌



Ms Dochartaigh said: "Over 150 passengers have been stranded in Tunisia since Saturday night. After 4 hr delay, Easyjet cancelled EZY 3072 from Enfidha to Belfast International Sat 22nd - early Sunday morning due to technical issues. They sent for an engineer from the UK but the plane is still out of service.

"EasyJet have only arranged and paid for 2 nights accommodation for affected passengers and have now completely relinquished their duty of care to their passengers. There has been no engagement team set up by the airline to liaise with passengers, zero transparency and seemingly no contingency plan for a cancelled flight exceeding 3 days! Complete communication blackout!

"I'm here on my own with 6 children as my husband had to cut his holiday short, and flew out the day before departure on Friday on 21st due to a family emergency. There are two pregnant women travelling with disabled children, elderly passengers who require special assistance and passengers running out of medication."

‌



View 3 Images Around 150 people were already waiting at the gate at Enfidha Airport (Image: Getty Images)

A spokesperson for easyJet told the Mirror that any customers who have booked with alternative carriers have been advised they will be reimbursed. Accommodation and meals have also been arranged by the airline, while customers who made their own arrangements will be reimbursed.

Ms Dochartaigh's post from yesterday continued: "There are teachers here who can't get home for start of term and business owners who are facing significant disruptions. Our children's grandmother sadly passed away this morning and we will all miss her funeral if we can't get home sooner.

‌



"The next available flight from Tunisia to Belfast is 1st Sept meaning we'll be stranded for 8 days which is unheard of for a major airline! Our son will also miss his first day of 1st year at secondary school!"

The airline explained today that an additional flight has been scheduled for tonight, with Ms Dochartaigh and her family understood to be booked on this service. The flight is scheduled for 9.40pm local time (9.40pm BST), landing at Belfast at 1.25am.

The last easyJet flight from Enfidha to Belfast was on August 18 and operated as normal, according to data from air traffic monitoring app Flight Radar. Stuart McCartney and his family were also among the passengers due to fly home on flight EZY3072.

‌



On social media yesterday morning, he said: "So what has been a great family holiday has turned into a complete nightmare. What should be a fully energised Monday morning starting back at work for both Natalie, mum and I has instead fast become an energy zapping nightmare.

"We are stranded in Tunisia thanks to easyJet. EasyJet cancelled our flight as we stood queued to board the plane on Saturday evening and our current only way home option being offered by easyJet is on the 1st September (yes, next Tuesday).

"Communication from easyJet has been horrendous, they have basically said we can get you home next Tuesday or you can seek alternatives yourselves home with conflicting reports on what they will reimburse. Currently, as I write this, Natalie has found a flight with TunisAir out of Tunis to Nice, lay over for 4 hours in Nice then to Belfast on Thursday for £4k.

‌



"Our clothes etc. have already gone through a week in 40-degree heat here in Tunisia. For those on medication they don't have enough to get to next Tuesday. At the end of my tether to say the least."

View 3 Images Tunisia is a popular destination for British tourists (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

The McCartney family are also understood to be among those travelling. A spokesperson for easyJet told the Mirror: "We are sorry that flight EZY3072 from Enfidha to Belfast on 22 August experienced a technical issue and was unable to operate.

Article continues below

"We have been doing everything we can to support our customers, providing hotel accommodation and meals and we will be reimbursing expenses that may have been incurred. As alternative flight options including with other carriers are very limited at this busy time of year, we will be operating an additional direct flight from Enfidha to Belfast this evening and providing onward transfers home where needed.

"We are contacting customers directly with information on booking this flight and a dedicated number 03305515147 is also available for customers in Enfidha who require assistance. easyJet holidays customers are also being contacted directly.

"The welfare of our customers is our highest priority and we are very sorry for the inconvenience caused."

News.title: Angela Rayner urged to U-turn on rent controls decision after study shows benefits
News.content:
Angela Rayner urged to U-turn on rent controls decision after study shows benefits

EXCLUSIVE: Dozens of MPs have written to Angela Rayner warning the Government that it has an 'opportunity to fix the foundations of our housing system for the long term'

View 2 Images Housing Secretary Angela Rayner last month said the Government was not planning to bring in controls despite previous speculation (Image: Toby Shepheard/PA Wire)

Dozens of MPs have written to Angela Rayner urging her to U-turn on her decision not to bring in rent controls in England.

‌



The Housing Secretary last month said the Government was not planning to bring in controls despite previous speculation.

‌



But new research showing tenants could save up to £1,418 a year if rent controls are introduced has reignited calls.

‌



The study, commissioned by the Joseph Rowntree Foundation (JRF) and carried out by the Autonomy Institute, tests three rent-control pathways introduced from 2027/28: a cap linked to inflation (CPI), a nominal freeze and a moderate approach that limits in-tenancy rises to inflation (CPI) and between-tenancy rises to inflation (CPI) plus 2%.

By 2031, per tenancy, tenants would be annually saving £1,418 if rents were frozen, £701 if moderate rent controls were brought in or £130 if CPI inflation-tracked rent controls were introduced, researchers said. The rent-control pathways are modelled alongside two other reforms: restoring full mortgage-interest deductions for landlords and applying National Insurance to landlord property income.

View 2 Images By 2031, per tenancy, tenants would be annually saving £1,418 if rents were frozen, the study shows (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The letter to Ms Rayner, organised by Labour MP Chris Hinchliff and signed by 26 MPs so far, backs the study and warns the Government it has an "opportunity to fix the foundations of our housing system for the long term".

It says: "On average rent now takes 36% of a renter’s salary, rising to almost half of their pay in some areas just to keep a roof over their heads. With so much of people’s income going on housing, it is little wonder that a third of renters are living in poverty.

"The impacts don’t stop at the front door either, when rent take up such a large chunk of a pay packet you aren’t able to spend in local cafés, restaurants or shops.

‌



"These extortionate rents are the elephant in the room when we talk about the cost of living. The Prime Minister is right to support a mass council housebuilding programme to lay the long-term foundations of a housing system based on meeting need. However, renters are feeling the pain of high rent today and rent controls are essential to easing that pressure."

It is signed by mostly Labour MPs plus a few Green MPs, as well as Your Party MP Jeremy Corbyn.

In 2023, Mr Burnham - who was then the Greater Manchester mayor - called for freezes to private sector rents during the cost of living crisis.

‌



But Ms Rayner told the BBC last month: "I don't think that rent freezes, rent controls, is a way forward at the moment. Three years ago, Andy called for that because there was a significant crisis in the rental market. We implemented between then the Renters' Rights Act which is giving renters more power and control."

She added that controls had not "necessarily brought rents down" where they had been imposed in other places in the UK, such as Scotland. Other critics warn rent controls could increase the housing crisis by putting off people from renting out their house.

Nearly a fifth of UK households now rent privately, and high rents have strained living standards for two decades.

‌



The new report, Rebalancing the market: Designing feasible rent controls, models the private rental sector from 2027 to 2031 using data from the 2024 English Private Landlord Survey and the latest Office for Budget Responsibility forecasts.

Dr Will Stronge, chief executive at the Autonomy Institute said: "Rent controls have often been dismissed as unworkable, but our modelling shows that a modern, well-calibrated cap paired with fair treatment of landlord costs can improve affordability for tenants without triggering the kind of landlord exodus that would leave renters worse off.

"Desperately-needed regulation of rents doesn’t pose a risk to the sector if it comes along with tax reform for landlords”

Article continues below

An MHCLG spokesman said: “We have no plans to introduce rent controls. International examples show they don’t necessarily bring rents down and our landmark Renters’ Rights Act already protects tenants from excessive rent increases. The Act limits rent rises to once a year, gives tenants strong powers to challenge above-market increases and bans rental bidding wars - giving renters the security they deserve.”

News.title: Former nurse extradited to UK denies having sex with mental health patient at London hospital
News.content:
Former nurse extradited to UK denies having sex with mental health patient at London hospital

Former nurse Jason Forde appeared at Wood Green Crown Court after being extradited from Barbados over allegations involving a mental health patient at Homerton Hospital in Hackney.

View 2 Images The allegations relate to a woman who was being treated at a mental health unit on the site of Homerton Hospital in Hackney. (Image: Humphrey Nemar)

A former nurse extradited to the UK has denied having unlawful sexual activity with a woman who was receiving treatment for a mental disorder at a London hospital.

Jason Forde, 56, pleaded not guilty to eight counts at Wood Green Crown Court on Tuesday afternoon over alleged offences dating back to the 2000s.

The allegations relate to a woman who was being treated at a mental health unit on the site of Homerton Hospital in Hackney, east London.

Appearing in court via video link, Forde denied having sexual intercourse with the woman at the unit, which was part of the East London and City Mental Health Trust - and now operates under the East London NHS Foundation Trust.

View 2 Images Forde pleaded not guilty to the charges at Wood Green Crown Court (Image: MyLondon)

He also denied charges alleging that he engaged the woman in other sexual activity while she was in his care in the east London borough.

Prosecutor Paul Fairley told the court it had taken "many, many years to achieve" Forde's extradition from Barbados, with the 56-year-old landing at Heathrow Airport earlier this summer.

Forde denied one count of "having sexual intercourse with a woman who was a mental defective" contrary to section 7(1) of the Sexual Offences Act 1956, and one count of "having unlawful sexual intercourse with a patient," contrary to section 128(1) of the Mental Health Act 1959.

Article continues below

He also denied three counts of "sexual activity with a person with a mental disorder impeding choice" contrary to section 30(1) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and three counts of being a care worker engaged in "sexual activity with a person with a mental disorder" contrary to section 38(1) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

Forde was remanded into custody.

News.title: Should Brits get their licences taken away for dangerous driving videos? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should Brits get their licences taken away for dangerous driving videos? Take our poll and have your say

As a ghoulish social media trend sees young motorists risk everything on the road for likes, but should those who upload dangerous driving videos face serious penalties?

View 2 Images Liberty Mitchell, 21, filmed herself speeding and swerving in a Mini Cooper for Snapcha (Image: Gloucestershire Police / SWNS)

Campaigners are calling for those who upload dangerous driving videos to be stripped of their licences, to prevent further bloodshed.

‌



While those who are found guilty of a drink-driving offence automatically lose their licence, no such legislation is in place to tackle an alarming online trend. As seen by the Mirror, young people are turning to social media platforms such as TikTok to share content of themselves, risking their lives on the road in the name of likes.

‌



Some of these clips show youngsters going 'ghost mode', speeding along narrow, winding country lanes with their lights off. Others partake in wrong way motorway driving stunts. This is a deadly trend that cannot be normalised and, as seen in recent weeks, the effects of reckless driving, whether filmed or not, can be catastrophic.

‌



In the early hours of Saturday, August 22, two police officers, PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, died following a nightmare collision near Middlesbrough, Teesside.

A Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way on the A66 dual carriageway collided head-on with the police vehicle that had been assisting in a search for the car. All five occupants of the Passat - Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jakub Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18 - died instantly.

‌



It quickly emerged that a TikTok profile believed to belong to Saddington frequently featured footage which glorified dangerous driving. One video, deleted shortly after the crash along with the account, appeared to show Saddington in a high-speed police chase alongside four other youngsters.

View 2 Images PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38, were both killed in the horror wrong-way smash (Image: Getty Images)

This tragedy came mere days after another wrong-way motorway crash in County Kildare, Ireland. Five teenagers - Jeremy O'Brien, 18, Alex McCarthy, 17, Joey Carthy, 15, Jack Kennedy, 17, and Kamil Pustkowski, 17 - died when their BMW, travelling the wrong way down the M9 motorway at more than 74mph, crashed head-on into a Hyundai.

‌



The Hyundai had been carrying three sisters, Ella, Niamh, and Alma Kinsella, in their 20s and 30s, and a seven-year-old boy, all of whom were driving to Dublin Airport for a family wedding. The five teenagers were killed at the scene, while the three sisters sustained severe injuries. The young boy suffered a broken leg.

It's an issue that has sparked concern for some time. In December 2022, newly qualified driver Liberty Mitchell recorded Snapchat videos of herself speeding at almost 100mph in a 60mph zone.

Overtaking three vehicles on the wrong side of the road near Aldsworth, Gloucestershire, the then-18-year-old lost control of her Mini Cooper and caused a multi-car pile-up, killing taxi driver Octavian Codreanu and his passenger, teacher Moyra Whelan.

Article continues below

This week, the Government has demanded that social media companies remove any content which shows people driving dangerously. Speaking with reporters during a visit to Kyiv on Monday (August 24), Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated: “Anybody who glorifies dangerous driving is doing something that’s truly reprehensible.”

Do you have a story to share? Email me at julia.banim@reachplc.com

News.title: Young man stabbed to death in broad daylight at Wembley council HQ as manhunt launched
News.content:
Young man stabbed to death in broad daylight at Wembley council HQ as manhunt launched

Emergency crews including the air ambulance rushed to Engineers Way in Wembley after a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre.

View 4 Images A young man was stabbed to death at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley. (Image: Alamy Live News.)

A murder investigation has been launched after a young man was stabbed to death at a council headquarters in Wembley.

‌



The incident happened in Brent Civic Centre on Engineers Way at around 2.30pm on Tuesday following reports of a stabbing.

‌



Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service and found the victim suffering from stab wounds.

‌



The victim is believed to be a teenage boy or a man in his early 20s, although police are still working to formally identify him and inform his next of kin.

View 4 Images A young man was stabbed to death at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley. (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

Despite the efforts of paramedics, he was pronounced dead at the scene. No arrests have been made and officers are carrying out urgent enquiries to identify and trace those responsible.

‌



Police have also authorised additional stop and search powers across a number of areas in Brent following the incident. A Section 60 order applies to Wembley Park, Barnhill, Tokyngton, Stonebridge, Roundwood, Dollis Hill, Willesden and Welsh Harp.

The order allows officers to stop and search people and vehicles without the usual requirement for reasonable suspicion.

Superintendent Chris Clarke, who leads emergency response policing in the area, said: “This is an awful incident, in which someone has tragically lost their life. We are working to urgently identify the victim and inform his next-of-kin as soon as possible.

‌



View 4 Images A young man was stabbed to death at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley. (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

“An investigation is underway to establish exactly what has taken place and trace those responsible. We recognise the concern this incident will cause within the local community and are committed to keeping residents informed as our enquiries progress.

“In light of the incident, we have authorised additional stop and search powers to help prevent further violence, support our investigation, and keep people safe.

‌



“There will be an increased police presence in and around the area in the coming hours while our officers continue their investigation.”

Police said there is not believed to be a wider threat to the community and the incident is not believed to be terror-related.

View 4 Images A young man was stabbed to death at Brent Civic Centre in Wembley. (Image: James Manning/PA Wire)

‌



London Ambulance Service earlier said it was called at 2.25pm to reports of a stabbing at Brent Civic Centre.

An ambulance crew, paramedics in fast response cars and an incident response officer were sent to the scene, while London’s Air Ambulance was also dispatched.

A spokesperson said: “Sadly, despite the best efforts of our crews, a patient was pronounced dead at the scene.”

Article continues below

Anyone with information has been urged to call police on 101 quoting reference 4032/25AUG.

News.title: Dolly Parton: The life of an iconic country singer
News.content:
Iconic country musician Dolly Parton has died at the age of 80, her family announced on her social media.

"Sadness lies with us, not with Dolly," Parton's nephew Brian Seaver said in a video announcement.

In a seven-decade career, Parton won 10 Grammy awards, sold more than 100 million records worldwide, and wrote in excess of 3,000 songs.

Parton took her writing seriously, and considered herself a songwriter over everything else. "It's my way of expressing myself," she said. "It's my therapy."

She was also a savvy businesswoman who wasn't afraid to make tough decisions. Armed with a quick wit and southern charm, she took control of her show business career that spanned more than 60 years.

Follow for live updates and read more about Dolly's life.

News.title: Father's house rammed before son died in A66 crash
News.content:
A house rammed by a car before the fatal A66 crash in Middlesbrough belonged to the father of a teenager who died in the incident.

Cole Worthy, 17, was one of five young men who died when a Volkswagen Passat travelling in the wrong direction hit a Cleveland Police armed response vehicle, also killing two police officers.

Before the crash at 03:39 BST on Saturday, police had received multiple reports of two cars driving dangerously around the town and a Volvo XC60 was seen ramming properties.

The BBC understands that, after his father's home was rammed, Worthy and the four others set out in the Passat. Police said they were linking the activities of the Volvo XC60 and the Passat.

There is no suggestion Worthy's father was involved in criminal activity.

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and Worthy.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct said officers had been pursuing the Passat for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when it turned on to the dual carriageway.

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology.

News.title: Trump says all mines cleared from Strait of Hormuz
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has said that the US Navy has removed or detonated all mines in the Strait of Hormuz - the vital waterway which Iran has largely closed since the beginning of the war in the Middle East.

"Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

There is no comment from Iran.

Closure of the strait has caused wild fluctuations in the price of oil on world markets. Trump has often said the US has control of the area - but Iran has fired against vessels it says have sought to cross without its permission.

Some 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas used to transit the Strait of Hormuz before the war, which began on 28 February with US and Israeli air strikes against Iran.

In addition to closing the strait, Iran retaliated against Israel and against US bases in the region as well as US Arab allies in the Gulf.

A ceasefire aimed at facilitating talks to end the war has collapsed and there has been intermittent exchange of fire between the US and Iran.

However, this week the US announced a raft of economic sanctions against Iran.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that any nation financially partnering with Iran would be isolated.

Iran and the US signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in June - a 14-point document which set a 60-day deadline to reach a deal on the Strait of Hormuz, before substantial negotiations on resolving the nuclear issue - allegations that Iran is building a nuclear weapon, which Tehran has consistently denied.

However, that deadline has now expired and talks have collapsed leading to the new US sanctions that Trump believes will lead to the collapse of the Iranian regime.

Iran has been under sanctions for most of the time since the founding of the Islamic Republic in 1979 and Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh said Tehran was "fully prepared" for the wider sanctions, which he added would lead to "another defeat" for the US.

Its economy, however, has suffered as a result of the war - and a blockade of Iranian ports that the US has been maintaining for weeks not to allow trade to continue.

On Tuesday, China - the biggest buyer of Iranian oil - said it was firmly opposed to what it called the US's "illegal unilateral sanctions" and would take "all necessary measures" to safeguard its rights.

The US announcement comes ahead of planned talks between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping next month.

Washington is likely to be wary of potential retaliation from Beijing, which processes the majority of the world's rare earths and other critical minerals, crucial in the manufacture of many high-tech products.

Beijing has already tightened export controls on rare earths as part of previous trade negotiations with the US.

News.title: Who does Iran trade with and what could Trump's 'economic D-Day' mean?
News.content:
The US has said "the single greatest financial offensive ever" will help it and Israel end their ongoing war with Iran.

However, Iran is no stranger to these tactics.

The regime has faced near continuous US sanctions since the Islamic Revolution of 1979. In that time, it has developed deep trade ties with several countries which either have a history of ignoring US economic pressure themselves or cannot afford to stop trading with Iran.

As a result, Iran says it is "fully prepared" for the new US sanctions and many economists argue the impact of Washington's latest move will be limited.

So, who does Iran trade with? And could what the US has called an "economic D-Day" have any real impact on Iran?

News.title: Man dies in crash after police pursuit
News.content:
A man has died and two women have been injured in a crash after a police pursuit near Stratford-upon-Avon.

Officers tried to stop a black Audi on Birmingham Road shortly before 17:30 BST on Monday but the driver failed to pull over, Warwickshire Police said.

A pursuit began and 15 minutes later the Audi crashed into a white Ford Puma, the force added, with the Audi's 19-year-old male driver confirmed dead at the scene by paramedics.

The driver of the Ford, a woman, was seriously injured and remains in hospital in critical condition, while injuries to a second woman - her passenger - were serious but not believed to be life-threatening. An investigation by the police watchdog is under way.

Officers said after failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439 Warwick Road where the crash occurred.

A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.

Warwick Road was closed on Monday from the Marraway roundabout to its junction with Ingon Lane and Sand Barn Lane, with the stretch remaining shut on Tuesday morning.

It later reopened.

News.title: Yellow weather warnings issued as thunderstorms and flooding forecast
News.content:
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.

The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.

It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.

While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.

News.title: Spanish government says sorry to people of Ceuta for migrant crisis
News.content:
The Spanish government has apologised to the people of Ceuta for the migrant crisis that has affected the city for weeks and it has unveiled plans to overhaul the country's immigration laws.

"I want to apologise to all those who may have felt, or who even still feel, abandoned or not sufficiently cared for," Defence Minister Margarita Robles told a parliamentary committee.

"I have witnessed first-hand your feelings of anxiety, of abandonment, of lack of safety."

At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, a Spanish exclave in North Africa on 30 and 31 July.

Most of the migrants swam around the border fence and at least 100 people died during the mass crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor, Juan JesÃºs Vivas.

The vast majority of the migrants returned to Morocco within hours of their arrival, but several thousand remain in Ceuta, many of them children, and most sleeping rough on beaches or streets.

The Socialist government of Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez has been under mounting pressure to resolve the situation, with many residents and the local authorities in Ceuta, which has a population of 84,000, complaining that it is unsustainable.

The SÃ¡nchez government has now declared a situation of interest for national security in the city, centralising management of the crisis. Territorial Policy Minister Ãngel VÃ­ctor Torres has been tasked with co-ordinating the response, relieving the Ceuta local government of that responsibility.

News.title: Inspectors to assess police after Henry Nowak murder
News.content:
An inspection into how a police force responds to violent incidents has been launched in the wake of Henry Nowak's murder.

The 18-year-old student was stabbed in Southampton by Vickrum Digwa, who lied to police and insisted he had been the victim of a racist attack.

Hampshire Police officers initially arrested Nowak and placed him in handcuffs as he lay dying.

His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Service (HMICFRS) will assess the force's processes, training and how officers are supported to make sound and impartial judgements.

The inspection was requested by Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones, who said the public "must have confidence" in the force.

"This inspection will provide an independent assessment of the force's training, processes and culture, including the handling of allegations of racially aggravated assault," she said.

"Henry's family deserve answers, and the public deserve reassurance that their police service is equipped to recognise victims and provide the highest standard of care when it matters most."

News.title: Young care leavers dying early a 'national tragedy'
News.content:
Young adults who have left care have a death rate around four times higher than the general population, a new review, external shows.

Often left alone "with no safety net," the report says the consequences can be catastrophic.

On turning 18, people leaving care in England often lose "significant levers of support", the Government-commissioned report concluded, as it warned the so-called "care cliff" must be addressed.

Speaking to BBC Radio 4 Today, report co-author and broadcaster Ashley John-Baptiste, who grew up in care, called the deaths a national tragedy.

There were 112 deaths of care leavers aged 18 to 24 notified in 2025, which the review said equalled about 130 deaths per 100,000 care leavers.

John-Baptiste recalled his own experience of turning 18 and moving out of the last of four foster homes he'd lived in.

"I was made to live alone and work out how to be an adult," he said.

Unable to afford a bed frame, he says he slept on a mattress on the floor of his council flat and felt a deep sense of abandonment and isolation.

News.title: Boy, 3, injured in crocodile attack returns home
News.content:
A three-year-old boy who was seriously injured in a crocodile enclosure has been discharged from hospital and is settling back in at home, his family has said.

The child returned home "a few weeks ago" and is "happy to be home, playing with his toys, sleeping in his own bed and being a big brother", his parents said in an update posted online.

The boy was visiting Johnsons of Old Hurst near Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire, with his family on 18 June when he was attacked by at least one of the animals.

In an update shared on a fundraising page on Monday, the boy's family said it was "nice to have us all back together in the comfort of our own home".

Cambridgeshire Police arrested and bailed a 30-year-old man from Norfolk on suspicion of attempted murder after the incident.

News.title: Legendary rugby league winger Boston dies aged 92
News.content:
Tributes have been led by prime minister Andy Burnham who said he was a "giant of a man in every way".

"Heartbroken to hear my friend Sir Billy Boston has died," he said on social media.

"Billy was one of the greatest rugby league players of all time but also one of the kindest and most down-to-earth people you could ever wish to meet.

"He always had time for people and gave so much to back to his adopted home, Wigan.

"I will miss him greatly and am thinking today of Billy's family, still grieving the recent loss of his beloved wife Joan."

Wigan owner Mike Danson said: "Billy Boston was everybody's hero, including my mum's.

"His achievements in rugby league were extraordinary, and his knighthood was a fitting recognition of a career that brought great credit to Wigan and to the game.

"But Billy's legacy was not simply what he achieved. It was the humility with which he carried it. Despite everything he accomplished, he remained a quiet, dignified and deeply respected man.

"He leaves behind an example that will endure for generations. Our thoughts are with his family and those closest to him.

"A great man, and a true Wigan legend. He will be remembered with pride and affection."

In a statement, Wales Rugby League said: "Today, rugby league has lost one of its greatest-ever players, Wales has lost one of its finest sporting sons, and our sport has lost a truly special gentleman."

The WRU also paid tribute, calling Boston "one of the best loved and most iconic figures in the history of Welsh sport".

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy added: "He was, in my view, the greatest rugby league player of all time and one of the nicest people I've ever had the privilege to know."

News.title: Former police officer charged with raping woman while on duty
News.content:
A former police officer allegedly raped and strangled a woman while on duty, according to the policing watchdog.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said ex-constable Rikki Hall had been charged with two counts of rape and one count of non-fatal strangulation.

The 33-year-old is accused of attacking the woman while on duty in Swansea city centre in February 2024.

Hall, who resigned from South Wales Police during the IOPC investigation, has also been charged with possession of a firearm and two counts of misconduct in public office.

He will appear at Bristol Magistrates' Court on Thursday.

The IOPC said its investigation began in February 2024 following a mandatory conduct referral from South Wales Police.

"A substantial file of material was submitted to the Crown Prosecution Service in February 2025 and, following further lines of enquiry being undertaken, charges were authorised by the CPS," it added.

News.title: 'We just want to get home' - dozens stranded in Tunisia after cancelled Belfast flight
News.content:
Dozens of people from Northern Ireland have been left stranded in Tunisia after their EasyJet flight home was cancelled, with the airline telling them it had no other flights available for another 10 days.

One man told BBC News NI he has spent Â£4,000 on travel home for his family-of-five, while another woman, Georgina Doherty, said she and her six children were trying to get home after the death of her mother-in-law.

Others described running out of medication for health issues, while EasyJet were also criticised over a lack of support and communication.

EasyJet has said it is operating an additional direct flight to Belfast on Tuesday night, and that it was "very sorry" for the inconvenience.

BBC News NI understands more than 100 people were booked onto the cancelled flight that was due to leave Enfidha-Hamamet Airport for Belfast International three days ago.

Stuart McCartney, from Dromore, County Down, said he had spent thousands on accommodation and flights to get his family home via a flight to Brussels.

"I'm willing to pay Â£4,000 to get us home, if needs be, and then battle for reimbursement if I have to after that," he said.

"But we shouldn't have to pay. My holiday was a fraction of what I'm paying to get home right now."

McCartney said EasyJet provided two nights of accommodation but then told the family to find alternative accommodation for the rest of the delay.

He said his mother Katherine, who accompanied his wife and children on the trip, relies on heart medication and they have had to keep a close eye on her remaining supply as the delay continued.

An EasyJet spokesperson said that the company "have been doing everything we can to support Mr McCartney, providing hotel accommodation and meals and we will be reimbursing expenses that may have been incurred".

Georgina Doherty, who is originally from Londonderry but now lives in County Donegal, told BBC News NI the last few days have been an "absolute nightmare" for her family.

Her husband returned home a day before they were due to fly back due to his mother taking ill. She has since died, with Doherty and her six children stranded in Tunisia.

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
Ministers have announced where more than 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost Â£10bn in a bid to address the housing crisis.

Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool. An additional Â£6bn was previously announced for London.

It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes, under the government's Â£39bn social housebuilding programme.

Housing charities welcomed the news but said it was still not enough to meet demand, while the Conservatives said it was an "unfunded spending commitment".

Social housing provides affordable homes at a low cost, managed by social landlords. It includes affordable rented properties as well as low-cost home ownership, such as shared ownership, and can be provided by local authorities and housing associations.

Earlier this year, before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had called for the entire Â£39bn affordable housing budget for England to be spent on homes for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents, and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it.

"I would actually devote all of it to social housing," Burnham told The Social Housing Podcast in May.

But of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent.

Housing Minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast he did not accept Burnham had failed to meet his previous commitment, saying the government had taken a "pragmatic approach" and wants to "get money out the door".

He said the next tranche of funding would be more focused on council houses - which are usually also classed as homes for social rent.

It is understood ministers decided against giving councils more of the funding announced in the first tranche because they did not believe councils would be in a position to build the required number of social homes.

News.title: Andrew Tate exaggerates and did not own supercars in photos, his lawyers say
News.content:
Controversial influencer Andrew Tate portrays himself as "uberwealthy" but did not own cars and a yacht featured on his social media and exaggerated his lifestyle for online attention, his legal representatives have said.

Tate and his brother Tristan are currently being held in a Florida jail but are seeking release on bail while they await the outcome of extradition proceedings.

They were arrested last month after British prosecutors unveiled new charges including alleged sexual offences against them, which both men deny.

Prosecutors have argued the Tates are a "flight risk", citing the brothers' past statements about their wealth and influence and having multiple identities to evade the law.

In a legal submission to the court, the brothers' legal representatives said the Tates' business model "depends on online attention".

"The outrageousness of the posts by them and about them is the point. The more hyperbolic and outlandish the post, the more likely it will generate views and likes, which in turn generates income. In short, they are playing a role," it says.

At times Andrew Tate has also exaggerated and used hyperbole for "comedic effect" with no intention to be taken seriously, the submission argues.

"The government alleges that the Tates are a risk of flight based on their social media claims that they are 'self-proclaimed billionaires' who own 'high-end vehicles, private jets, and a custom $50-million-dollar superyacht and have unrestricted access to traditional funds, cryptocurrency, and bitcoin,'" it says.

"But the government has not established these grandiose claims are true," it adds.

News.title: Man jailed for killing student over fake Rolex row
News.content:
At about 17:00 GMT on the night he died, Oladipo left his girlfriend's flat carrying a plastic bag of leftover snacks and was on the phone to her while he walked back to his accommodation nearby to watch football.

But outside the De Montfort University's Innovation Centre, he was met by Dennis who was captured on CCTV walking up and down in the "busy" area.

"It took less than 30 seconds for the two men to come together, to struggle and for the defendant to leave," Osborne told the court.

The court was told Oladipo's girlfriend heard him say "why did you come up and stab me?" over the phone before asking for her to call the ambulance.

A post-mortem examination showed he had suffered six wounds, five to the chest including one which penetrated his heart, and one to his thumb.

Despite being taken to the Leicester Royal Infirmary, he was pronounced dead just over an hour after the stabbing, which took place near the DMU campus.

Giving evidence in his defence on Wednesday, Dennis said he was "fearful" for his life when Oladipo approached him with a knife, adding he was "wrestling" to prevent the 20-year-old from stabbing him.

In cross-examination, prosecutor Jane Osborne KC asked if Dennis knew he had stabbed Oladipo, to which he replied: "I didn't know and I didn't know he was hurt, and I didn't intend to cause any serious harm."

Jurors were shown CCTV footage of Oladipo and Dennis walking towards each other, with Osborne suggesting Dennis used his hands to open a folding knife.

Dennis denied the suggestion he had a knife in his possession, and said he did not leave his accommodation with one.

Addressing Dennis, the prosecutor said there was "bad feeling" between Dennis and Oladipo - and suggested Dennis left his accommodation with a knife "to settle it".
