Sports.title: Football Daily | Two goals, some polish and a rebrand: City flip Sávio for quite the profit
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN WINGERS UNDER THE HAMMER

We see Manchester City have managed to flip Savinho for quite the profit. Football Daily had previously assumed this sort of wheeler-dealing was restricted to the Dion-Dublin-adjacent property market, or the Harry-Redknapp-infused used car scene, but it seems we were mistaken. We have no idea how City ended up trousering a £44.2m markup on a player who cost £30.8m two seasons ago, and has achieved the square root of eff all since, but they’ve done it. Consider standing stock still and allowing a ball to clank off you and into the net in an FA Cup tie at Newcastle analogous to installing a new bathroom suite and giving the front room a lick of paint, or taking a microfibre cloth and some polish to the crevices of that grimy dashboard. Result! Goal! Ker-ching! That’s 75 million-nil!

Spurs were the mark, and they could end up paying £85m if all the silverware-related add-ons kick in. So £75m it is, then. But that’s still a fair old whack for an attacking player who scored two goals for City in 53 league appearances. The 22-year-old Brazilian plays on the right flank, so will almost certainly take the place of Mikey Moore, who thought his day at Brentford last weekend had gone badly enough, only for his manager Roberto De Zerbi to go out of his way to namecheck him – and him alone, twice – in his post-match deconstruction of a 3-0 fiasco for which pretty much everyone wearing Tottenham’s traditional blue, gold and dayglo pink was culpable.

Upon signing, Savinho announced that he wishes to be known forthwith as Sávio, reverting to the monicker from his time at Girona, where he scored 11 goals and set up 10 others during a loan stint that was a damn sight more successful than his spell at the Etihad. It’s also his actual name, so there is that. Sávio is far from the first of his countrymen to toy with this most personal of brands – Brazil’s greatest-ever player was actually called Manuel Francisco dos Santos, and Pelé was the result of a name change too – and we’re pretty sure he won’t be the last. Spurs meanwhile will simply be hoping they’re getting the Girona version of their new purchase, because otherwise City will have, in more ways than one, properly flipped them off. Omar Marmoush – 16 goals in 62 appearances, brand-new kitchen worktops, shiny hubcaps – next!

Enough is enough” – a group of influential current and former footballers, including Mikaël Silvestre, Lucy Bronze, Emmanual Petit and David James, have piled more pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa. However the Cameroon Football Federation’s head-honcho and one-time unimpressed interviewee, Samuel Eto’o, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership. “I don’t think that [he] has done anything wrong,” he honked. “I think the timing of all [the criticism] is because there’s an election coming out.”

Sports.title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.

Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere. Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.

Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.

Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.

West Ham’s clearout after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.

Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.

West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are planning to strengthen further.

Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out.

The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.

Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League academy sides will play in tier three of the pyramid from the 2027-28 season after the controversial proposal was approved by the Football Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

The FA said data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues.

Quick Guide How do I 

The FA said WNL clubs would receive central funding for the first time and that changes to the loan market would encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s football at the FA, said: “For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: ‘He’s box office’: Gary Lineker admits wanting Roy Keane to join The Rest Is Football
Sports.content:
With an all-conquering podcast empire and a new deal that will make his football punditry show a regular fixture on Netflix, there seems little left for Gary Lineker to wish for.

However, while the former Match of the Day presenter is full of praise for Alan Shearer and Micah Richards – the fellow pundits on his The Rest Is Football show – Lineker has admitted to admiring a combative figure playing for his main rivals.

Asked which of the plethora of football pundits he would want to poach, Lineker admitted that Roy Keane’s brutal delivery and viral rants meant the former Manchester United captain would be his dream signing.

“He’s box office,” Lineker said during an appearance at the Edinburgh TV festival, before joking that, analytically, the Irishman “doesn’t give you that much”.

“He’s bloody good at being Roy Keane,” he said. “I’ve met Roy a few times. He’s really sweet … he just plays a character and he’s good at it. He’s really good at it, and he obviously knows his [stuff]. I was kidding about the analytical thing, a little bit.”

Keane is a member of a podcast team that has emerged as Lineker’s main opposition – Gary Neville’s The Overlap operation, which includes the Stick to Football show. Soon after The Rest Is Football signed up with Netflix, Stick to Football announced a similar deal with Disney.

While the rivalry is good natured, a tongue-in-cheek Lineker couldn’t help but add a slice of football needle, saying Keane “probably would” 

“You’ve got Gary [Neville] and his team, you’ve got Piers Morgan and his team [making the World Cup Uncensored] show, and they’re just trying to copy,” Lineker joked. “They’re trailing in our wake and I wish them all the very best. There is room, particularly in football. There’s a lot of competition.”

The deals bringing football podcasts to the world’s biggest streaming services are a sign of a thirst for sport content. Given the huge expense of live sporting rights, punditry has become a popular option.

The Rest is Football appeared in Netflix’s daily top 10 charts on every day of its 40-day run of daily episodes filmed during the World Cup, and the US company has opted to continue their partnership during the domestic season.

The Rest is Football obtained more than 7m monthly streams for its content alone last season, leading Lineker to joke that Neville’s outfit was “languishing miles behind”.

Lineker was interviewed on stage about his transition from footballer to presenter to media mogul, as the co-founder of successful podcast stable, Goalhanger. During the appearance, he explained why he continued to speak out on political issues, particularly Gaza.

In the last week, the Telegraph criticised him for reposting a video of Tony Greenstein, an anti-Zionist who was cleared last week of inviting support for Hamas. In the video, the activist said: “Zionism is in the tradition of the Nazis who persecuted Jews.”

11:01 Gary Lineker calls for Burnham to introduce wealth tax - The Latest

Lineker said: “I don’t think I speak much about politics, although politics is involved in everything that I speak about.

“I think ultimately you need to live with yourself and if I see things that upset me in humanitarian terms, then I find it quite upsetting, and it triggers me to use a platform that I would never have had before … People can disagree and that’s absolutely fine.”

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round. Arsenal dominated every metric against a promoted Coventry team that looked, frankly, a little spooked by their first sight of that fresh Everest.

So, a tiny sample size. It may mean absolutely nothing. It could get flipped on its head before we hit September. Also, it is important to note that pure possession stats have rarely dictated with any certainty who will win a game. The top teams always tend to have most of the ball, thus skewing the overall stats.

Otherwise, possession has been a far less reliable guide to victory than, say, expected goals, which speaks clearly to the effectiveness of a system. Whereas simply keeping the ball is often a sign of the opposite of good health, of football as a collective anxiety attack, out there playing with your worry beads, tramping a horseshoe shape into the grass while your opponents mass for the decisive blitzkrieg.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

But it wasn’t just the possession numbers that were notable this weekend. The rhythms of the matches were striking. All three Sunday games featured nine or 10 substitutes in the last 40 minutes or so, and a sense of two separate halves, of finishers brought into play, of a broken, episodic tactical to‑and‑fro in response to shifts in the scoreline and the flow. The World Cup also had that pattern. Maybe this is what football is now.

Mainly there was a striking level of targeted physicality, rehearsed blitz-transitions, groups of players running suddenly forward quickly in formation at certain triggering events. Anthony Elanga’s opener for Newcastle captured this best: 12 seconds, two passes, 70 metres covered in a single perfectly straight line, no off‑the‑cuff inventions or what you might call conventional “creativity”, but a perfect moment of planned collective intelligence and breathtaking athleticism.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This was the pattern elsewhere too, games defined by rapid breaks, by powerful players sourced for their ability to win duels and to carry the ball, and a weekend that felt like another ratcheting up in the Premier League’s journey into hyper‑physicality.

Isn’t it a trend? Is this the next stage in the league’s narrow but furiously intense evolution? There are several managers in new jobs who have reputations for the game of sprints, blitz‑ball: most notably Matthias Jaissle at Newcastle and Roberto De Zerbi at what was, on Saturday, the least De Zerbi‑ish of Spurs, a Spurs that seemed to have absorbed only the mouse part – play dead, hide, roll over – of that fast‑breaking cat‑and‑mouse football.

There are two things worth saying about this. This is not a rejection of Guardiolaism and positional play. Keeping the ball was always about preparing for the moments when you don’t have it. Guardiola’s later Manchester City team would often win by direct means.

But pure possession can also be boringly risk-averse, a kind of footballing atrophy where everyone just sits quivering on the touchline like a swarm of beached jellyfish at dusk. The spectacle is more gripping when the emphasis is on those transitions either side of the passing patterns.

More specifically, it is also an interesting development for Pep’s successor at City, Enzo Maresca, Coolio to his Tupac, whose methods are still very much pure Pep origins, based in control of the ball and rigid positionism, like the last soldier still fighting the second world war from inside a bush on Iwo Jima in 1976.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s Anthony Elanga celebrates his superb strike against Liverpool. Photograph: Simon Davies/ProSports/Shutterstock

Is Maresca ready for this? Is he even ahead of it? He gave a televised interview at the weekend where he spoke about the tension between control and risk, possession and creativity, and where he defined players being encouraged to run into unexpected positions as “chaos”. On Monday morning there were headlines describing the Premier League weekend in those terms. But this isn’t chaos. We’ve seen chaos. We’ve seen attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion, jinking wingers, dogs of war, hitting the space, Lee Chapman, Rod Wallace and Eric Cantona making heavy metal music with two bass guitars and an antique viola. You want chaos. We can give you chaos.

What the Premier League brought at the weekend, the quick breaks, the freedom to attack at selected moments, was more a kind of hyper-managed shock and awe, targeted speed and physicality born out of calculated risk, numbers, data, heavy briefings.

It was also exciting to watch, which is no bad thing in the world’s most tightly contested, space‑averse league. No doubt there will be tightening, a reaction to the reaction, instant counter‑moves and contingency planning. August can also be odd and silly season-ish, the dog days of a World Cup summer. But it did at times feel as if we were in a post‑something moment. If not quite post‑Pep, whose influence will continue to loom, a tactical Machiavelli with plenty of tapes still left in the vault.

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.

“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 4: Brighton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 6th (NB: this is not necessarily Sophie Downey’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 7th

Prospects

A first FA Cup final was a historic moment for Brighton. Despite losing to Manchester City at Wembley, it will have filled Dario Vidosic and his team with the belief that they are on the right track.

It has been a summer of relative stability on the south coast. While there are seven new faces, departures have been limited to four. The arrivals of Lia Wälti and Gabby George bring vast experience and increased defensive acumen to the ranks while the Republic of Ireland’s Emily Murphy and Poland’s Nadia Krezyman are young attacking talents who have started to make a name for themselves.

Brighton’s inconsistency was their downfall last season. They were seriously hampered by the lack of an out-and-out centre-forward after the anterior cruciate ligament injury suffered by the Arsenal loanee and England Euros hero Michelle Agyemang. Kiko Seike finished as their highest scorer in the league with eight and she was their only representative in the Women’s Super League’s top 20 for goals and assists. That problem remains unsolved and will surely be a focus for the remainder of the transfer window.

The conclusion of their season certainly gave Brighton something to build on over the summer. They secured an impressive league victory over City and a draw against Arsenal and will hope to outdo the latter when they host Renée Slegers’s side at Crawley in their opener on 6 September. That on paper is the toughest of Brighton’s opening four fixtures.

Off-field picture

Pinterest has become the first solo sponsor of the women’s team with a four-year partnership. The deal pivots around the concept of ‘matchday style’, bringing to life the way fans show support for their team. Plans continue for the construction of Europe’s first purpose-built women’s football stadium. Located next to the Amex Stadium, the hope is it will open for the start of the 2030-2031 campaign.

The manager

Now entering his third season, Vidosic is the second-longest serving manager in the WSL, a period that has brought much-needed stability to the club and allowed the Croatian-born Australian time to fully implement his aggressive pressing and possession-based style. He has been on a journey, developing an out-of-possession style to help his team deal with some of the bigger clubs in the WSL The 39-year-old has never hidden from his desire to bring silverware to Brighton and last season’s FA Cup final will have given him a taste of the steps required to realise that ambition.

Star signing

The acquisition of Wälti remains one of the biggest coups of the summer. The 33-year-old Switzerland captain returns to England after a year in Italy with Juventus, bringing with her a wealth of experienceand, from her seven years with Arsenal, a WSL title and a Champions League winners’ medal. Wälti’s technical ability is second-to-none, as is a level of intelligence that allows her to dictate play from the middle of the park. She leads by example and guided Switzerland to the quarter-finals at Euro 2025. If Wälti can stay injury-free, she could play a significant role this season.

View image in fullscreen Lia Wälti should bring quality and know-how to Brighton. Photograph: Neil Holmes/Focus Images Ltd/Shutterstock

Stat attack

Brighton had a finishing problem in 2025-26. Not in terms of hitting the target – no other side had as strong a shot accuracy – but only three teams converted a lower proportion of their on-target efforts. If the Seagulls can fire towards the corners of the goal rather than close to the goalkeeper, they could fly this season.

Set for a breakthrough

Sophie Peskett has already made history when in 2021, aged 18, she became Ipswich’s first professional player. The winger spent the best part of seven years at Ipswich, making 127 appearances and helping them earn promotion to the WSL 2 twice. Now 23, it would have been a big decision for her to leave, but Brighton seems like a sensible next step. A nifty player with an eye for goal, Peskett will prove useful to Brighton’s attacking output.

What they say …

“Brighton is not a team that has to hide. In the last couple of years, they’ve been able to hurt the big teams in many moments, and they reached the FA Cup final last season as well. We’re not going to be favourites in every single game, but that’s a nice position to be in.” – Lia Wälti

Where are they playing their home games?

Brighton will continue to play most of their home games at Crawley’s Broadfield Stadium although four of their six opening home fixtures will be at the Amex. The club have added an Amex 4-Match Pack to their ticketing options, priced at £45 for adults. The club have also launched ‘Built For Her’, their dedicated women’s football membership option that offers a bundle of exclusive perks as they look to build their fanbase before the stadium move.

Sports.title: National League star says he’s ‘ready for the next challenge’ after club rejects record offer
Sports.content:
National League star says he’s ‘ready for the next challenge’ after club rejects record offer

Boreham Wood forward Abdul Abdulmalik believes he is 'capable of reaching the top' as he issued an impassioned plea to join Djurgarden.

The Swedish club recently had a £1.5million bid for the 23-year-old rejected by Boreham Wood.



2 Abdulmalik is ready to call Stockholm his new home Credit: Getty

Had the offer been accepted, it would have broken the record for an outgoing transfer from the National League.

The current record was set in 2012 when Leicester City forked out £1m to sign Jamie Vardy from Fleetwood Town.

Although Boreham Wood chairman Danny Hunter was hailed by Peterborough United owner Darragh MacAnthony for his 'cojones' in rejecting Djurgarden's advances thus far, Abdulmalik has now voiced his desire to make a life-changing move in a post on Instagram.



What did Abdul Abdulmalik say in his statement?

"Through sheer hard work and perseverance, the opportunity to progress has come around," Abdulmalik wrote.

"This is my chance to push myself as a footballer, elevate my game and most importantly fulfil my promise to the ones around me.



"Opportunities like this are rare, especially within the National League where some of the hardest working talent is overlooked. The game of football is forever changing and decisions are fast paced. There's no guarantee that the same chances come knocking twice.

"I owe it to myself and the kids growing up just like me to fight for this one I've been offered.



"Moving on from a club is one of the toughest decisions in a footballer's career. I'm more than grateful for everyone that has been a part of my journey so far.

"Everyone at Boreham Wood FC and the incredible fans have played a massive part. You will always have my respect.

"With this said, I'm ready for the next challenge. I'm ready to prove to myself and those around me that I'm capable of reaching the top."

2 The 23-year-old has made just shy of 100 appearances for Boreham Wood since he joined Credit: Getty



How did Abdul Abdulmalik perform for Boreham Wood last season?

Djurgarden's interest in Abdulmalik comes on the back of the 23-year-old registering 17 goals and ten assists last season for Boreham Wood.

His goal contributions could not fire the club into League Two as they were beaten in the National League play-off final by Rochdale on penalties.

He was not involved in Boreham Wood's National League clash against Forest Green last weekend, which saw Boreham Wood win 3-0.

He did play in their first two league matches, though, scoring once and getting two assists during showdowns against Tamworth and FC Halifax Town.



Following the match, Boreham Wood boss Luke Garrard effectively issued a hands-off warning to Djugarden by declaring Abdulmalik 'is our player'.

The 23-year-old joined the Hertfordshire outfit in 2024 as a free agent after being released by Millwall, where he rose through their academy ranks.

Abdulmalik also has three appearances for England's Under-17s, where he played alongside Jamal Musiala, Omari Hutchinson and Jarell Quansah.

Sports.title: Chelsea will not challenge Arsenal for the title due to glaring problem, it’s not just Robert Sanchez
Sports.content:
Chelsea will not challenge Arsenal for the title due to glaring problem, it’s not just Robert Sanchez

Chelsea have the capacity to beat Arsenal in a single game, but lack the stamina over 38 matches to challenge for the title.

This is the view of the talkSPORT Breakfast panel with Chelsea told it's not just their goalkeeping problem holding them back from a first league title in a decade.



3 The defensive trio made their first appearance together in a 3-2 win at Craven Cottage Credit: Getty

Morgan Rogers scored on his competitive debut against Fulham at Craven Cottage as Xabi Alonso's side secured a hard-fought 3-2 victory.

The Blues opened up the scoring after just 31 seconds after Joao Pedro slotted home the club's first goal of the new campaign.

The attacking trio of Cole Palmer, Rogers, and Pedro provided a devastating frontline display for the home fans.



However, Chelsea's defensive frailties raised immediate concerns—particularly regarding goalkeeper Robert Sanchez, whose error directly contributed to Fulham's first goal, scored by Josh King.

Following the match, Alonso said his front three needed to 'lead the rest' so that the 'other ones will follow'.



However, Jeff Stelling told talkSPORT Breakfast that the blame can not only be placed on the man between the sticks.

He said: "It's not just Robert Sanchez. They look lovely going forward. But as I mentioned a moment or two ago, Fulham really should have got something out of that game.



"Antonee Robinson is through one-on-one with Sanchez. Lobs the ball, I was going to say wide, but it's so far wide. They had chances and that was the problem.

"Chelsea gave Fulham, who I thought were quite encouraging, a few chances. They couldn't cope with Josh King.

"I just think that defensively... if Moises Caicedo is back, he'll give them more of a shield, that is for sure. I don't know much about Marco Palestra. I haven't seen him play, so I can't really comment on that one. But I think defensively, they're too vulnerable."

3 Sanchez conceded two and looked nervy throughout the match on Monday Credit: Getty



Clean sheet drought

Maxence Lacroix produced a respectable performance on his competitive debut for the Blues, while Josh Acheampong made several crucial last-ditch interceptions.

However, Levi Colwill seemed out of control on multiple occasions and was lucky Lacroix was covering behind him, suggesting the previous seasons defensive problems still remain as the Blues failed to keep a clean sheet for a 17th consecutive match.

Ally McCoist added: "I think they could beat Arsenal on a one-off. I'm not sure they have the consistency to take them over the 38 games. I think they've got real quality in forward areas. It was a beautiful finish.

"Cole Palmer when he's like that, he's irresistible to watch. He really is. He's just wonderful to watch. They've got brilliant, brilliant players. But I just don't think that consistency wise, you're going to have to maintain a level of consistency over seven, eight months.



"I'm not sure Chelsea will do that. But I think they could beat Arsenal on a one-off, definitely."

Arsenal is THE defensive benchmark

Arsenal enter the campaign defending their crown with an upgraded squad — particularly in defensive areas following the addition of Ezri Konsa.

3 The England international will be most likely a benchwarmer for Arsenal when they have a fully fit squad Credit: Getty

To win the Premier League title, Mikel Arteta made his side the strongest defensively during the previous campaign



They only conceded 27 goals last term, in comparison to Chelsea' who shipped 52.

Additionally, the Gunners' David Raya finished the season with 19 clean sheets in only 37 appearances, and was awarded the Golden Glove award.

Meanwhile, Robert Sanchez managed just nine in 35 outings for the Blues during last term.

Sports.title: David Moyes snaps back at reporter over ‘dead stupid’ question
Sports.content:
David Moyes snapped back at a reporter's question regarding his desire to win cup competitions with Everton this season.

Moyes was visibly annoyed after being asked how important success in the Carabao Cup and FA Cup is for the Toffees.



2 Moyes was annoyed by a question he was asked during his press conference Credit: AFP

Everton start their Carabao Cup campaign on Wednesday night when they take on Preston in the second round.

Ahead of that game at Deepdale, Moyes spoke to the media in his press conference to preview the midweek action.

But one question in particular launched him into a quick rant against journalists that he labelled 'dead stupid'.



Moyes snaps back at journalist

Moyes was asked: "How important are the cups to you this season?"

And that seemed to hit a particular nerve for the Everton boss, who then hit back at the reporter.

"I think it's a question that every journalist asks every manager," he began in reply.



"In some ways, I think are those journalists dead stupid? Do you think none of the managers want to win the cups?

"Of course we all want to win the cups... so the answer is yes, the cups are hugely important."



"Would it be more important to win a cup than to stay in the Premier League?" he then asked back to the journalist.

The journalist quickly replied no, with Moyes hinting that he values survival in the top flight over success in the cup by adding: "So, there we go. You've half answered it."

2 Everton have not won a trophy since 1995, so success in the cups would be huge Credit: Getty

When did Everton last win a trophy?

Moyes may be right that a lot of managers are asked the same question about the importance of cup success.



But for Everton, the Carabao Cup and FA Cup have some extra significance considering their trophy drought.

The Toffees have not won a major trophy since 1995, which was a success in the FA Cup.

Fans are sure to want to end their 31-year wait for glory, so they will expect big things from their side each year.

Last season, a loss to Wolves in the Carabao Cup second round ended their journey early, with Moyes now under pressure to go further.



However, if he values league football above the cup, could Everton be in for another year of no silverware?

Sports.title: Paul Scholes tells Bruno Fernandes to ‘keep mouth shut’ as two other Manchester United stars called out
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes tells Bruno Fernandes to ‘keep mouth shut’ as two other Manchester United stars called out

Manchester United icon Paul Scholes was not in the mood to hear Bruno Fernandes' frustrations over the shock loss to Hull City.

The Red Devils slipped to a 2-0 defeat against the Tigers last weekend, marking the first time they'd been beaten by a newly-promoted side to start the campaign.



3 Prior to Saturday, United had not lost to Hull City since 1974 Credit: Getty

Worryingly, United boasted 72 per cent possession and fired off 20 shots but could not find a way past a stubborn Hull defence.

In the aftermath of the result, United captain Fernandes bemoaned the team made the 'same mistakes as we did last season', something Hull's players were well placed to take advantage of.

"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set plays and not concede these types of goals," Fernandes added.



"Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment."

What did Paul Scholes say in response to Bruno Fernandes' comments?

But Scholes, speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football, felt Fernandes was better served by staying silent, at least publicly.

"I'd be interested to know what (Fernandes) means by that," Scholes said.



"What mistakes were they giving set-piece goals away?

"Especially when you perform the way he did as well, I think it's probably best to keep your mouth shut, because he didn't have his best performance either, and there was quite a few of them like that."

Co-host Paddy McGuinness added Luke Shaw even admitted United could have prepared better, prompting a cutting response from Scholes.



Paul Scholes shreds Luke Shaw over preparation comment

"Luke Shaw always says something," Scholes said.

3 Shaw may have been given a talking-to by Carrick over his comments Credit: Getty

"That's a slight on your staff, that's a slight on your manager.

"If one of your players was saying that, f****** hell, you'd have him in Monday morning wouldn't you, 'What do you mean by that?'"

Shaw and Fernandes weren't the only United players in Scholes' crosshairs, with Harry Maguire also coming in for criticism.

Harry Maguire's bizarre marking called out by Paul Scholes

Scholes was especially bemused by Maguire's role during Hull's opener, as the United defender appeared to hold back teammate Noussair Mazraoui.



Had either Maguire or Mazraoui been free, they could have made a play to prevent Semi Ajayi's goal.

"I think he's (Maguire) just lost his bearings or something, I don't know," Scholes said.

3 Maguire won't want to look back at his marking on this set piece again Credit: Getty

"I don't think he's looking at the players, he's looking at the ball, isn't he?



"The only thing I can think is that he's lost his bearings and he's looking at the ball and he could feel somebody in front of him, and he's just gone like that."

United will now look to shake off the humiliating loss to Hull when they return to action on Sunday against Ipswich Town.

Sports.title: Brandon Williams leaves EFL club after two-month trial as ex-Man United starlet not offered deal
Sports.content:
Brandon Williams has reportedly left Rotherham United following a trial, having not been offered a contract at the club.

The former Manchester United starlet had been training with the League Two side since June, but he won't be signing for them.

2 Williams, who most recently played for Hull, will not be signing for Rotherham Credit: Anna Gowthorpe

According to the Rotherham Advisor, Williams has not received an offer to join the Millers on a permanent basis.

He is understood to now be training elsewhere after being part of their sessions up until late last week.

The 25-year-old featured in seven friendlies during his trial at the club and remained part of their camp as the League Two campaign started two weeks ago.

But Rotherham are said to be looking at different recruitment priorities ahead of the transfer deadline on Monday.

What next for Brandon Williams?

Williams is hoping to revive his football career after he was handed a suspended 14-month prison sentence for dangerous driving last year.

He has since spoken openly about his regret over his actions and revealed multiple off-pitch issues he has struggled with.

His last professional football match was on August 23 in 2025, as he played five minutes for Hull City against Blackburn.

They were his only minutes for the Tigers during a very short stint, and since that spell, he has been a free agent.

It appeared that Williams could be closing in on a return to the game with Rotherham as he began a trial.

However, he has not got the move and he will now hope that offers could come from elsewhere this summer.

2 Williams played just five minutes in his brief spell with Hull Credit: Getty

Honest conversation

Williams is unlikely to have been too shocked by Rotherham's decision not to offer him a permanent contract.

Manager Alex Bruce, son of Steve Bruce, had already revealed earlier this month that he told the left-back to explore other options.

"I've had a conversation with Brandon," Bruce said. "If there's anything out there for him in terms of someone being desperate for him, then of course he's got to go and explore it.

"At the minute, he's happy training here, he's happy being around the place.

"But we are in a situation where other areas of the field might need addressing first before we look at that one.

"We just have to play it by ear for the time being."

And now, it seems as if Rotherham have decided to address those other areas and not sign the ex-Man United man after his trial.

Sports.title: Is Match of the Day in trouble? Simon Jordan tells flagship show to learn from Football Focus’ demise
Sports.content:
Is Match of the Day in trouble? Simon Jordan tells flagship show to learn from Football Focus’ demise

Match of the Day is under threat and needs to raise its game - but it remains just as valuable despite the numbers not being the same.

That is the verdict of talkSPORT's Simon Jordan, who believes lessons can be learned from the demise of former BBC show Football Focus.

8 The BBC currently has a deal to show highlights of Premier League matches until the end of the 2028-29 season Credit: Getty

Football Focus, which first aired on television screens in 1974, came to an end at the end of last season, with the show's first presenter Bob Wilson telling talkSPORT of his disappointment.

Former MOTD pundit Mark Lawrenson has since sparked debate by suggesting that the BBC's flagship show could go the same way.

The iconic football highlights programme has undergone numerous revamps in recent years, with long-serving presenter Gary Lineker stepping down as host at the end of the 2024/25 season, having presented it since 1999.

Earlier this year, it was revealed that traditional linear viewing had declined by 770,000 viewers in December 2025 compared with the same month in 2024.

However, changing audience habits have meant that digital consumption of MOTD has almost doubled since the 2022-23 season.

Is Match of the Day in trouble?

Liverpool legend Lawrenson claimed that retaining authoritative pundits like Alan Shearer is crucial to the BBC programme's future.

Newcastle hero Shearer, who is also a key figure in ex-MOTD presenter Lineker's successful podcast 'The Rest is Football', is reducing his Match of the Day appearances this year to reclaim some weekends.

Put to talkSPORT's Jordan by Jim White that without the care it deserves, MOTD will go the same way as Football Focus, the former Crystal Palace owner replied: "Well, I think there's an element of, 'That's right.'

"Of course, if Mark was still sitting on the show, he probably wouldn't be saying this. There was an element of that, but there's no reason for it to go the same way as Football Focus.

8 Football Focus' 52-year reign on the airwaves came to an end at the end of last season Credit: BBC

"There was a comment made by the BBC chairman [Samir Shah] talking about the necessity to replicate some of the things that were on Football Focus in Match of the Day and make it more about talk.

"And I thought that was an absolutely absurd thing to say, and I think that Match of the Day is a very good show.

"I think, like every show in the world, if you don't have good talent on there, then you are not going to have a good product.

"Shearer's good. I think Wayne [Rooney] is getting much better. The digital landscape is, of course, undermining linear broadcasting.

"It is decimating linear broadcasting. And the figures that you get now of that once upon a time you'd turn on EastEnders and 20 million people would watch it, those days have gone.

"But digital is still underpinned to some extent by the credibility of mainstream media. And so the good pundits that land in mainstream media and do digital as well will still want mainstream media to seed some of their credibility, viability, and validity so that they can do the digital stuff."

8 Premier League legends Shearer and Rooney are MOTD's top pundits Credit: Getty

Will it go the same way as Football Focus?

Jordan continued: "I wrote articles about Football Focus, with due respect to the people that were involved, I thought it was a very poor show that was very poorly presented. And the editorial was poor.

"It was more about virtue signalling and woke rubbish rather than actual subject matter that people wanted to listen to.

"They hid behind the fact that it was other broadcasters that were doing other things, that were games.

"Let me tell you what people watch: 'What's good!' And they don't mind watching it when something else is on.

"They don't mind watching it on behind the red button and replaying it and proving it from a different forum.

"And they don't like bad content. So the reason why Football Focus was eventually wound down is not for all the excuses that they've made, which is that, 'Oh, there's live football on, there's other ways of watching football that have moved on.'

"It's because the content was poor. The presenter wasn't great.

8 BBC Sport chief Alex Kay-Jelski was quick to defend Alex Scott in the wake of Football Focus' demise Credit: BBC

"The subject matter became something that people didn't want to hear or watch anymore.

"So when that day comes for us, we'll be shuffled out the door as well. Right now, that's not our circumstance, and it was theirs.

"Now, if they replicate that kind of thinking, where they put people in positions that shouldn't be there, they start steering content into things that people don't want to watch, then you're going to find that Match of the Day, which is a blueprint show for the BBC around the world, which underpins the value and actually was the cornerstone of the broadcast deals.

"The reason why the Premier League was able to launch was that it still had a terrestrial deal with the BBC, which underpinned and seeded Sky's Opportunity in 1992.

"Without the Match of the Day vehicle, they would never have got the awareness that ultimately got the subscriptions for Sky."

8 Match of the Day broadcasts on Saturday evenings, with MOTD2 screened on Sunday evenings Credit: BBC

Is Match of the Day still as prestigious?

Ex-lead presenter Lineker, who told talkSPORT in June he didn't miss doing the show, was reported to have seen his podcast company earn around £14million from Netflix, which amounts to ten times more than his old BBC wages.

He presented his popular The Rest Is Football podcast from New York during the World Cup, in contrast to his former employers, who drew criticism for their decision to cover the start of the tournament remotely.

Asked whether Match of the Day was still as prestigious in the new digital football landscape, Jordan unequivocally replied: "Yes!"

"But if we get people like Mark Lawrenson telling us not, then eventually people will believe it. It does need to be handled with care.

"The lessons that can be learned from the Football Focus demise, which in its own right, when the people that presented that show over the years, which was an iconic show that we grew up watching and liking and listening to Bob Wilson, Des Lynam and whoever else ran that show. It was a great show.

"It was the precursor to The Weekend. Yes, I know that the audience has been challenged now by a different way of watching television, but people still watch the BBC. People still enjoy watching the BBC.

"If it was good and if the Football Focus show was good, it would still be on now, and it wasn't.

8 Lineker was a staple at the BBC for more than a quarter of a century Credit: Getty Images - Getty

"So if Match of the Day does the same thing as Football Focus, it'll be off. If it doesn't, if it protects the values, looks after good talents, grows the next set of talents that are going to say meaningful, insightful things, doesn't bore us to death.

"I do think there's a paralysis by analysis. I do think some of the over-analysis is a bit repetitive, and the football is a primary factor that we want to watch with a little bit of analysis and interesting people that say insightful things.

"Alan Shearer’s bold. Wayne Rooney's becoming a really good observer. We've got past the ‘mmmmm’ part, and we're now into a situation where he's actually saying things, and he's bold about saying it.

"[Danny] Murphy is a great observer, and they're good pundits. So it has real value in that space."

'If you've seen some of the digital content, it's proper garbage'

Unsubstantiated reports emerged last week that big-name analysts have fallen out with Alex Kay-Jelski, the BBC Director of Sport.

In addition to Shearer, Micah Richards will also be appearing on MOTD less this season, to focus on their successful podcast with Lineker.

With the growth of such mediums, Jordan was asked about Lawrenson's fear that no pundit would feel obliged to stay if they're worried about the show's direction.

"Well, first and foremost, who is worried about it besides you, Mark? Second of all, the digital landscape is what it is, and you can't listen to irresistible force.

"If you've seen some of the digital content, it's proper garbage. And I watched some of the rest of this football stuff over the World Cup.

It was a cure for insomnia. Well done to Netflix for paying a lot of money for it, but they didn't get great content.

"The bottom line is that good content is good content. And there is value in the BBC.

"And I know that we've got big arguments about the BBC's political impartiality. I know we've had arguments about the nature of the way that people behaved on those shows, with Lineker included and Ian Wright and all that motley crew.

"The bottom line is that it's still a good product. And if you get good pundits on there, then you'll have good outcomes.

"If you don't and you allow it to disappear into what Football Focus became, then it will become a thing of the past. And that'll be sad."

8 Lineker was joined by a variety of guests as well as the usual panel of Micah Richards and Alan Shearer Credit: PA

The value of Match of the Day in the modern media landscape has come under scrutiny with highlights of every Premier League game available to watch for free on YouTube or other digital platforms hours before each new episode of the programme airs.

Asked what remains the true value of MOTD in those terms, Jordan responded: "Well, it's distribution opportunity via the BBC.

"The fact that the BBC is a worldwide brand that doesn't just sell into the UK, and the fact that it has good punditry that can be multifaceted, that can do its own thing.

"Pundits, ask Shearer why he's working on Match of the Day. Ask him; he'll tell you."

Does the Premier League still need Match of the Day?

"No, of course it doesn't, but that's not the point, is it? The point is that Match of the Day is an entity.

"I said it was key in 92. And it's a fact. If the highlights package hadn't been negotiated, then the awareness of the Premier League would never have got the traction.

"And so Sky would have never got the opportunities they've got."

When asked if it is still key, Jordan continued: "No, of course not. But is it valuable? We don't expect the same numbers.

"When you watch television shows now, the numbers that people are getting now that are getting excited about - would have been laughed at 20 years ago, because the people are watching their content differently.

8 Match of the Day celebrated its 60th anniversary in 2024 Credit: Getty

"Good content will supersede the availability of bad content.

"You can go onto social media and onto the digital world, and we can listen to people screaming at Man United. Fantastic.

"That's what you're going to watch, and watch-alongs, and all that sort of stuff. That's an audience, and well done to them for that.

"But if you've got good punditry, and you've got the next generation of good pundits that come behind Shearer, the next generation of players that want to cut their teeth in this space, is it challengeable? Yes. Is it under threat? Yes.

"Does it need to raise its game or keep its game at a high level? Yes, it does."

Sports.title: ‘He’s the best’ – Jose Mourinho exposes subtle detail in journalist’s question
Sports.content:
Spanish journalists will have to do a lot better if they want to catch Jose Mourinho slipping.

At a press conference ahead of Real Madrid's LaLiga clash against Real Sociedad, one reporter remarked people inside the club told him Mourinho appeared 'much more relaxed and calm.'

2 Mourinho is already enjoying the limelight in the Spanish capital Credit: Getty

Although it may have been intended as a compliment, there was a curious detail in the reporter's comment that Mourinho latched on to.

What did Jose Mourinho say to the journalist?

"So you have a source inside the club? Good to know," Mourinho replied.

The reporter later noted to Mourinho he had 'a lot' of contacts within the walls of the Bernabeu, prompting another intriguing retort from the Portuguese icon.

"A lot?" Mourinho said.

"You say good things, but if you speak bad of me, be careful."

Mourinho's press conference antics had a number of Madridistas in awe, with one remarking on X: "He's the best."

Jose Mourinho enjoys winning return at Real Madrid

Perhaps the 63-year-old is indeed a more relaxed figure after his second stint in charge of the Spanish giants got off to a dream start.

Summer signing Carlos Espi struck in the 90th minute to help Real secure a 2-1 win over Espanyol.

Jude Bellingham opened the scoring in the ninth minute before Espanyol's Alex Calatrava responded on the half-hour mark.

But Espi ensured there would be one final twist shortly before full time.

2 Espi, who joined Real for £21m this summer, has already won a space in Mourinho's heart Credit: AFP

Kylian Mbappe drove into the box but had the ball poked away from him. Fortunately for Espi, he was in the right place at the right time as he collected the ball and nudged it out of his feet before firing into the net from close range.

When is Real Madrid next game?

Real will aim to make it two wins from two to start the domestic campaign on Wednesday against Real Sociedad at the Bernabeu.

The San Sebastian-based club opened their LaLiga account with a 1-0 loss away to Real Betis.

Real and Mourinho will then cast their attention towards Thursday's Champions League draw, which will be held at UEFA's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.

The draw begins at 5pm BST.

Sports.title: Randal Kolo Muani dug out by new manager just weeks after £32million transfer
Sports.content:
Randal Kolo Muani dug out by new manager just weeks after £32million transfer

Randal Kolo Muani has been openly criticised by Juventus manager Luciano Spalletti after just one game of the new season.

Spalletti called out Kolo Muani for thinking he is playing at 'an exceptional level' when the boss believes that isn't the case.

3 Kolo Muani has faced some tough comments from his boss one game into the season Credit: Getty

The French striker, who spent last season on loan at Tottenham, had three shots in Juve's 1-0 win over Frosinone on Sunday.

But he missed one big chance and only hit the target once, also committing two fouls and completing 58 per cent of his passes.

And his performance hasn't pleased Spalletti, who wasted no time in digging out his new forward.

The Italian also suggested another striker would come in this summer to provide competition for Kolo Muani.

What did Spalletti say about Kolo Muani?

"We went out and got him, we nurtured him, and we know his true worth," Spalletti said on Kolo Muani to DAZN.

"But he needs to realise that he hasn't played for two years - and there's a reason for that.

"Sometimes you think you're at an exceptional level, but in reality, you've left something behind and need to go back and reclaim it."

The Juve manager added: "He knows how to hold up the ball and find space, and he is physically strong...

"But these are matches where he needs to deliver goals. The spaces were all there for him to exploit."

"We are also looking for someone with different characteristics," Spalletti went on to reveal, hinting at another striker coming in to potentially challenge Kolo Muani for a starting spot.

3 Spalletti is clearly not happy with what he is seeing from Kolo Muani at Juve Credit: Getty

3 The Frenchman only scored one Premier League goal for Spurs last season Credit: Getty

Kolo Muani's recent struggles

Kolo Muani joined the Italian giants earlier this month, signing for the club from Paris Saint-Germain for £32.4million.

Spalletti clearly thinks Kolo Muani has to up his game if he wants to succeed at Juventus following a rough couple of years.

He had not played a game for PSG since December 2024 before his permanent exit from France this summer.

A loan spell at Juve in the first half of 2025 bought him some success though, as he scored eight goals in 16 Serie A appearances.

However, after joining Tottenham on loan last year, his goals dried up, with Kolo Muani scoring just five times in 41 games.

Only one of his goals came in the Premier League as he struggled to make an impact for relegation-threatened Spurs.

Now, Juve have signed him for a second time, hoping that he can recapture his form from his previous stint.

But it seems he's not made the most impressive start, with Spalletti desperate to see some more from the 27-year-old.

Sports.title: Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of flop strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson
Sports.content:
Chelsea's summer clear-out continues as Blues close in on agreeing staggering £115MILLION double sale of flop strikers Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea have agreed a staggering £50million sale Liam Delap to Nottingham Forest.

Delap is now in line to leave Stamford Bridge after only a single season, with the Blues having triggered his £30m release clause at Ipswich Town last summer.

He scored one Premier League goal in 28 games in 2025-26, and two in 41 in all competitions.

Delap was missing from the Chelsea squad which defeated Fulham 3-2 in their first Premier League fixture of the season.

The 23-year-old had been training separately to Xabi Alonso’s main group at their Cobham base after being made available for sale, along with Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson is also closing in on a £65m switch to Aston Villa. That would see Chelsea secure their asking price for the 25-year-old Senegalese.

Chelsea have agreed a £50million fee with Nottingham Forest to sell them Liam Delap

Nicolas Jackson is also nearing a £65million move to Aston Villa from Chelsea

The Chelsea star is understood to be keen on a reunion with former boss Unai Emery

They had been seeking at least £50m for Delap. It is believed Forest’s agreement involves £45m plus £5m in add-ons.

It represents a remarkable profit secured by Chelsea after a disappointing campaign for Delap, whose No 9 shirt was handed to Joao Pedro before this current season started.

Delap had been keen to stay at Chelsea and prove himself, but he became surplus this summer.

With Joao Pedro untouchable at the front of Chelsea's attack, they also signed Danny Welbeck from Brighton and have Emmanuel Emegha. Jackson and Marc Guiu are in line to leave.

Sports.title: Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Declan Rice is one of five Arsenal players in attendance - as Man United boss Michael Carrick as well as Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish arrive on the red carpet for Manchester bash
Sports.content:
Stars hit the red carpet at the PFA Awards: Declan Rice is one of five Arsenal players in attendance - as Man United boss Michael Carrick as well as Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish arrive on the red carpet for Manchester bash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A plethora of key figures within English football have all descended upon Manchester ahead of Tuesday night's Professional Footballers' Association (PFA) Awards.

The annual ceremony is taking place this year at the Opera House Theatre.

Among those in attendance sees representation from several Premier League teams.

Champions Arsenal are represented by a key quintet of David Raya, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes, William Saliba and Declan Rice. Those five will hope to be involved in at least the PFA Team of the Year, while potentially collecting the prize for PFA Player of the Year.

Arsenal were in a title pursuit with Manchester City all of last season and beat them in the Community Shield two Sundays ago.

That quintet will cross paths with City trio Antoine Semenyo, Rayan Cherki and Nico O'Reilly who are also there.

Arsenal stars David Raya, Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba (left to right) were on the red carpet ahead of the PFA Awards in Manchester on Tuesday night

Manchester City were represented at the bash by Antoine Semenyo (centre) and Rayan Cherki

Semenyo enjoyed a prolific season at Bournemouth and City last term, while O'Reilly had a breakout campaign which saw him end it as part of England head coach Thomas Tuchel's - who is also attending - World Cup squad which reached the semi-finals.

Aged just 21, the City academy graduate is the favourite to win PFA Young Player of the Year.

City's bitter rivals Manchester United are represented by head coach Michael Carrick and CEO Omar Berrada.

The pair have had a busy day following the £70million transfer completion of Carlos Baleba from Brighton and Hove Albion.

Baleba will add some much-needed dynamism to United's midfield and will play behind captain Bruno Fernandes - who is another leading contender for the PFA Player of the Year award after a fantastic 2025-26 where he broke the Premier League assists record for a single season with 21.

In May, he won the Football Writers' Association's men's Footballer of the Year award and was named Premier League player of the season, meaning it could be a clean sweep of accolades if he's victorious come 9pm.

Liverpool icon Kenny Dalglish also donned the red carpet alongside his wife Marina.

Arsenal are also well represented in the women's game in Manchester with Alessia Russo, Mariona Caldentey, Emily Fox and Olivia Smith representing the Gunners too.

Nico O'Reilly (left) could win PFA Young Player, in front of England boss Thomas Tuchel there

Michael Carrick (left) and Omar Berrada are among those representing Manchester United

Liverpool legend Kenny Dalglish smiles for the cameras alongside his wife Marina

Arsenal Women's Olivia Smith, Mariona Caldentey, Alessia Russo, and Emily Fox (left-right) attended Tuesday's event at the Manchester Opera Theatre

Former Lionesses Karen Carney, Eni Aluko, Jordan Nobbs and Toni Duggan are also in the crowd for Tuesday night's showpiece.

In terms of former male footballers the likes of Mikael Silvestre, Sebastian Bassong, Ashley Young, Asmir Begovic, Kolo Toure are also present.

Ex-Manchester United and Arsenal defender Silvestre hit the headlines on Monday after calling out FIFA president Gianni Infantino, telling him to stand down.

Silvestre, who is part of FIFA's Players' Voice Panel, took to X to demand change, writing: 'Enough is enough!'

The post, which went on to call for structural change within FIFA, was shared by France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit as well as Lioness Lucy Bronze.

Infantino is also facing calls to quit from his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in the wake of a hugely controversial plan to sell stakes in a company to run the World Cup to private investors.

And players have now begun to speak out against the 56-year-old, with Monday's widely shared statement evidential of those who 'share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world'.

Karen Carney (left) and Mikael Silvestre are among the ex-footballers at Tuesday's ceremony

It added: 'Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA's current leadership.

'For too long we've seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

'Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership's ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football.'

Silvestre's interjection is significant given it effectively comes from within the FIFA fold, with the Players' Voice Panel a 16-strong group formed by the global governing body to monitor and advise on initiatives to tackle racism.

The statement continued: 'Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.

'We call on all stakeholders to step forward and help reshape the future of our sport.'

Sports.title: Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Man United youngster Chido Obi Martin linked with loan move to Europe, Red Devils land Carlos Baleba while Nottingham Forest close in on Liam Delap deal: WINDOW WATCH

To catch up on all of yesterday's developments - including Aston Villa making contact with AC Milan over Rafael Leao - click HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

United youngster linked with Feyenoord

Manchester United forward Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Feyenoord.

The Dutch side, coached by Giovanni van Bronckhorst, want cover in case they lose a forward in the final stages of the window.

Obi Martin, a Denmark U21 international, had interest from Cologne earlier in the window.

Feyenoord would also offer Champions League football.

Chido Obi Martin has emerged as a loan target for Dutch side Feyenoord

Forest close in on Delap deal

Nottingham Forest and Chelsea are closing on a £45million deal for Liam Delap.

Talks intensified on Monday following Chelsea's game at Fulham and a verbal agreement is in place for the 23-year-old to link up with Oliver Glasner's team.

He is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours.

Liam Delap is expected to undergo a Nottingham Forest medical in the next 24 hours

United complete Baleba deal

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

‘I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level,' said the 22-year-old, who has signed a five-year contract at Old Trafford.

‘The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.’

For more on this story click HERE

Carlos Baleba with Manchester United's director of football Jason Wilcox

Gonzalez says goodbye to City ahead of £50m Newcastle move

Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez is travelling to the North East to finalise his £50m move to Newcastle United.

The 24-year-old Spaniard will undergo his medical in the next 24 hours.

Gonzalez said his farewells to City team-mates this morning and the deal is set to be £47m plus £3m in add-ons.

Nico Gonzalez will become Newcastle United's latest signing of the summer

City defender Kabore set for Wrexham medical

Manchester City defender Issa Kabore is due for a medical at Wrexham after they agreed a £2million fee. The 25-year-old spent last season on loan at Wrexham and wants to continue with the club as they attempt to take the next step up to the Premier League.

Kabore, who has 55 caps for Burkina Faso, has had eight loan spells since joining City from Mechelen in 2020.

Ipswich Town want £9m for Wrexham target Anis Mehmeti and Birmingham City are also interested.

Issa Kabore, pictured while on loan at Luton in 2024, is set to move to Wrexham

Bees still buzzing about Diouf

Brentford are continuing discussions with West Ham for left wing back El Hadji Malick Diouf. The Senegal international joined last summer from Slavia Prague for £19m but had an indifferent season.

West Ham's El Hadji Malick Diouf is a target for Brentford

Forest talk over £13.6m move for Andre

Nottingham Forest are in talks over a £13.6million move for Corinthians midfielder Andre.

The 20-year-old only made his league debut a year ago but has quickly established himself as one of the best young midfield talents in the Brazilian league.

AC Milan attempted to sign him in January but he wanted to see out the season with Corinthians. Crystal Palace have also been watching him .

Forest have been looking to strengthen their midfield since selling Elliot Anderson to Manchester City.

They have made offers for Lucas Bergvall at Spurs and Tijjani Reijnders who left City for Al Qadsiah.

Wrexham close on £8m move

Wrexham are closing in on a move for highly-rated Angers wing-back Jacques Ekomie as they look to bolster their side for a Premier League push.

Phil Parkinson has been keen to add to his squad before next week’s deadline and it’s understood there has been a breakthrough with Angers for Ekomie, who is valued at around £8million.

Co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac were in attendance for Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Watford and Parkinson revealed he had a ‘good chat’ with the Hollywood pair about transfers.

Ekomie has been a man in demand this summer with interest from Hamburg and West Ham but Wrexham are confident they have won the race to land the 23-year-old.

Wrexham's first bid for Ekomie, rejected on Friday, was £4.3m.

They are also trying for Millwall forward Femi Azeez and Ipswich's attacking midfielder Anis Mehmeti.

NATHAN SALT

Olympiacos in for Edson

Olympiacos have made an offer to take West Ham defensive midfielder Edson Alvarez on loan.

The Mexico international has also had interest from Real Sociedad and Ajax so far.

Doncaster living the life O'Reilly

Doncaster Rovers are set to sign Aston Villa starlet Tommi O’Reilly on a season-long loan.

A plethora of clubs, including Sheffield Wednesday, have been interested in the midfielder who got over 20 goal contributions in League Two last season while on loan at Crewe.

Tommi O'Reilly starred at Crewe Alexandra on loan last season

Tottenham seal Savinho deal

Tottenham have confirmed the signing of Manchester City winger Savinho.

Daily Mail Sport reported last week that a fee had been agreed comprising £75m plus £10m in add-ons.

Roberto De Zerbi's side lost 3-0 at Brentford in their Premier League opener and their new signing will come into the mix ahead of tomorrow's League Cup clash with Charlton. Spurs are also expected to bring in Omar Marmoush in a double swoop from City.

Savinho said: 'It's taken a while but I'm very happy to be here. It's a wonderful opportunity at a brilliant club with one of the best managers in the world.

'As soon as I spoke to the head coach I knew I had to come. He told me he wants to help me reach the highest level, and I believe we can do that together, as a team.'

De Zerbi described Savinho as 'a player who brings energy, imagination and quality in wide positions. He has the courage to attack defenders and the ability to change a game with his creativity.

'We’re very pleased to have him with us, and I’m looking forward to working with him, helping him continue to grow and seeing him bring his personality to the team.'

Savinho signs on the dotted line for his move to Spurs

Pinnock in for Coventry medical

Ethan Pinnock is due to have his medical at Coventry today ahead of singing a three-year contract with an option to extend.

The promoted club agreed a £6m fee with Brentford for the 33-year-old defender yesterday.

Ethan Pinnock is set to bolster Frank Lampard's squad at Coventry

Chelsea in talks over Guiu exit

Napoli are continuing talks with Chelsea for Marc Guiu and defender Mamadou Sarr’s proposed loan to Sociedad is progressing. Chelsea have asked about Atalanta defensive prospect Honest Anahor.

Villa look at Leao deal

Aston Villa are exploring the finances of a deal for AC Milan's Rafael Leao.

Daily Mail Sport reported last night that the club had made contact over the winger, 27. Turkish giants Galatasaray remain in the mix for the Portuguese as well.

Rafael Leao in pre-season action against Chelsea

Bakwa off to Lille

Nottingham Forest winger Dilane Bakwa is joining Lille on loan.

The 23-year-old signed for Forest from Strasbourg last September in a deal worth £30million but has failed to have the desired impact.

He is due for a medical today and will play in the Champions League with Lille.

Dilane Bakwa is set to leave after just one season at the City Ground

City set to go back to Enzo

Manchester City are expected to go back in for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez.

The Blues previously set City a deadline of 5pm on August 13 to pay £120m to get the deal done - a deadline City did not meet.

But contact has continued with his agent Javier Pastore so City know the 25-year-old is open to coming and now they are set to come back in for the midfielder, who played the final half-hour of Chelsea's 3-2 win away at Fulham on Monday night.

For more on this story click HERE

Enzo Fernandez came on as a substitute at Fulham on Monday night
