Sports.title: Sir Billy Boston dead aged 92: Rugby league legend - and the sport's first knight - was a gentle giant and a breaker of barriers, writes OLIVER HOLT - he belongs in the same company as Jackie Robinson and Arthur Ashe
Sports.content:
Sir Billy Boston was a giant of a man, who spoke with gentleness and humility and self-deprecation and who bequeathed a gift to the sport of Rugby League that will last far beyond the records he set and the tries he scored and the entertainment he provided to millions as a player for Wigan.

Sir Billy, who died on Tuesday at the age of 92, was a breaker of barriers, a man who deserves to be remembered in the same company as heroes like Jackie Robinson, major league baseball’s first black player in the modern era, and Arthur Ashe, who swept away so many prejudices in the game of tennis.

Boston became the first non-white player to represent Great Britain on a Lions tour in 1954. He scored 36 tries in 18 appearances in Australia and New Zealand, and played in 31 international Test matches.

The numbers say that he scored 478 tries in 488 matches for Wigan and played in six Challenge Cup finals for the team but his standing in the game and in the world of sport as a whole, the way he carried himself, the way he wore his greatness lightly, made him a hero to many more.

‘Heartbroken to hear my friend Sir Billy Boston has died,’ prime minister Andy Burnham wrote yesterday. ‘Billy was one of the greatest Rugby League players of all time but also one of the kindest and most down-to-earth people you could ever wish to meet. He always had time for people and gave so much to back to his adopted home, Wigan…A giant of a man in every way.’

Today we mourn the loss of a true sporting icon, Sir Billy Boston, who has passed away surrounded by his family.



Rugby League’s first knight, a Wigan legend, and "Everybody's Hero," his legacy on and off the field will endure for eternity.



Rest in peace, Sir Billy. 🍒⚪️ pic.twitter.com/y8Dw9XPPGi — Wigan Warriors 🍒⚪️ (@WiganWarriorsRL) August 25, 2026

Sir Billy Boston was hailed as 'simply the greatest' by Wigan head coach Matt Peet

For the first 130 years of Rugby League’s existence, the establishment did not judge a single one of its players worthy of a knighthood and the omission felt like a sign of society’s disregard and disdain for the sport.

In the same period, rugby union was awarded 20 knighthoods, yachting 12, motor racing eight, horse racing eight and sheep shearing one. It had begun to feel as if rugby league was a pariah.

But two years ago, Billy Boston changed that. His stature was such that he had already had three statues in his honour - in Cardiff, where he was born, at Wembley, where he played in those Challenge Cup finals, and in Wigan, where he lived for the last 72 years of his life – and then there came the final symbolism of the knighthood.

I met him in a hotel on Piccadilly, in London, on the eve of the ceremony at Buckingham Palace in June 2025. He was accompanied to London by Wigan Warriors owner Mike Danson and club legend Kris Radlinski, now Wigan’s chief executive. Boston was 90 by then and a little frail but he still carried himself like a king of old.

Wigan have indicated that they will pay tribute to Boston ahead of their Betfred Super League match against Hull KR on Thursday night and that day in London, Danson and Radlinski both radiated pride in him.

They knew what a hero he was to so many. They knew what he meant to fans of the sport and beyond. They knew he was a crossover star. ‘We’ve just never had that breakthrough moment before,’ Radlinski said.

‘One of the problems is we promote humility and create these humble guys, but we actually need them to be superstars. One thing about rugby league in our town and many northern teams is everybody lives in the town and access is unbelievable. So it’s your biggest strength, but also your biggest weakness.’

Danson also pointed out that only a small percentage of knighthoods are earned by people from the north. If you are northern and working class, that percentage shrinks even more. Boston smashed through that barrier, as well. His death came only four days after the funeral of his wife, Lady Joan, to whom he had been married for 70 years.

Boston grew up playing rugby union before switching codes to sign for Wigan in 1953 at the age of 19 and graced the sport throughout the 50s and 60s. The Welsh Rugby Union paid tribute to him, too, yesterday, and Wigan head coach Matt Peel praised one of the town’s favourite sons.

Boston was knighted by the King last year

'Billy Boston is woven into the fabric of this club,’ Peel said. ‘Every day we walk through the doors, we’re reminded that we have a responsibility to represent all those who have gone before us and made Wigan Warriors what it is today. Billy stands at the very top of that history.

'Those fortunate enough to have seen him play tell me he was simply the greatest. His achievements, the man he was and the standards he set will continue to inspire everyone who pulls on this shirt.

'His legacy goes far beyond records and trophies. His impact on Wigan, on rugby league and on the wider sporting world was recognised at the very highest level. We will do everything we can to honour his memory by representing this club with the pride, humility and excellence that he embodied.

'Sir Billy Boston will always be one of Wigan Warriors’ greatest sons, and he will never be forgotten.'

Sports.title: Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day
Sports.content:
Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

Baleba has signed a five-year-contract at Old Trafford with the option to extend it by 12 months after agreeing personal terms and passing a medical.

United will pay an initial £65m and up to £5m more in add-ons to Brighton who have included a sell-on clause as part of the deal.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international, who is currently sidelined with an ankle injury, becomes United's third midfield signing of the summer after the club spent a total of £85m on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba, who has been linked with United for more than a year, said: 'It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

'I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

Carlos Baleba has completed a £70million transfer to Manchester United from Brighton

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford, with the option for an extra year

'The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.'

United's director of football Jason Wilcox is delighted to complete the club's midfield rebuild after Casemiro left as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte was ruled out for much of this season with a knee ligament injury.

'Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further,' said Wilcox. 'He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

'We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

'Carlos' determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.'

Fans will be relieved to see United get the deal over the line, particularly after their woeful start to the season at Hull City on Saturday.

First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy, both coming from set-pieces, left the Mancunians in the dust.

United's midfield of Santos and Tielemans with Fernandes ahead of them, lacked the dynamism that Baleba should hopefully aid with once he's fit.

Sports.title: Revealed: Chelsea's Spygate threat at Cobham HQ after two unknowns caught walking past training, Cristiano Ronaldo's set-piece analyst joins Blues and what really happened with Enzo Fernandez after Fulham win - CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL
Sports.content:
Revealed: Chelsea's Spygate threat at Cobham HQ after two unknowns caught walking past training, Cristiano Ronaldo's set-piece analyst joins Blues and what really happened with Enzo Fernandez after Fulham win - CHELSEA CONFIDENTIAL

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

There is a secret entrance to Chelsea’s training ground. Those arriving via the nearby Cobham & Stoke D’Abernon train station use it frequently because it beats going the long way around.

Only regular visitors to the club’s Surrey HQ know it is there, this doorway which takes you down a passage surrounded by foliage until you are left walking towards the first-team building.

However, Willie Isa did not appear too pleased with the use of this hidden gate last week. The New Zealand-born former Samoa rugby league star, who is now Chelsea's player support and development officer on Xabi Alonso's staff, seemed irked that two unknowns had walked past what was supposed to be a closed training session on Friday.

Clubs are understandably cautious around unknown visitors to training grounds following the Southampton Spygate scandal earlier this year. As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Saints manager Tonda Eckert sent a junior analyst to record opposition training sessions, for which the club were kicked out of the Championship play-offs in May and docked four points from this season's campaign.

You can only get through the offending Cobham gate if security let you through after verifying your identity, so these individuals will have had clearance to be within the Cobham grounds on this particular afternoon. Yet Isa did not know who they were, and did not seem to like that they had potentially gotten a glimpse of Cole Palmer and Co preparing for their Premier League opener away at Fulham.

Let’s just say the security staff from then on were telling those trying to use this gate that they had better make the 15-minute walk to the front entrance – just as it began raining above Cobham.

Two unknown people were caught walking past Chelsea's closed training session at Cobham, sparking fears of a potential Spygate

Willie Isa (left), the former rugby league star who is now Chelsea's player support and development officer, has warned security not to let anyone in through the offending gate

Blues hire Ronaldo's set-piece analyst

After bringing in Austin MacPhee from Aston Villa, Chelsea have further added to their set-piece department by hiring a new first-team analyst called Andre Reis.

Reis spent the last seven years working with the Portuguese FA, analysing set-pieces for Portugal at the 2026 World Cup, throughout their victorious 2024-25 Nations League campaign and at Euro 2024.

Reis’ role was believed to involve on-pitch work as well as from behind his laptop. He built his way up to helping Cristiano Ronaldo and Co after originally acting as an analyst for Portugal’s youth.

Now, he will be helping Chelsea’s new set-piece specialist MacPhee, who joined this summer from Aston Villa and also spent the last year with Portugal.

Alonso said last week that he wants the ‘best possible specialists’ in every department.

Chelsea have brought in Andre Reis, who has been working with Portugal on set-pieces

Revealed: Hudson-Odoi's agent banned

Callum Hudson-Odoi’s brother, Bradley, who is the former Chelsea and current Nottingham Forest winger’s agent, has been suspended for six months.

Bradley was accused of breaching FA Rule E1.2, and charged with allegedly approaching or representing a minor without first obtaining the additional authorisation; and that he then performed agent services without first entering into a representation agreement.

The FA hit him with a six-month suspension from all activity that falls under the Football Agent Regulations, including but not limited to Football Agent Services. The ban began on Monday this week and it will end on February 24, 2027. He was also fined £500.

Callum, who joined Chelsea as a seven-year-old and went on to make 126 first-team appearances as well as being capped three times by England, signed a new contract with Forest last season which was overseen by his sibling. That deal ties him down to the City Ground until 2028. He was an unused substitute in their opening-day home defeat by Leeds United.

Confidential contacted Bradley for comment and received no reply.

Bradley Hudson-Odoi (right), brother of Callum, came through Fulham's academy and was a non-League forward for 10 years before retiring in 2019 and becoming an agent

Sources say, Liquidator will stay!

Stamford Bridge sources say they will not be following Wolverhampton Wanderers in binning their traditional pre-match playing of The Liquidator.

After a review, Wolves have confirmed the song will be avoided at Molineux, owing to supporters using its tune to chant offensively about their rivals, West Bromwich Albion.

Some Chelsea fans still use The Liquidator to sing ‘f*** off Tottenham’ at the Bridge, though much of the fanbase have been vocal in saying they do not like how a mention of Spurs invades what should be their song as the players prepare to play.

Chelsea’s first home fixture is against Luton Town on Thursday in the Carabao Cup with Brighton visiting in the Premier League on Sunday.

Enzo's full-time antics

Chelsea insiders are anticipating an official move from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez before the summer transfer window closes on September 1, but those inside Stamford Bridge are also entitled to believe they hold the power over this situation.

Fernandez is tied down to a long-term deal, and as shown in Chelsea's Premier League opener away at Fulham, they are happy to keep using him.

They would only sell the Argentine for an enormous sum after spending all summer demanding at least £120million, and they want a replacement lined up. Otherwise, they would be weakening themselves and strengthening a rival.

A video clip on social media appeared to show Fernandez walking away from his Chelsea team-mates and towards the tunnel as they stood in front of the away end following their 3-2 Premier League victory over Fulham.

Chelsea insiders are anticipating an official move from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez before the summer transfer window closes on September 1

However, Confidential was at Craven Cottage, and in his defence, Fernandez did stand in front of the visiting supporters with everyone else. We then watched as Fernandez gave his shirt to a fan in the home end – we think they were holding a River Plate away shirt if our eyes were not deceiving us, in homage to the team he joined as a six-year-old and represented for 15 years – before exiting.

The BBC’s Match of the Day title credits this season include Fernandez in his Chelsea shirt, shown briefly in between Xavi Simons for Tottenham Hotspur and Erling Haaland for City.

It is almost as if the Beeb are tempting fate after the Argentine's noisy ‘will he, won't he’ summer.

Anything can happen while the summer window remains open and City boss Enzo Maresca made a point of using Marc Guehi in midfield next to Elliot Anderson in their 2-1 comeback win over Bournemouth. Anderson left the field injured in the second half.

Neto asking price puts off Saudi bids

Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal turned their attention to Arsenal’s Gabriel Martinelli after learning that Chelsea valued Pedro Neto at close to £100million.

The Blues slapped that valuation on Neto after noting the asking prices for other wingers in this window and because they appreciate him highly internally.

However, Al Hilal are now getting closer to an agreement for Martinelli instead worth between £50-55million, with Neto relegated to a back-up option.

Neto got an earful from Chelsea captain Reece James during their 3-2 win at Fulham for not tracking back after he replaced Malo Gusto as a right wing-back.

Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal turned their attention to Arsenal’s Gabriel Martinelli (right) after learning that Chelsea valued Pedro Neto (left) at close to £100million

Josh steps in and steps up

The Chelsea predicted lineup in Fulham's matchday programme had Wesley Fofana starting in the visitors’ defence despite being suspended for this clash.

In Fofana’s place, Josh Acheampong impressed, though the 20-year-old academy graduate's situation remains one to watch between now and the end of the window. As revealed by Daily Mail Sport last week, Chelsea have been considering whether to keep him where he is or sanction a loan.

They have long maintained that they do not want to sell him permanently. But performances like the one he put in at Fulham may only tell a few suitors that he is ready for more regular game time.

Sports.title: Man United Confidential: Joshua Zirkzee will leave United with Aston Villa and Serie A duo circling, why Amazon documentary is doubling stars' workload and how club have slashed Old Trafford beer queues this season
Sports.content:
Joshua Zirkzee fully expects to leave Manchester United in the next week, Confidential understands.

While there is a feeling that United need more players through the door before Tuesday’s 11pm deadline following the shock opening-day defeat at newly promoted Hull City, there is an expectation that Zirkzee will go – most likely on loan.

A £36.5million signing from Bologna two years ago, Juventus have set their sights on taking Zirkzee back to Italy. There is interest from their Serie A rivals Napoli and Aston Villa have also enquired.

The 25-year-old Dutchman made just five starts in all competitions last season and was an unused substitute at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. Zirkzee is eager to get regular first-team minutes, and the sense around the player is that a compromise is required on all sides to facilitate a move.

Zirkzee is one of the most popular players in the dressing-room, but with his best position being as a No10 – the role occupied by captain Bruno Fernandes – opportunities to play are at a premium.

As for replacing Zirkzee, who has scored just nine times in 75 appearances for the club, United are prioritising a new left-back amid interest in Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde and 19-year-old Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander. But insiders are far from certain there will be any more incomings to add to £155million midfield trio Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba, and free-agent goalkeeper Karl Darlow.

Joshua Zirkzee is expected to leave Manchester United in the next week

After scoring on his United debut at home to Fulham two years ago, Zirkzee has added just eight more goals in 74 appearances

United announced the £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton on Tuesday but are not currently close to adding any more arrivals before the window closes next week

Double or Nothing!

Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary has doubled United’s broadcast commitments this season.

Filming began during the club’s pre-season camp in Dublin earlier this month and hit full flow last week, with crew working on the access-all-areas documentary now part of the furniture at Carrington and Old Trafford. The demands of producing the programme have dawned on those at a club which is already the biggest media draw in the Premier League for players and staff.

The Amazon documentary may be earning the club more than £10million, but it means United face twice the broadcasting demands as before, representing a real challenge in a season that could bring as many as 15 extra games following a return to Europe.

It’s understood that all the United stars have had to sign waivers giving permission to be filmed behind the scenes, and journalists covering the club have done likewise so that footage from Michael Carrick’s press conferences can be included.

MUTV’s studio boost

As much as Amazon are demanding a significant amount of United’s time, Confidential understands the new Snapdragon Studio at Carrington has been installed for the benefit of MUTV rather than the streaming giant.

The editing suite on the first floor of the training ground will be used by the club’s in-house TV station to produce the increasing amount of content United broadcast on their own channels. The equipment there is powered by Snapdragon as part of United’s £60million-a-year shirt sponsorship deal with California-based tech firm Qualcomm which is currently due to run until 2029.

Amazon will have to use their own facilities to produce the highly-anticipated docuseries on United which is due to air in the summer of 2027.

Sleeve it out

With Snapdragon on board as shirt sponsor for at least another three years, and Betway having recently agreed a record deal to have their name on United’s training kit, the club are now looking for a new sleeve sponsor.

United’s £20million-a-year partnership with DXC Technology ran out in May after four seasons, and they kicked off the new campaign at Hull on Saturday without branding on their sleeve for the first time in eight years.

The club were prepared to be patient last season when they went without a training-kit sponsor after the deal with Tezos lapsed, before cashing in on their return to the Champions League this season by signing the multi-year agreement with Betway. The deal, also believed to be worth £20m-a-year, is said to be the biggest standalone training kit or playing shirt sleeve deal in world football.

Reds escape rail chaos

United avoided the rail chaos that affected many of their 2,400 fans at Hull on Saturday by travelling back from Humberside on the team bus – although some players returned under their own steam.

United stars trudge off the pitch at the MKM Stadium after the 2-0 defeat at Hull City last Saturday

The Reds routinely take the train to games in London, and usually fly further afield, but the 200-mile round trip between Manchester and Hull meant that Carrick and his squad went there and back by bus.

It was just as well after the matchday announcer at the MKM Stadium appeared to take great pleasure in informing the United fans that the trains scheduled to depart from Hull for Manchester at 3.30pm and 5.03pm had been cancelled – much to the delight of the Hull supporters.

The team bus got away on time, but not before Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw were spotted walking across the car park towards their own transport. Confidential understands that several other United players did the same because they had plans for their day off on Sunday.

OT is pitch perfect

United may have requested to kick off the new season away from home so they could complete a major upgrade of the pitch at Old Trafford, but Confidential understands that the stadium would comfortably have been ready to host a game last weekend.

The turf has been relaid for the first time in 14 years – complete with new foundations and drainage system – and United have also taken steps to protect the players from injury by safeguarding the perimeter of the pitch.

The club confirmed earlier this summer that ‘the grass is being extended to provide a consistent surface at pitchside, and a layer of protection is being added to the brickwork at the foot of Old Trafford’s famous slope’.

There had been concerns over the ditch and perimeter wall that were created when the pitch was elevated in the 1990s, with players at risk of injury if they came off the grass at speed and collided with the advertising hoardings. Most recently, Benjamin Sesko hurt his shin in the victory over Liverpool in May, with the Slovenian only returning to action at Hull on Saturday.

United have also upgraded the home and away dugouts to increase the number of seats for substitutes and coaching staff from 16 to 20, in keeping with UEFA criteria ahead of the club’s return to the Champions League.

Benjamin Sesko hurt his shin after colliding with an advertising hoarding in the victory over Liverpool in May, with the Slovenian only returning to action at Hull on Saturday

All the work was completed in advance of United’s trip to Humberside, meaning the club could have played at Old Trafford last weekend after all, although insiders say the extra week will give the new turf – which is made up of 96 per cent natural grass and four per cent artificial fibres – more time to mature before Sunday’s home opener against Ipswich Town.

United have made the improvements despite pressing ahead with plans to build a new stadium to replace Old Trafford, hopefully by 2035.

The club have also improved the stadium experience for fans as part of new partnership with Levy, the sports and entertainment hospitality specialists. It aims to provide a better quality, faster service for supporters which has seen new draught beer taps installed around Old Trafford. There will be more self-service bars which will enable fans to tap their payment card and grab a beer, which should reduce queues and improve flow.

There will also be a wider range of dining options outside the ground, including a number of kiosks featuring independent Manchester vendors selling street food.

JJ passes Under 21s audition

Confidential was in position at Leigh Sports Village on Monday night to witness JJ Gabriel’s stunning competitive debut for the Under 21s.

Gabriel, still only 15, scored a sublime goal when he chipped Ipswich Town goalkeeper Woody Williamson from outside the area, and also added two assists for Victor Musa and Jaydan Kamason.

Michael Carrick and his assistant Steve Holland were among the small crowd in Leigh, and it was hard not to marvel at Gabriel’s display as he thrived in a No10 role.

The Under-21s played in a 4-2-3-1 system to mirror the first team, even playing without a recognised No9, much like Carrick did at Hull by using Matheus Cunha through the middle. That allowed Gabriel to play the Bruno Fernandes role. The expectation is that Gabriel will train regularly with the first team throughout the season while also playing a starring role in the Under 21s.

JJ Gabriel, still only 15, scores a sublime chip from the edge of the area against Ipswich Town Under 21s

He scored 29 times across 32 appearances last season, helping his team reach the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under 18s Cup finals

He was outstanding for the Under 18s under Darren Fletcher last season despite starting it as a 14-year-old. He scored 29 times across 32 appearances, helping his team reach the FA Youth Cup and Premier League Under 18s Cup finals.

Carrick and Holland were beaming by full time. With a star like Gabriel on their hands, who could blame them?

Scouts flock to see Under 21s

It was noticeable just how many EFL scouts were there on Monday night to watch an Under 21s team that is still ripe for picking before next week’s deadline.

Kamason and Harry Amass, who started at right-back and left-back in the 5-0 win, are both expected to draw interest. Confidential understands that both are expected to leave, with permanent exits not being ruled out as both players draw significant interest in the Championship, with nothing left for either to gain in academy football.

United have cashed in on several young players this summer as Radek Vitek, Tyler Fredricson and Ethan Williams left the club permanently, with buy-back clauses and matching rights included as part of their exit packages.

Jaydan Kamason celebrates scoring the third goal in United Under 21s' 5-0 win over Ipswich

Harry Amass, who started at left-back on Monday against Ipswich, is also likely to leave United in the next week

New cyber threat warning

News that Premier League teams face a fine of up to £100,000 if they fail to follow new cybersecurity rules coming into effect this season revived memories of the attack on United in November 2020, which paralysed the club’s computer network.

Staff were forced to communicate by WhatsApp for several weeks after the ransomware attack crippled United’s email accounts and other systems, forcing the club to call in the National Cyber Security Centre for help.

It was never revealed how much the hackers demanded as a ransom – or if United paid up – but the NCSC said at the time that the biggest single loss to a sports organisation from cyber-crime was £4million. United are believed to have upgraded their cybersecurity since then in an attempt to prevent another breach. The new rules will be implemented in three phases through April 2029.

Jamie Akhtar, CEO and co-founder of CyberSmart, said: ‘This is an important shift for the Premier League. Cyber security is moving from being viewed primarily as an IT responsibility to becoming an enforceable element of club governance.

‘Football clubs hold significant volumes of sensitive supporter, employee and player data, while also relying on systems for ticketing, payments, stadium access and matchday operations.’

Wes & Pally at Salford

Given that United host Ipswich Town on Sunday, those at a loose end on Saturday need look no further than Salford Lads & Girls Club.

United are teaming up with the iconic club to host an open day where former players Wes Brown and Gary Pallister will be in attendance. The pair are hosting a Q&A at the event which will give fans the chance to buy limited edition adidas third shirts, which have been designed to celebrate the Salford club’s centenary year.

A football fun day, which starts at midday, for those after a football fix on Saturday.

Sports.title: What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery, why he could still sign new contract and Villa's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins’ absence from the Aston Villa team for the opening-day thrashing at Brighton is the latest chapter in a story that started 18 months ago.

Manager Unai Emery was so enraged by his star striker's omission from the matchday squad on the south coast amid rumours of a move to Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal that he could only reply 'silence' when asked what had caused it, adding: 'I think you can call him, call his agent and he can respond.'

The England forward spoke to his team-mates on Monday to explain his side of the story and was expected to return to some training this week. The stance remains the same: Villa are willing to sell Watkins to the Saudis, but only if their current valuation of at least £50million is matched.

That may shift in the days ahead, with Villa seeking reinforcements in defence, out wide and at centre-forward. Though this row might have been handled differently by both sides, it has not come from a clear blue sky.

Daily Mail Sport looks at how we got here and what might happen next.

Where it all began

At some point last week, Watkins had a discussion with Unai Emery. The Villa boss left those talks believing Watkins wanted to move to Al Hilal and was prepared to go to significant lengths to ensure the deal went through.

Unai Emery was in no mood to protect Ollie Watkins when his star striker was not available for the opening day at Brighton

Al Hilal, whose squad includes former Wolves captain Ruben Neves (furthest right) and Chelsea centre back Kalidou Koulibaly (second right) need to match Villa's £50m valuation

Watkins did not train last week as he waited for Villa to accept a bid. Al Hilal did not make the required offer and once he understood Watkins would not be involved in the preparation work, Emery did not consider him for last Sunday’s match at Brighton.

Without the injured Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, strikerless Villa were hammered 4-0 and Emery did nothing in his media appearances to protect Watkins. Sure enough, the 30-year-old was targeted mercilessly by supporters online.

To understand why this happened, we must rewind to a sliding doors moment for Villa and Watkins – Boxing Day 2024. In the previous three league games, Emery had decided to pick Jhon Duran, the chaotic but brilliant Colombian, ahead of Watkins, and Duran had scored in all three.

Heading into the next match at Newcastle, it looked as though Duran had become Villa’s undisputed No1 striker and the club started to make contingency plans for January. They knew Arsenal were chasing a forward and had an interest in Watkins, a boyhood Gunners fan.

Then Duran was given a straight red card at Newcastle and when he completed his suspension, Emery did not feel his form or attitude merited a return to the team. Al Nassr arrived with a £70million offer for Duran and Villa decided to cut their losses on a player who was hugely difficult to manage.

Villa were unwilling to sell both forwards in the same window and Watkins was denied his dream move to Arsenal, whose offers never approached Villa’s £65million valuation. The forward was disappointed but at the end of the window, Emery said: ‘Now we need him, like he needed Aston Villa.’

As far as the Spaniard is concerned, the same applies now. Emery has already lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa this summer and wants a few senior men to stick with him to build the new era, which includes another Champions League campaign this season.

Usually, Emery does not stand in a player’s way if he wants to depart but this one feels more personal.

Aston Villa have already lost the likes of Youri Tielemans (left) and Morgan Rogers (right) this summer and Watkins (centre) may be next

Jhon Duran was primed to be Villa's No1 striker 18 months ago before a red card at Newcastle

Contrasting positions

Watkins is easily the top client at Two Touch, the agency run by former Arsenal youngster Paolo Vernazza which represents an extensive list of players including Watkins’ Villa team-mate Matty Cash and Crystal Palace midfielder Will Hughes.

If Watkins were to move to Al Hilal, it would likely be one of Two Touch’s biggest deals and it is clear Villa are unhappy with how Vernazza has handled it. Vernazza may yet push this one through but were he to have his time again, he might make a different plan. Daily Mail Sport has attempted to contact Vernazza since Sunday but he has yet to respond.

Watkins is thought to earn a little more than £100,000 a week at Villa yet the salary proposed by Al Hilal is thought to be substantially more. Watkins has been Villa’s leading scorer in every season since he joined from Brentford in 2020 and is their all-time top Premier League marksman.

He has also seen Ezri Konsa, who is two years younger, allowed to join Arsenal for roughly the same sum Villa want from Al Hilal. Watkins turns 31 in December and if he believed Villa’s price was too high for a player his age, you could understand it. Not surprisingly, Villa see it differently.

Since Emery took charge in 2022, Watkins has developed into one of the best strikers in Europe, thanks also to Emery’s willingness to back him. Duran had to score five times after coming off the bench before he was given a run in the side. Donyell Malen was sold to Roma last January because Emery backed Watkins over the Dutchman, who has since scored 18 times in 21 games for the Serie A club.

Even when Watkins scored only once before December last season, and only once more between January 4 and March 11, Emery kept faith – and was rewarded when his main man hit 12 in 13 games at the end of the season to force his way into England’s World Cup squad.

Emery has lost four key players this summer and with two forwards injured, he felt he really needed Watkins at Brighton. No wonder he was ticking before the pre-match interviews. With Emery, the less he says, often the angrier he is.

He looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual, grew irritable with the opposing bench and stalked down the tunnel at full time without approaching Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler for a handshake. Emery and Hurzeler are certainly not best friends, but the reaction was still telling.

Emery looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual and grew irritable with the opposing bench

Watkins struck 12 goals in the final 13 games of last season to force his way into England's squad for the World Cup, where he scored in the warm-up against Costa Rica

Is there a way back?

A year ago, it looked as though Emiliano Martinez had played his final game for Villa. Desperate to move to Manchester United or Atletico Madrid, Martinez was not included in the Villa side for the home defeat by Crystal Palace – a display just as bad as the Brighton one.

Martinez is still at Villa today, still trying to get out, though he knuckled down last season and helped the club win the Europa League. So it would be foolish to write off Watkins’ Villa career just yet.

The Saudi Pro League’s top clubs can also be ruthless. If they decide a target is no longer worth pursuing, they will move on. Right now, that is the nightmare scenario for Watkins.

Yet the best outcome for all parties is probably to agree a deal. Watkins would have a huge job winning over Villa fans again. If he moves, he will have his new chapter and Villa will be able to pursue his replacement.

If Watkins stays Villa will give him a new deal, but that risks a loveless marriage. Despite the late goal rush, there were signs last season that Watkins was in decline. Do player or club really want to be tied to one another for the next two or three seasons?

There have already been informal talks behind the scenes regarding Nicolas Jackson and Emery is keen on the Chelsea striker, who he coached at Villarreal. In midfield, they hope Leon Goretzka will arrive while there have been discussions for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez, even though he is injured.

There have already been informal talks behind the scenes regarding Nicolas Jackson and Emery is keen on the Chelsea striker, who he coached at Villarreal

There have been discussions for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez (right), even though he is injured. Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they host Arsenal on Monday

Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they take on Arsenal at Villa Park on Monday.

With both Abraham and Madjo still struggling, one of Villa’s best-ever forwards risks being booed by some of his own fans in their first home game of the season, against the team he supported.

If nothing else, that prospect should focus a few minds.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
