World.title: Iraq to allocate $15 billion for delayed projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq plans to allocate 20 trillion Iraqi dinars (about $15 billion) in its draft 2027 budget primarily to complete delayed projects while entirely blocking funds for new projects.

The state budget approach indicates a clear shift toward performance-based expenditure, cost savings, and meeting long-term infrastructure obligations.

The entire capital expenditure portion of the budget focuses on revitalizing infrastructure. Mazhar Saleh, the financial adviser to Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, stated in an interview with Iraq’s official newspaper al-Sabah that there will be no funding allocated for new development projects.

The proposed budget offers a low-risk average oil price target of $60 to $70 per barrel.

Hospitals, schools, bridges, tunnels, and water networks are among the critical public services targeted by the multibillion-dollar commitment.

Following the decision to skip a formal 2026 budget due to regional disturbances, the Iraqi parliament’s financial committee anticipates the official 2027 draft being submitted for approval between late October and early November 2026.

While focusing on current projects gives a more direct path to infrastructure improvement, Iraq is reorganizing its budget due to severe financial pressures.

The Iraqi Ministry of Finance is working with the World Bank to shift from traditional line-item expenditure to a program-and-performance approach.

Iraq’s budget deficit exceeded 21 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $16.1 billion) in the first half of the year due to huge governmental payroll expenditures. As a result, more than 1,800 development projects have been canceled or suspended.

Military operations in the region and shipping restrictions via the Strait of Hormuz have slashed marine crude exports, which account for more than 85 percent of state revenue.

To secure cash for the 2027 budget, Baghdad has allowed three-month temporary marketing mechanisms to diversify export outlets and is focusing on pipelines through Turkey and Syria to increase oil exports.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate slightly falls against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight decline on Tuesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,543.5 Iraqi dinars on Tuesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,537.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,544.5 and 1,543.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq, Germany discuss international coalition withdrawal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Commander of German Forces Deployed Abroad, Gunter Schneider, met on Monday in Baghdad to organize the US-led international coalition forces’ imminent withdrawal from Iraq.

The meeting addressed strategies to strengthen bilateral relations between Iraq and Germany in the military and security fields through initiatives aiming to improve the performance of the Iraqi armed forces, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stressed the need to develop broader partnerships with the international coalition’s member countries. He praised Germany for aiding Iraq in its battle against terrorism, notably during the confrontation with ISIS.

Al-Zaidi said earlier that the military mission of the international coalition will expire on September 30, 2026, and that the decision is final and irreversible.

The prime minister underscored that October 1 will bring in a new period of total Iraqi independence and full territorial sovereignty, with no foreign military presence.

Iraq’s future interactions with the international coalition’s member states will focus on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared military victory over ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to provide advice and training services at Baghdad’s request.

The official withdrawal of the international coalition follows a bilateral arrangement agreed upon by Baghdad and Washington.

World.title: Nasiriyah International Airport reaches 68% completion, targets early 2027 opening
World.content:
Nasiriyah (IraqiNews.com) — Construction work on the Nasiriyah International Airport project in Dhi Qar Governorate has reached a 68% overall completion rate, according to statements made on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, by Captain Ihab Saad, Director General of the General Company for Airports Management and Air Navigation Services.

Saad characterized the construction momentum as continuous and accelerating, confirming that the facility is projected for official delivery in early 2027, provided current construction schedules proceed without unforeseen disruptions.

Technical Milestones & Equipment Inspection

Current Progress: Civil and structural engineering works stand at 68% completion.

Ground Handling Systems: Progress rates are set to increase significantly upon the delivery and installation of new ground handling and airfield equipment batches.

Factory Acceptance Testing in China: A specialized technical committee is traveling to China to conduct rigorous factory acceptance tests on navigational, baggage, and ground operations equipment prior to on-site installation.

Contractual Adjustments: Project authorities have resolved primary operational bottlenecks and are finalizing a new contract appendix to formally settle remaining technical and logistical requirements.

The foundation stone for Nasiriyah International Airport was laid in June 2021 to serve as a major commercial and logistics hub for southern Iraq:

International Contractors: In mid-July 2024, the Ministry of Transport finalized a consultancy and design contract appendix with Turkish firm Kiklop Design Hertz Insaat, alongside an amended engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract with China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC).

Delivery Schedule Evolution: Following earlier timeline revisions from late 2025 into early 2026, project management has established early 2027 as the targeted commissioning window to accommodate factory testing, equipment integration, and final aviation certification.

Upon completion, Nasiriyah International Airport will serve as a critical gateway for passenger transit, business investment, and cultural tourism in Dhi Qar, providing direct international connectivity to the ancient city of Ur, the Mesopotamian Marshes (Ahwar), and surrounding southern industrial zones.

World.title: Iraq continues to be South Korea’s fourth-largest oil supplier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq was the fourth largest crude oil supplier to South Korea in the first half of 2026, accounting for 7.4 percent of the country’s total oil imports.

According to the Korea Petroleum Association (KPA) and the Korea National Oil Corporation, South Korea imported 467.12 million barrels of crude oil in the first half of the year, an eight percent decline compared to the same period in 2025.

However, the value of the country’s oil imports increased by 8.1 percent to $41.36 billion as global oil prices surged, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Saudi Arabia was the largest supplier of oil to South Korea, making up 30.5 percent of the country’s total oil imports. The United States followed with over 20 percent of South Korea’s crude oil imports.

Oil supplies from the United Arab Emirates accounted for 15.1 percent of South Korea’s oil imports.

The figures indicate a notable shift in South Korea’s oil supplies, with Middle Eastern oil falling from 68.7 percent to 62.3 percent throughout the time. This shift is basically due to the effects of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which caused interruptions in oil supplies worldwide.

Iraq’s average oil shipments to South Korea totaled 113.7 million barrels in 2025, which is an average of 311,500 barrels per day. This represents a 12 percent increase compared to 2024.

World.title: Iraq U20 Draws 0-0 with Iran to Wrap Up Thailand Training Camp
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraq Under-20 national football team played to a 0–0 draw against Iran on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, in Bangkok, concluding their final overseas preparatory camp ahead of the upcoming AFC U20 Asian Cup qualifiers.

The friendly encounter was attended by Iraq Football Association (IFA) Executive Board members Khalaf Jalal, who heads the youth national team delegation, and Abdul Razzaq Akram Al-Shalah.

Iraq completes its preparatory training camp in Thailand with an unbeaten 3-match run:

Match 1: Iraq 1 – 0 Kuwait

Match 2: Iraq 2 – 1 Indonesia

Match 3: Iraq 0 – 0 Iran

The scoreless draw against Iran provided the coaching staff with a high-intensity defensive and tactical test against one of the continent’s perennial youth powerhouses, following back-to-back victories against Kuwait and Indonesia earlier in the camp.

Following the conclusion of the Bangkok camp, the Iraqi youth squad will relocate to the host city of Chonburi, Thailand, to begin their official qualification campaign.

Iraq has been drawn into Group F, competing against:

Thailand(Host nation)

United Arab Emirates

Turkmenistan

The group winners, alongside the best-ranked runners-up across all qualification groups, will secure direct berths to the final tournament of the AFC U20 Asian Cup.

World.title: U.S. prepares to return diplomats to Iraq and Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The United States is preparing to return evacuated foreign service personnel to several diplomatic missions across the Middle East, according to an internal U.S. State Department document and confirmations from three U.S. officials reported by The New York Times on Tuesday, August 25, 2026.

The decision indicates that Washington does not anticipate a return to full-scale regional hostilities following recent conflict escalations, despite stalled direct talks between Washington and Tehran and renewed threats of economic sanctions.

Phased Staffing Levels by Mission

The State Department’s operational plan outlines specific staffing quotas and regional safety parameters:

Iraq, Kuwait, and Bahrain: Restoring on-site diplomatic staff up to 75% capacity.

UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Lebanon: Restoring on-site personnel up to 85% capacity, with Lebanon receiving some of the earliest returnees.

Israel, Jordan, and Oman: Authorizing a 100% full return of diplomatic personnel.

Dependent Travel Restrictions: Washington will maintain strict restrictions on accompanying family members across Lebanon and all six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, reflecting a calibrated security posture where overall threat levels have declined relative to the peak of the conflict but remain elevated compared to baseline conditions.

The planned return follows progressive emergency evacuations initiated in late February and early March 2026:

Pre-Strike Precautionary Moves: In late February 2026, non-essential personnel and family members at the U.S. mission in Jerusalem were offered voluntary departure immediately preceding joint military operations.

Baghdad Evacuations and Standoff: In early March 2026, the State Department ordered the mandatory drawdown of non-emergency staff across regional posts, including Baghdad, ahead of drone and rocket strikes targeting the U.S. Embassy compound on March 17.

Ceasefire Dynamics: While a 60-day ceasefire expired last week without formal renewal terms finalized, U.S. security assessments determined that resuming partial mission staffing balances operational foreign policy objectives with on-ground personnel safety.

Former U.S. diplomatic and defense officials noted that while redeploying personnel underscores an administrative assessment that active war footing is receding, emergency contingency mechanisms remain in place should regional security dynamics shift.

World.title: Iraq discusses launching direct flights to Austria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The first deputy speaker of the Iraqi parliament, Adnan al-Dulaimi, and the Austrian ambassador to Iraq, Axel Wech, discussed on Tuesday the launch of direct flights between Baghdad and Vienna.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two sides discussed strategies to develop bilateral relations and activate the meetings of the Iraqi-Austrian Joint Committee within the framework of the Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Both sides emphasized the need to establish a direct air link between Baghdad and Vienna to improve collaboration in a variety of sectors, notably the economy.

Iraqi and Austrian officials have held high-level discussions, including most recently during the Munich Security Conference, to push for the formal resumption of direct passenger flights between Baghdad and Vienna.

During a meeting with Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner in February, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein urged Austria to resume direct flights between Baghdad and Vienna.

The Iraqi foreign minister stated that the return of direct flights between Baghdad and Vienna, given the considerable improvement in security in Iraq, will stimulate travel and economic and tourism interchange between the two countries.

The negotiations built on a prior agreement between Iraqi and Austrian aviation officials to help pave the way for European airlines.

Both parties underline that direct flights will boost bilateral trade, reduce travel restrictions, promote tourism, and make mobility easier for foreign investors.

Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called upon Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to pivot away from being framed solely by climate vulnerability and isolation, while also urging global leaders and private sector partners to view island economies as dynamic "laboratories for innovation".Delivering a keynote statement at the opening ceremony of the Small Island Developing States Global Business Network (SIDS GBN) Forum 2026, Muizzu outlined an economic modernization plan aimed at turning geographic constraints into digital and strategic advantages.With the global dialogue surrounding small island nations focused on their acute climate risk, geographical isolation, and structural economic constraints, Muizzu stressed that vulnerability represents only half the story."For too long, the story of Small Island Developing States has been told primarily through the lens of vulnerability. The other part is our determination. Our scale can become an advantage. SIDS can serve as laboratories for innovation and incubators for ideas, technologies, and solutions,â he said.The president's address focused on the Maldives 2.0 agenda, designed to leverage technology to overcome the traditional barriers of an archipelagic state.Under this strategic initiative, the Maldivian government aims to expand its digital and creative sectors, setting a target for these industries to account for 15 percent of national GDP by 2030.âWe have identified the digital economy and digitalisation as central to advancing our economy. Through our Maldives 2.0 agenda, we are working to use digital connectivity to overcome the limitations of geography and scale â making government and financial services more accessible, enabling businesses to operate more efficiently, and connecting Maldivian enterprises and talent to global markets,â said Muizzu.The Maldives is enhancing financial technology accessibility for micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). Key measures include launching homegrown digital payment platforms such as BML Swipe and expanding international gateway integration through services like PayPal.Muizzu also announced plans for the country's first Trade Acceleration Zone, set to launch by January 1, 2027, to incentivize enterprise development and fast-track commercial growth.While reaffirming the Maldives' commitment to attracting international capital through a modernized foreign investment framework, Muizzu stressed that foreign partnerships must align with national interests. New legal safeguards have been introduced to protect domestic commerce by reserving specific commercial activities strictly for local entities, ensuring economic growth directly benefits Maldivian citizens, he stressed.Muizzu called upon international investors, technology companies, and global financial institutions to establish concrete commercial partnerships with small island states. He reiterated the Maldives' commitment to implementing the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS), urging global stakeholders to bridge the gap between initial innovation and sustainable commercial financing.

World.title: India, China to work towards political settlement of boundary question in long-term interests; Beijing stresses package solution
World.content:
Ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month, India and China held the 25th round of Special Representatives (SR) Dialogue on the Boundary Question, endorsing efforts to formalise the recent turnaround in the relationship on the back of border peace and discussing issues like de-escalation, boundary demarcation and border management.

After the talks chaired by Special Representatives

and Wang Yi, while India said both sides agreed to work towards a political settlement of the boundary question in their long-term interests, Beijing also recalled a 2005 bilateral agreement to stress its proposal for a package solution.

Doval was quoted as saying by the Chinese side that India and China are partners, not competitors, and developing a stable, predictable, and forward-looking India-China relationship carries great significance also for Asia and the world.

âThe normalcy we have witnessed in our relationship has been a direct result of both sides maintaining peace and tranquillity in the border areas,â said Doval, stressing the significance of border peace for further progress in bilateral ties. Wang, however, reiterated Chinaâs position that the border issue must be placed in an âappropriate positionâ in ties.

According to a Chinese readout, Doval and Wang held "in-depth communications" on advancing boundary demarcation negotiations, improving border management and control and promoting cross-border cooperation, while reaffirming their commitment to the 2005 agreement on political parameters and guiding principles for a "fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable package settlement" to the boundary question.





China had dropped the mention of package settlement, which seeks a quid-pro-quo approach, in its readout of the last round of talks but had used it regularly for SR meetings earlier. Indian governments in the past, like in 2007 in Parliament, have said that they were exploring a "final package settlement" covering all sectors of the boundary under the 2005 bilateral agreement but India has not used that formulation recently, stressing instead on a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable settlement framework.

On this occasion, the Indian government said in a statement that under the strategic guidance of PM Narendra Modi and President Xi, - in a constructive and forward-looking spirit â Doval and Wang had a candid exchange of views and agreed to continue their work in seeking a "political settlement of the boundary question in the context of their overall and long-term interests".

The SR talks took place ahead of likely back-to-back bilateral meeting between Modi and Xi - first in Kyrgyzstan on the margins of the upcoming SCO summit and second at the BRICS summit that India will host on September 12-13.

Xi is expected to arrive in India on September 12 for his first visit to the country in 7 years. While the schedule is yet to be confirmed, official sources said he will have a bilateral meeting with Modi and attend the PM's welcome dinner for BRICS leaders on September 12, before participating in the BRICS summit the next day.

On the boundary issue, the Chinese side further said that both countries agreed to properly handle the boundary question through dialogue and consultation, jointly safeguarding peace and tranquility in the border areas.

According to Beijing, Wang said that China-India relations have surpassed the bilateral scope and hold global and strategic significance and pointed to consensus reached in Modi-Xi metings in Kazan and Tianjin.

"China is willing to join hands with India to grasp bilateral relations from a strategic height and long-term perspective, strengthen communication, enhance understanding, resolve differences, overcome obstacles, and serve as good neighbors, friends, and mutually enabling partners, thereby realizing the vision of the Dragon-Elephant Tango," said Wang.

World.title: 2 killed at NHAI construction sites in J&K
World.content:
JAMMU: Two workers, aged 25 and 45, died in two separate accidents at NHAI construction sites in Samba and Jammu districts in J&K on Tuesday.

âGotam Sahu, from Bihar, was engaged in laying the pier of a bridge on the Delhi-Amritsar-Katra project in Sambaâs Jakh, when a concrete structure collapsed suddenly, killing him on the spot.

Another worker, also from Bihar, suffered injuries,â said NHAI project director Rajiv Kumar.

In a similar incident, Budhi Singh (45), from Ramban, died after falling from a height at his workplace near Sidhra Tawi Bridge construction site in Jammu on Tuesday, officials said.

âHe was rushed to Govt Medical College and Hospital (GMCH), Jammu, where doctors declared him dead,â an official said.

World.title: Hydel project shutdown triggers power crisis in J&K
World.content:
Baglihar stage-I in Ramban district has remained non-operational for a week (Photo for representation)

SRINAGAR: Jammu & Kashmir is grappling with power shortages and unscheduled outages after key hydroelectric projects, including the 450MW Baglihar stage I and the Salal project, were shut for silt-flushing operations. Baglihar stage-I in Ramban district has remained non-operational for a week, with accumulated silt at its gates delaying restoration work.Officials said desilting work at Baglihar stages I and II and the Salal project began on Aug 18. While Baglihar stage II resumed generation on Aug 22, stage I is yet to restart. Salal is expected to resume operations on Tuesday.The prolonged shutdown has widened the regionâs power deficit. Jammu & Kashmirâs peak electricity demand stands at about 2,500MW in summer and 3,000MW in winter. With both Baglihar units largely unavailable for most of the past week, Jammu & Kashmir faced a shortfall of nearly 900MW.Built on the Chenab river, Baglihar stages I and II are among Jammu & Kashmirâs key power sources. Following the disruption, the power department is exploring alternative arrangements to bridge the supply gap.The crisis comes amid criticism of the Omar Abdullah-led govt over rising electricity tariffs. From Sept 1, power consumers in Jammu & Kashmir will face a 6.83% tariff hike.

World.title: 8 terror suspects held in Kashmir; arms-ammo, posters seized
World.content:
SRINAGAR: Joint teams of security forces arrested eight terror suspects and seized arms, ammunition, and other incriminating material in separate operations in three Kashmir districts.

Six arrests were made in south Kashmirâs Shopian district and two in Pulwama, also in south Kashmir. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmirâs Sopore district, J&K Police said Tuesday, claiming the action had dealt a major blow to terror networks operating in the Union Territory.

During a naka check at Shopianâs Heerpora, a joint team of the Army, CRPF and J&K Police intercepted a two-wheeler. Three suspects â Junaid Muzaffar Dar, Aamir Yousaf and Junaid Bashir Dar; all from south Kashmirâs Kulgam district â were arrested after two hand grenades and incriminating posters were recovered from their possession, a police statement said.

In a separate operation in Shopian, three terrorist associates â Haris Manzoor, Ashiq Hussain and Arif Ahmad Kumar; all from south Kashmirâs Anantnag district â were arrested by a joint patrolling team of the Armyâs 34RR, CRPF, and local police. Security personnel seized a hand grenade, two AK-47 magazines, 20 rounds and incriminating posters from them, the statement said.

World.title: 'Country is not a dharamshala': Amit Shah sets target for illegal immigration-free India
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah on Tuesday said the Narendra Modi govt has set a goal to make the country illegal immigration-free in a âvery short period of timeâ and, for this purpose, reached out to the border states over the past eight months, sharing with them its document on a quadrangular approach to border security.

The policy drawn up by the Centre enlists the border guarding forces, state and district administration, relevant arms of govt of India and local citizens as key stakeholders in securing the borders.

Addressing the valedictory session of the national security strategy conference (NSSC) organised by Intelligence Bureau here, Shah reiterated that âthis country is not a Dharamshala and only the citizens have the right to live hereâ.

âInfiltrators are a threat of the countryâs security, economy and trigger unnatural demographic shifts,â he stated at the event attended by over 850 officials of the Central security agencies and forces, the state/UT police and intelligence agencies.

With NSSC focused on anticipating security trends and challenges over the next 15-20 years and devising strategies to avert them, Shah underlined that challenges should be identified and destroyed before they become big.





"By creating such an ecosystem, we will be able to create a secure, infiltrator-free and narcotics free India,â he told the officers that included both young ones at the cutting-edge level and their seasoned, experienced seniors.

Stating that PM Narendra Modi had set the target of making the nation developed by 2047, Shah said the first condition for this would be making its internal security more robust.

Commending the state police forces, central agencies and the Central armed police forces (CAPFs) for having eliminated the challenge posed by three hotspots â J&K, Left-wing extremism-hit areas and the north-east â the home minister said that had the past governments visualised these problems before they became acute, the country would not have had to bear the brunt of them for decades.

Shah also described the dismantling of the Popular Front of India (PFI) network âin one nightâ (in multi-state raids of Sept 2022), apart from imposing a ban on it, as âan excellent instance of Centre-state coordinationâ.

The home minister emphasised on the need to take the countryâs first anti-terror doctrine â PRAHAAR â from document to practice, to âeradicate terrorism and dismantle the terror ecosystemâ. He said the govt has strengthened the anti-fugitive drive, having deported 274 fugitives from different countries between 2019 and 2026.

âAll the states should aim to bring the fugitives back to face the law here,â he stated.

Stating that global instability, lack of energy security, supply chain disruption and increasing radicalisation of cyber misinformation have emerged as the key challenges, Shah insisted that the security policy taken each of these into account and aim to effectively tackle them.

"Police of all states should implement the Narcotics Control Vision Document 2026-2029 on the ground to protect the new generation and work on three D's âdetect, disrupt and destroyâ for "a drug-free India,â he stated.

Shah also asked the officers to used the integrated data bank of CCTNS, ICJS, Natgrid and NAFIS to develop actionable intelligence through data integration, analysis and identification of modus operandi through AI, so that future challenges can be prevented.

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday approved a hike in salaries of Adarsh Schools' teachers taking their monthly pay from around Rs 10,000 to over Rs 22,000, officials said.According to an official release the decision will benefit around 1,100 teachers and reaffirms the state government's commitment that those shaping Punjab's future must themselves receive fair compensation, dignity and due recognition.Mann said his government will continue to safeguard the interests of teachers because strengthening the education system and securing the future of every student begins with empowering the teachers who build it.Chairing a meeting with a delegation of the teachers, Mann said successive governments neglected the teaching community despite their pivotal role in shaping the future of Punjab."Teachers are the backbone of our education system. For nearly two decades, these teachers have served with dedication despite receiving a meagre salary. Our government has decided to correct this long-standing injustice by increasing their salaries by more than 120 percent," he said.The CM said teachers would not only receive enhanced salaries but would also be extended facilities on the Kendriya Vidyalaya school pattern, providing them with improved service conditions.More than 15,000 students are currently studying in these CBSE-affiliated Adarsh Schools, and the state government remains fully committed to protecting the interests of both students and teachers, he said."When teachers feel secure and respected, students receive better education. Our priority is to safeguard the interests of teachers so that the future of every child studying in these schools remains secure," he added.Mann said every genuine demand of the Adarsh School teachers had been addressed after years of neglect under previous governments."Our government is committed to the welfare of every section of society. We have accepted the legitimate demands of these teachers and will continue ensuring they can discharge their responsibilities in a smooth and hassle-free manner," he added.

World.title: EU approvals, easier sterilisation rules to speed device access
World.content:
Faster access to some newer medical devices. (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Patients in India could get faster access to some newer medical devices already approved in the European Union, with the government expanding its list of trusted foreign regulatory jurisdictions while also easing licensing requirements for manufacturers outsourcing sterilisation.The Health Ministry has amended the Medical Devices Rules, 2017 to include the European Union among jurisdictions recognised for waiver of clinical investigation requirements for eligible medical devices that do not have a predicate device in India. The list earlier included the US, UK, Australia, Canada and Japan.The change means eligible devices that have already received regulatory approval in the EU can potentially avoid a fresh clinical investigation in India, reducing the time and regulatory steps required before they can be made available to patients. The waiver remains subject to the conditions prescribed under the rules.The government said the move would reduce regulatory timelines for manufacturers and importers and facilitate faster availability of advanced medical technologies in India. The addition of the EU also brings Indiaâs medical-device regulatory framework closer to international regulatory practices.Separately, manufacturers outsourcing sterilisation to a facility with a valid licence will no longer need a separate loan licence, reducing paperwork, compliance costs and delays.However, they will still have to print the sterilisation facilityâs licence number on the device label, with six months to comply. The labelling requirement had drawn industry concerns over added compliance burden and possible export delays.The government has also introduced a standard fee schedule for testing and evaluation of medical devices. The new charges include Rs 5,000 for implantation tests, Rs 2,000 for sterility testing, Rs 1,000 for syringes and needles and Rs 3,000 for surgical sutures. Testing fees for condoms and intrauterine devices have been fixed at Rs 2,500 each.For tests not specified in the schedule, the charges will be decided by the concerned laboratory or medical device testing officer. The prescribed fees will automatically rise by 5% annually.The three changes are aimed at cutting regulatory duplication, making compliance costs more predictable and speeding up access to medical devices while retaining requirements for quality, safety and traceability. The sterilisation and testing-fee amendments were notified as the Medical Devices (Second Amendment) Rules, 2026.

World.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani opposes RSS chief Bhagwat's Madison Square event
World.content:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) said he does not support the planned event at Madison Square Garden where Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will address members of the Indian diaspora.

However, he said the city may not have jurisdiction to cancel the “private" event, which is scheduled for August 29.

Mr. Bhagwat arrived in the U.S. earlier in the day as part of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's (RSS) centenary-year global outreach programme. During his stay in New York, he would participate in the Universal Oneness programme and address a gathering of around 5,000 people at the iconic Madison Square Garden (MSG) on Saturday (August 29, 2026).

"I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” Mr. Mamdani said at a news conference in New York.

The Indian-origin mayor was responding to a question on RSS, the planned event at MSG and the protests against the event.

He was asked whether the “rally” at MSG should be cancelled.

“I also stand here as the first Indian-American Mayor in our city's history, and my mother's family is all still in India," Mr. Mamdani said.

He said the vision of India that he was taught by his family and the one that he grew up being very familiar with was that of "a pluralistic society, of a secular republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India".

“And it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision of any country, frankly, and so it is one that I find myself in deep opposition to, not only as an Indian-American but also as the Mayor of a city that believes deeply in the belonging of each and every person, no matter their colour, their creed, their religion, their faith, wherever they're from,” Mr. Mamdani said.

Several interfaith and civil rights organisations held a press conference outside New York City Hall, the seat of the city government, opposing Mr. Bhagwat's appearance at MSG and urged the iconic venue to cancel the event.

The organisations included Hindus for Human Rights, Indian American Muslim Council and Interfaith Centre of New York, among others.

The Universal Oneness Celebration, organised by AHEAD Forum, which is hosting Mr. Bhagwat, said in a social media post that the RSS chief will attend the Universal Oneness Celebration in New York on August 29.

“The event carries a timeless and universal message: 'The world is one family'. It calls upon us to look beyond artificial divisions and differences, recognise the bonds that unite humanity, and embrace a spirit of mutual respect, harmony, and oneness,” the post said.

Mr. Bhagwat is visiting the U.S., Canada and the U.K. as part of the Sangh’s centenary-year global outreach programme.

World.title: Several injured as police stop Bihar students’ protest march
World.content:
A protest by students in Patna turned violent on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) when police used batons and water cannons to stop them from marching to the Bihar Chief Minister’s residence.

Protesting in Patna since August 18, the students have made various demands, including changes to the format of the Teacher Recruitment Examination (TRE), which is currently held in two rounds - preliminary and main. The students are demanding that the test be held in a single phase without negative marks. Other demands include transparency in all competitive examinations, end to alleged discrimination against Hindi-speaking candidates in exams held by the Bihar Public Service Commission (BPSC), and a high-level independent inquiry into previous exam controversies.

On Tuesday (August 25, 2026), hundreds of students gathered at J.P. Golambar near Gandhi Maidan to start the march toward Lok Sevak Awas, the official residence of the Chief Minister. The protesters, backed by the Students’ Federation of India (SFI), All India Students’ Association (AISA) and other student organisations, broke through the police barricades at Dak Bungalow Chowk at the heart of the city, leading to clashes with the police.

Several students as well as police personnel were injured in the scuffle, including a Deputy Superintendent of Police who suffered severe injuries in the stone-pelting by the protesters. A few girl students fainted. Due to the protest and the road blockade, vehicular movement was severely affected, leaving motorists stuck for hours. Many protesters were also detained by the police.

The escalation of the protests also came in the wake of controversial remarks made by BPSC Examination Controller Rajesh Kumar Singh on Monday (August 24, 2026) while addressing a press conference in Patna. To a question regarding the protests by students, Mr. Singh had quoted the Hindi proverb “Hathi chale bazaar, kutta bhaunke hazar” (focused people should ignore irrelevant criticisms). Many students had assumed that Mr. Singh had referred to protesters as “dogs”. Mr. Singh had since expressed regret, saying he had no intention to hurt anyone’s feelings and that he was quoted out of context.

On Monday (August 23, 2026), Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav met the protesting students at the venue and urged the government not to ignore voices of the protesting youth but to establish a positive dialogue with them.

“I demand that immediate and necessary steps be taken in this matter, prioritising the future of lakhs of students and youth in Bihar; otherwise, the united strength of the students and youth will compel the government to do so,” Mr. Yadav had said.

To resolve the problems of students, Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary had launched the ‘Vidyarthi Sahyog’ portal to convey students’ issues and suggestions directly to the government. Student support camps will also be organised to address students’ grievances on the fourth Tuesday of every month, the government said.

On August 18, the Bihar government issued the notification for 32,388 teaching posts to be filled by the TRE.

The students in the State are also demanding that fair decisions be taken regarding filling up vacant posts for Assistant Professor, relaxation in age limits and 100% domicile-based recruitment in government jobs and teacher appointment, and job security for guest Assistant Professors. They are also pressing for dates for all pending examinations and the issuance of an annual examination calendar covering all exams be made mandatory.

World.title: Allahabad High Court orders relocation of Hathras victim’s family to Ghaziabad or Noida within three months
World.content:
The Allahabad High Court on Monday directed the Uttar Pradesh government to rehabilitate and relocate the family of the Hathras gang rape and murder victim to Ghaziabad or Noida within three months, after finding “unnecessary resistance” on the State’s part in complying with its earlier directions.

A Bench of Justices Rajan Roy and Jaspreet Singh observed that the State’s February 22, 2025 decision offering to rehabilitate the family in Kasganj, Etah or Aligarh did not consider its request for relocation to Ghaziabad or Noida and was, therefore, “no decision in the eyes of law”.

Such orders, the Bench said, lent credence to the family’s assertion that the State was treating the matter as “adversarial litigation” and was adamant about not granting it statutory benefits under the court’s orders. “We, therefore, see no reason to grant any further time to the State for reconsideration of the matter,” it said.

The court directed the Additional Chief Secretary (Home) to file a compliance affidavit. In case of non-compliance, he will have to appear before the court in person on November 30.

The Bench noted that despite an earlier direction to consider the family’s request for relocation to Ghaziabad or Noida, the State’s subsequent decision did not even mention the request.

Speaking to The Hindu, the victim’s elder brother said the judiciary had been providing them succour, but the government was delaying the relief. “It has been almost six years, but our life has not come back on track. As the districts offered by the government are adjoining or close to Hathras, we wanted to be rehabilitated to Delhi-NCR for safety,” he said.

The 19-year-old woman was allegedly raped by four men from her village in September 2020 and died at a Delhi hospital a fortnight later.

World.title: Gang steals nine lakh from ATM near Somangalam
World.content:
Unidentified men broke open an ATM of a private bank and stole ₹9 lakh at Puthupper near Somangalam in the early hours of Monday.

The ATM is located in a commercial complex on the Somangalam – Padappai road. According to the police, the gang entered the ATM centre around 4 a.m. and used a crowbar and gas-cutting equipment to break open the machine and fled with the cash.

The police said the suspects had disconnected the alarm system and surveillance camera wires before carrying out the robbery.

All the shops in the commercial complex were closed when the robbery took place. The police have formed a special team to identify the suspects and arrest them.

World.title: Delhi Health Minister reviews H1N1 preparedness as count grows
World.content:
Delhi Health Minister Pankaj Kumar Singh on Tuesday chaired a review meeting to assess preparations for seasonal influenza, including H1N1, currently the predominant influenza subtype in the city.

Mr. Singh directed officials from the Health Department, Municipal Corporation of Delhi, New Delhi Municipal Council, and Delhi Cantonment Board to ensure adequate medical supplies, including medicines and testing facilities, while intensifying surveillance mechanisms and awareness drives on prevention.

The Capital has recorded 2,308 H1N1 cases so far, as per the Minister’s office. On August 21, the number stood at 1,777.

“I want to reassure the people of Delhi that there is no need for panic. Our health infrastructure is fully prepared and we are continuously monitoring the situation. At the same time, we cannot be complacent. I have directed all agencies concerned to intensify drives on preventive measures,” the Minister said.

Mr. Singh added that the density and connectivity in urban spaces can contribute to the spread of respiratory infections, making timely awareness and preventive action particularly important.

He called for coordinated campaigns involving the Transport Department, Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, and civic bodies.

Meanwhile, the Directorate of Education issued a circular asking all government and private schools to adopt a ‘Healthy School-Healthy Community’ approach and reinforce respiratory hygiene and other preventive practices.

“There is no need for panic. Seasonal illnesses, including influenza, are seen during this period of the year. Our focus is on preparedness, awareness, and timely preventive action,” Education Minister Ashish Sood said.

‘No ICU cases yet’

Dedicated H1N1 wards have been set up at several government hospitals in the city. Dr. Ramesh Chand Meena, Associate Professor (Department of Medicine) at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, said, “We have dedicated beds [for H1N1 cases] and a dedicated section in the ICU. No patients have been admitted to the ICU so far.”

He added that while most healthy adults are recovering well, complications have been reported among the vulnerable sections such as the elderly, children, pregnant women, and those with existing respiratory issues.

World.title: KPSC chairman suspended for second time by Governor
World.content:
After the Karnataka Cabinet decided to recommend the suspension of Karnataka Public Service Commission Chairman Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar, who is embroiled in controversy in recruitments, Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot on Tuesday suspended the Chairman again.

This is the second time that the Governor has suspended the KPSC Chairman. The order cites provisions of Article 317 (2) of the Constitution, and the High Court of Karnataka’s order of August 18. The Governor has directed the senior-most member of the KPSC to act as the Chairman until further orders. Currently, B. Prabhudev is the senior-most member of the KPSC.

Before Cabinet

Earlier, on July 10, Mr. Sahukar was suspended by the Governor over submission of false income certificate by one of his two daughters, who claimed the annual income to be ₹40,000, while applying for the post of Industrial Extension Officer. However, the Cabinet’s approval for suspension had come later.

Mr. Sahukar had challenged the Governor’s order that was taken without the aid and advice of the Cabinet in the High Court, which quashed the Governor’s order and directed Mr. Sahukar’s reinstatement. Meanwhile, the Karnataka Cabinet on Friday cleared the suspension, and recommended to the Governor to suspend the Chairman.

Amid ED raids

The order also comes at a time when the Enforcement Directorate has taken up the investigation of bribe and corruption in the recruitment of Veterinary Officers and has already searched over 20 premises, including the KPSC, residence of Mr. Sahukar and IAS officer and former Controller of Examination in KPSC Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, several middlemen among many others.

World.title: Man held on charge of assaulting mother for quarrelling with his wife in Maduravoyal
World.content:
A 31-year-old man was arrested for assaulting his 70-year-old mother following a quarrel between her and his wife at Maduravoyal on Sunday night.

The accused, Karthik, a resident of Cholan Nagar, attacked his mother Kanniyammal, 70, after she questioned his wife over talking to women from the neighbourhood outside their house. According to the police, the incident occurred on August 23.

A verbal altercation broke out between Kanniyammal and her daughter-in-law. Hearing the commotion, Karthik intervened and assaulted his mother. Kanniyammal, who sustained injuries, was treated at a private hospital. Based on her complaint, the Maduravoyal police registered a case and arrested Karthik, 31. The police said he already had two criminal cases against him.

He was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.

World.title: SIR in Karnataka: Chief Minister seeks more time for SIR claims, verification
World.content:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has urged the Election Commission of India to extend the time available for submitting claims and objections and verification of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka.

In a letter to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Mr. Shivakumar said the scale of names placed under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others (ASDDO) categories and those facing verification over “logical discrepancies” warranted adequate time and a proper verification process.

According to the letter, nearly 1.08 crore of Karnataka’s 5.54 crore electors have been placed in the ASDDO category. Following publication of the draft rolls on August 24, around 43.8 lakh electors are expected to receive notices over “logical discrepancies” or the absence of a link to the 2002 electoral roll.

‘Mobility should not mean disenfranchisement’

Mr. Shivakumar said a significant number of voters categorised as “Absent” could be genuine electors who were away from home when Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visited them, including for work, health or other reasons.

Similarly, voters who had shifted to another polling station were not given an opportunity to submit enumeration forms at their new addresses during the house-to-house exercise, he said.

“In Bengaluru and other cities, even moving across the street can mean a change of polling station,” the Chief Minister said, pointing out that such voters would now have to file Form 6 for inclusion in the rolls.

He expressed concern that voters categorised as Absent or Shifted would not receive the notices being issued to those facing “logical discrepancies” and “unmapped” status, and could therefore remain unaware that their names had been deleted.

“Mobility should not translate into disenfranchisement,” Mr. Shivakumar said.

Longer verification period

The Chief Minister sought an extension of the claims and objections period so that voters whose names are missing from the draft rolls, including those in the ASDDO categories, have sufficient time to ascertain their status and file claims.

He referred to the 2023 Manual of Electoral Roll and said the prescribed period could be extended by the Election Commission through a notification.

Mr. Shivakumar also sought a minimum of three to four weeks for voters facing verification over “logical discrepancies” or lack of a link to the 2002 roll to respond and produce documents.

He said the proposed process, involving notices and disposal of cases within about 45 days, could put an unreasonable burden on working people, migrants and the elderly, particularly when documents need to be obtained or voters have to travel.

Ward meetings, Gram Sabhas sought

The Chief Minister also urged the CEO to specifically direct District Election Officers to convene Ward Committee meetings in urban areas and Gram Sabhas in rural areas, with adequate advance publicity.

He said the draft rolls should be read out at these meetings so that omissions and errors could be identified and corrected.

While referring to the CEO’s August 20 communication on the provision, Mr. Shivakumar said merely referring to the procedure without specifically directing the meetings could result in it becoming a “pro forma compliance” rather than an effective mechanism for detecting errors.

More officials sought

The Chief Minister also sought an increase in the number of Additional Electoral Registration Officers and District Election Officers in districts with a high number of ASDDO cases and “logical discrepancies”.

He said the large number of objections and applications expected during the claims process, combined with the limited time available, could place an enormous workload on the existing machinery.

The State government, he said, was ready to provide assistance, including mobilising local administration for Gram Sabha and Ward Committee meetings, undertaking publicity campaigns and providing logistical support.

“The objective must be an electoral roll that the people of Karnataka can trust,” he added.

World.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs1.12, high-speed diesel by Rs1.11
World.content:
The government on Tuesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.12 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.11 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs343.10 per litre while HSD will cost Rs371.80 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to a Petroleum Division notification, the new prices will be applicable on Aug 26 and 27.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Imran's hospital transfer: SC to take up Dr Uzma's contempt plea on Sept 16
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court will take up on Sept 16 a contempt of court petition filed by Dr Uzma Khan against the government for allegedly violating its Aug 18 directions to transfer incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad.

The same three-member bench, comprising Justice Shahid Waheed, Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, which issued the Aug 18 order, will hear the contempt plea filed by Imran’s sister.

On Sept 16, the bench was also scheduled to resume hearing the pending cases concerning the former premier’s health and issues related to family meetings.

However, it is not clear whether the same bench will also take up the review petition filed by the Islamabad chief commissioner, challenging the court’s directions to shift PTI founder Imran Khan to a private hospital.

An informed source told Dawn that early fixation of the case was not possible because 94 criminal original petitions of the same category were pending before different SC benches.

Under the fixation policy, cases are required to be fixed for hearing in their turn within the relevant category. It is therefore unlikely that the contempt case will come up before Sept 16, the source said.

However, since the main case concerning Imran’s health is pending for hearing on Sept 16, the contempt petition is also expected to be taken up on the same date, the source added.

Earlier in the day, the PTI resubmitted the contempt of court petition by PTI founder sister to the SC’s registrar against the alleged violation of its Aug 18 order.

Later, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan also filed an application for the early hearing of the contempt petition.

The contempt plea was re-submitted shortly after the SC returned it after raising certain objections.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said that the SC registrar had informed him that the petition was being returned, with one of the objections being that the list of charges levelled against the respondents had not been dispatched. He had also said that the PTI was going to resubmit the petition after removing the objections raised.

Last week, Imran’s sister Uzma Khan had filed a petition before the SC against the authorities for violating the court’s Aug 18 order. In its order, the court had ordered the government to shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital, a private facility, within two days for examination and treatment by a multidisciplinary medical board.

However, the government instead took the PTI founder to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), a government hospital, for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside” the hospital for the diversion.

In her petition, Uzma — who was present for the check-up — had named Islamabad Chief Commissioner (retired) Lieutenant Sohail Ashraf, Interior Secretary Ahmed Raza Sarwar, Punjab Inspector General Prisons Mian Salik Jalal, Adiala Jail Superintendent Sajid Baig, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar as respondents.

She had alleged that the respondents had committed wilful, deliberate and contumacious disobedience and violation of the order. She had also requested the apex court to depute an officer or appoint a local commission to ensure that Imran was immediately shifted to the private hospital in accordance with its earlier directions.

At the same time, the Islamabad chief commissioner had also approached the SC, seeking an early hearing of his review petition, in which the legality of the Aug 18 order was questioned.

On Monday, Gohar had met the SC registrar and was assured that a bench would be constituted soon to proceed with the contempt of court petition.

Responding to a question, he had also brushed aside the impression of any deal with the government, saying that the PTI founder did not make deals, otherwise he would not have spent three years in prison.

Early hearing plea

In her plea for an early hearing, Uzma highlighted that the matter at hand concerned the life, health, dignity and physical well-being of Imran, whose health was “deteriorating and whose life is stated to be in jeopardy”.

“Every further delay may cause serious and irreparable harm,” the application said.

The application stated that the Aug 18 court order was required to be obeyed forthwith and in letter and spirit.

“The filing or pendency of any review petition on part of the chief commissioner does not, by itself, suspend or dilute the binding force of the order unless its operation is expressly stayed by the Supreme Court,” the petition said.

It added that respondents named in the contempt plea were legally required to act strictly in accordance with the directions of the Supreme Court.

“If any genuine clarification or modification was considered necessary, the proper course was to approach the Supreme Court, rather than to depart from or substitute its express directions,” it argued.

The applicant also expressed regret that “disobedience” by the respondents was “continuing in nature” and emphasised that this required “immediate judicial consideration so that the authority of the Supreme Court was upheld and its directions concerning the life and health of the prisoner were implemented without further loss of time”.

“The applicant has a strong prima facie case and the balance of convenience lies entirely in favour of early fixation,” the application said, arguing that no prejudice would be caused to the respondents if the matter was heard at the earliest.

However, it added, a delay may cause “irreparable loss and injury”.

The application also cited media reports and recalled that the chief commissioner, in his review petition, had also prayed for an early hearing of his plea.

World.title: Govt forms high-powered body to break deadlock over Iran-Pakistan gas pipeline amid penalty threats
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: With millions of dollars in potential penalties looming, the government has constituted a high-powered committee to find a “mutually acceptable” way out of the decades-old impasse over the Pakistan-Iran gas pipeline, as it weighs the cost of penalties against the country’s growing energy needs.

Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik told the Senate on Tuesday that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had set up the committee to examine the project’s legal, financial and energy dimensions and recommend a way forward “in Pakistan’s national interest”.

Raising an attention notice, Senator Talha Mahmood noted that the project had been delayed for two decades and that Iran had already laid the pipeline up to the Pakistani border. He asked whether Pakistan was ready to receive Iranian gas once sanctions were lifted and how much work had been completed on its side of the pipeline.

“Can Pakistan immediately integrate Iranian gas into its system? How long will it take to make the pipeline operational after sanctions are lifted? What preparations has Pakistan made to receive the gas?” he asked.

The senator further asked whether the infrastructure for transporting Iranian gas had been completed and what practical progress had been made on the project.

Malik said the matter had gone into arbitration in Paris under the Gas Sales Purchase Agreement signed between the two countries in 2009.

Under the agreement, Pakistan was to complete its 781km pipeline by December 2014. The deadline was later extended, but Islamabad could not begin construction on its territory due to US sanctions and a lack of financing. Iran completed its section years ago.

In 2023, Tehran served a formal notice seeking damages for the delay, with reports suggesting the claim could run into billions of dollars.

The dispute is now being heard by an international arbitration tribunal in Paris.

“The committee is looking at the potential liability facing Pakistan, the implications of litigation and the country’s future energy requirements,” the petroleum minister told the house. “These factors will help determine the way forward on the project.”

He added that the government wanted to avoid further complications from litigation and was therefore pursuing a negotiated settlement with Tehran.

“Iran is a brotherly country and the leadership of the two countries remains engaged in efforts to reach an amicable settlement acceptable to both sides,” the minister said.

Malik noted that Iran had already made “substantial physical progress” on its side of the pipeline, having brought gas from the South Pars field to a major city near the Pakistani border.

The petroleum minister also addressed concerns over gas supply problems in Balochistan. He said the prime minister had directed him to engage with provincial stakeholders.

He informed the house that another high-level committee, headed by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, was examining Balochistan’s gas-related problems, including technical faults and payment issues.

In May 2009, Pakistan and Iran signed an agreement for the supply of 750 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) of gas for 25 years from Iran’s South Pars gas field.

Both countries were required to implement the project in their respective territories. According to the agreement, the project was to start supply by January 2015.

World.title: Imran Khan’s sister Noreen Niazi meets him in Adiala jail for second consecutive week
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Former prime minister Imran Khan’s sister, Noreen Niazi, met him at Adiala jail on Tuesday for the second consecutive week, in line with the Supreme Court’s (SC) directions.

In response to Imran’s petition filed in May, the SC on August 18 ruled that meetings should be facilitated between the prisoner and his family members once a week. The court had also directed that the government would facilitate the prisoner in speaking to his sons by telephone twice a week.

Following the SC’s directions, Imran’s family reassured the court that they would not speak to the media.

According to PTI lawyer Awais Younas Chaudhry, Noreen’s meeting with Imran today lasted around 45 minutes.

“Earlier, Bushra Bibi’s family was allowed to meet her, and then it was conveyed that Noreen Niazi could meet Imran Khan,” Chaudhry told Dawn.

“The other two sisters were waiting in the vehicle. When Noreen Niazi came out of the jail, all the sisters left without speaking to the media,” he said.

Chaudhry said that PTI was following the guidelines and orders of the apex court.

Noreen had also met Imran last Tuesday, on August 18.

“We really appreciate the role of the Supreme Court as the meetings with PTI’s founding chairman have become possible only because of the court,” Chaudhry said.

He said he hoped the government would implement the court orders in full and shift Imran to Shifa International Hospital for medical treatment, where his personal physicians would be allowed to examine him.

However, the government instead took the PTI founder to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), a government hospital, for a check-up and then subsequently transported back to prison. At the time, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar had blamed “the security situation created by PTI workers on the way to and outside” the hospital for the diversion.

In October 2025, the Islamabad High Court directed the Adiala jail superintendent to implement a March 24 order that reinstated the twice-a-week meeting schedule for the PTI founder.

World.title: Pims says its CT machine 'remains functional' following reports of failure to conduct Imran's heart scan
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Following reports that jailed PTI founder Imran Khan could not undergo a heart scan during a visit to the hospital last week, the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) said on Tuesday that its CT machine “remains functional and continues to support diagnostic services”.

When Imran was brought to Pims last week for an eye procedure and other diagnostic examinations, doctors recommended a CT coronary angiography (CTA), but hospital staff reportedly said the facility was unavailable.

After undergoing other tests, he was subsequently shifted back to Adiala Jail without the CTA, which can help detect coronary blockages and assess the risk of a heart attack. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also took notice of the non-functional CTA facility at Pims and constituted an inquiry committee to determine the facts.

Sources had earlier told Dawn that the Cardiac Centre’s conventional angiography facility at Pims was different from a CTA. While conventional angiography involved inserting a catheter into a blood vessel, a CTA was performed using a CT scanner.

In the statement issued on Tuesday, the Pims administration said, “[The] CT machine, installed in 2022, remains functional and continues to support diagnostic services.”

It said that “imaging investigations are undertaken regularly on the basis of clinical assessment, specialist advice, patient-safety considerations and prescribed medical protocols”.

“The use of a particular imaging procedure should be viewed within its clinical context and should not be interpreted unnecessarily,” it said.

A senior doctor at Pims, who wished not to be named, told Dawn that around a dozen CTAs had been conducted before the statement was released.

After reports regarding the failure to conduct the test had emerged, the PTI had reiterated its demand to move Imran to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad without any delay — which the Supreme Court had also directed on August 18.

PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram also cited details submitted to the court, saying a medical board constituted by the government had examined Imran on August 10 while a Pims cardiologist had already recommended the test for him on August 1 due to fluctuating blood pressure, palpitations, headaches, restlessness and the potential risk of cardiac complications arising from his age and prolonged isolation.

“Even the government’s own doctors considered this diagnostic test necessary,” he said.

“Yet, when Imran was taken to Pims, the procedure was not performed. Hospital officials claimed that the required facility was unavailable, despite the presence of a functional CT scanner in the radiology department capable of conducting the test,” he alleged.

World.title: Opposition, govt spar in Senate over Imran Khan’s medical treatment
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The opposition and the government on Tuesday sparred in the Senate over the treatment of PTI founder and former premier Imran Khan in hospital, with both sides accusing each other of contempt of a Supreme Court (SC) order.

On August 18, the apex court ordered the government to shift the PTI founder to the Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad and to constitute a medical board, including his sister and personal physician.

However, instead of shifting Imran to the Shifa Hospital, the government took him to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), citing security concerns and shifted him back to the Adiala jail after the medical board declared him medically fit. The PTI and Imran’s family have been accusing the government of not implementing the SC’s order of shifting him to Shifa Hospital.

The heated argument broke out on Tuesday after presiding officer Shahadat Awan disallowed the opposition from moving a resolution concerning the implementation of the SC’s order regarding Imran’s medical treatment at Shifa International Hospital, but allowed discussion on points of order.

The opposition slammed the government for what it called “throwing the binding orders of the SC in the dustbin”, while the government insisted that it was for the court to determine whether the verdict had been implemented.

The session, chaired by PPP Senator Shahadat Awan, ruled that the matter was sub judice and could only be raised through a point of order, not a resolution.

PTI parliamentary leader Barrister Ali Zafar, who sought to move a resolution, said the Senate must uphold the “supremacy of the Constitution” and reaffirm its commitment to implementing SC orders.

Speaking on the floor of the house, Zafar cited the SC’s Aug 18 order directing the authorities to take Imran to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and constitute a medical board.

“Neither was he taken to Shifa Hospital nor was a board constituted. Even a machine to check his heart was not available at Pims,” Zafar alleged.

“Can any government refuse to implement a Supreme Court order? No, it cannot,” he said, referring to Articles 190 and 204 of the Constitution, which make compliance with court orders binding and non-compliance contempt of court.

“You may oppose Imran Khan’s politics. Do that. But do not play politics with his health,” he added. “Governments come and go, but the Constitution remains.”

PTI Senator Azam Swati accused the government of double standards. “When someone has to be given a benefit, relief is provided in judicial matters. Institutions were sent to Islamabad airport to give relief to Nawaz Sharif,” he said.

Responding on behalf of the government, Adviser to the Prime Minister Rana Sanaullah said the state was “subject to the Constitution” and had complied with the SC order.

“The court also said security arrangements would be assessed by the administration. Given the law and order situation, he was taken to a government hospital where qualified doctors were available,” he said.

Sanaullah said a doctors’ panel had examined the PTI founder and declared his health “satisfactory”, after which he was sent back to jail.

“The matter is before the court. The report will be submitted on Sept 16. Let the court examine it and decide whether the order was implemented.”

He questioned why the opposition was “determined to prove him ill” when his own doctors and family had said he was in good health. “Do not do politics on health. If you are telling us not to, then you should also refrain,” he said.

Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas called on the government to show “magnanimity” and implement the court order “in letter and spirit”. He proposed that a Senate committee be formed to visit the jail.

“Politics and politicians are being crushed. Who will run the country then? It is not too late. There is no benefit in contempt of court,” he said.

World.title: Speaker, deputy speaker take oath after election to AJK Assembly
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: Chaudhary Tariq Farooq of the PML-N was elected the 16th speaker of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Legislative Assembly, while party colleague Muhammad Ahmed Raza Qadri was elected deputy speaker, in elections to both offices held on Tuesday.

The session started at 2:30pm, with outgoing Speaker Chaudhry Latif Akbar of the PPP in the chair. Akbar could not retain his seat in the recent general elections.

The PPP had fielded Chaudhry Qasim Majeed and Aamir Abdul Ghaffar Lone for the two offices.

All 46 legislators — 32 from the PML-N and its ally and 14 from the PPP — who had taken oath on Monday participated in the polling.

Farooq, elected from LA-7 (Bhimber City), secured 32 votes, while Majeed, elected from LA-2 (Chakswari), received 13 votes, with one PPP vote being rejected.

The rejected vote was reportedly cast by PPP lawmaker Zobia Khurshid Raja, who was elected to a women’s reserved seat through a draw of lots after her votes had equalled those of PML-N candidate Riffat Abid.

After Majeed and some other PPP lawmakers pointed out that Raja’s vote had been rejected, she reportedly told a colleague that she had marked a tick rather than a cross on the ballot paper.

Farooq was then administered the oath by his predecessor.

PML-N leader Raja Farooq Haider, whose camaraderie with Akbar is well known, paid rich tribute to him for running the House smoothly. He highlighted that he and Akbar were the last members of the outgoing Assembly who had also been elected in 1985, following the restoration of democracy in AJK and Pakistan.

PPP regional president Chaudhry Muhammad Yasin also paid what he described as a “big tribute” to Akbar, praising his unflinching commitment to the PPP and democracy.

Farooq later conducted the election for deputy speaker, which was won by Qadri with 32 votes. Interestingly, Lone also secured 13 votes, with one PPP vote being rejected again, prompting speculation within the party about whether the rejection was deliberate rather than accidental.

Farooq then administered the oath to Qadri as deputy speaker.

Both Qadri and Lone belong to Kashmiri refugee constituencies — the former from Rawalpindi and the latter from Karachi.

The PML-N had reportedly earlier decided to field Raja Asif of LA-11 (Sehnsa) for the slot, but he declined the offer. The PPP had initially nominated Zaffar Iqbal Malik of LA-8 (Raj Mahal) before changing its decision and fielding Lone.

Members from both sides made brief speeches congratulating Farooq on his election and expressing good wishes. Alongside Haider, among those who spoke were PML-N president Shah Ghulam Qadir, Syed Shoukat Shah, Sehrish Qamar, Pir Mazhar Saeed and Qadri. PPP members also spoke, including Yasin, Majeed, outgoing prime minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, Abdul Majid Khan, Mian Abdul Waheed and Deevan Ali Chughtai.

They expressed the hope that the new speaker would ensure impartiality in conducting the proceedings and provide adequate space to both the treasury and opposition benches to voice their concerns.

Former law minister Mian Abdul Waheed said Farooq had earned the office through his political struggle, hard work and contribution to the parliamentary system.

“You got this office on merit, owing to your political struggle, hard work and valuable contribution to the system. I congratulate your party for elevating you to this office,” he said.

Farooq, a Bhimber resident who defeated former prime minister Chaudhry Anwarul Haq by a margin of more than 12,000 votes, is the PML-N’s regional secretary general. He is regarded as a well-versed and articulate politician who regularly engages with party workers and the wider public through social media platforms.

He also has close connections with the Kashmiri diaspora in the UK and Europe. Several prominent members of the diaspora, including Ateeque-ur-Rehman, a former mayor of Oldham, travelled to AJK to attend his swearing-in ceremony.

His election and oath-taking were witnessed from the visitors’ gallery by all three of his wives and his children.

Speaking at the conclusion of the session, Farooq thanked members from both sides and said the office demanded impartiality.

“In a democratic society, the role of the opposition is very important. To me, all members carry equal importance regardless of their affiliations, and I will ensure they get maximum possible opportunity to voice the sentiments of their electorate and problems of their constituencies concerned,” he said.

“I will leave no stone unturned to maintain the dignity, honour and sanctity of this House,” he vowed.

Since the office of the AJK president has remained vacant since January, Farooq will also serve as acting president, as did his predecessor, until the election of a new president.

Meanwhile, the schedule for the election of the leader of the House was also issued on Tuesday. According to the schedule, nomination papers will be submitted and scrutinised on Thursday, followed by polling the same day.

The newly elected leader of the House will take oath before the acting president at the High Court ground on Thursday afternoon.

World.title: Apple launches faster Mac mini, Mac Studio to tap AI boom
World.content:
Apple on Tuesday unveiled a more powerful Mac mini aimed at consumers looking to host AI agents remotely, marking what is likely the final product launch of Tim Cook’s tenure as CEO.

The new mini, unveiled alongside a beefed-up Mac Studio, starts at $899 and comes with either Apple’s new M6 chip or the M5 Pro. It is $100 more expensive than its predecessor.

Both devices have become popular with consumers looking to run autonomous AI agents such as OpenClaw locally, with high demand depleting inventories at several Apple stores.

“Whether it’s being used as a home computer, powering a professional studio, or as an always-on agentic device, it’s the little Mac that can do it all,” the company’s hardware boss Johny Srouji said.

The unveiling is likely Apple’s last major launch before Tim Cook hands over the reins to hardware veteran John Ternus in one of its most closely watched leadership transitions. It also highlights mounting cost pressures as memory chip prices climb on strong demand from AI data centres, which prompted Apple to raise prices on some Mac and iPad models in June.

One variant of the new mini is powered by Apple’s 2-nanometer M6 chip, which the company said delivers up to four times faster AI performance and double the graphics and storage speeds compared with the previous M4-powered model.

The higher-end variant, powered by its M5 Pro chip, offers up to an 18-core central processor and 20-core graphics processor, targeting professional users working on tasks such as visual effects.
