World.title: The Dunedin clinic helping wean patients off antidepressants
World.content: Between 2019 and 2023, the number of New Zealanders on antidepressants grew by 15 percent from about 537,000 to just under 619,000, according to data from Pharmac. It is unclear what the average time is for a New Zealander to take antidepressants. In Australia, patients on average take the medication for about four years. However, clinical guidelines only support taking them for six to 12 months for “a single episode of major depression”, says Professor Katharine Wallis, a former New Zealand GP who is now at the University of Queensland. She helped develop the RELEASE guidelines, a resource for the public and doctors on safe deprescribing.

World.title: Pacific Games Council seeks legal advice after Solomon Islands court ruling
World.content:
The Pacific Games Council (PGC) says it will seek legal advice on the next steps after a court ruling that the Solomon Islands National Hosting Authority (NHA) had breached public finance rules while hosting the 2023 Pacific Games in Honiara.

PGC chief executive Andrew Minogue confirmed on Monday that the council had received notification of the High Court ruling after the Solomon Islands' Auditor-General's Office filed a case seeking clarification.

The ruling follows a dispute between the PGC and the NHA last year over which laws applied to the expenditure of public funds from the Sports Solomons Fund.

"To date, the Pacific Games Council has supported the position of the National Hosting Authority that the 2023 Pacific Games Act, passed by the Solomon Islands Parliament in 2017, in consultation with Council, deliberately contained clauses to streamline the procurement process for the Games, and that these provisions should guide the post-Games audit process," Minogue said in response to questions raised with them if they were aware of the court ruling," he said.

"The PGC will consider the next steps in the legal process."

The High Court ruled that the NHA breached provisions of the Public Financial Management Act (PFMA) 2013 governing the expenditure of public funds.

The court's clarification was sought after the Auditor-General's office pointed out that because the funds earmarked for the Games were public funds, the PFMA 2013 was applicable in how the funds were being appropriated, expended and managed.

However, this was not accepted by the NHA, led by Dr Jimmy Rodgers, who said the funds were subject to the Pacific Games Act, and appropriated by the Parliament Development Budget of the Office of the Prime Minister and Cabinet (OPMC).

But the High Court has ruled that while the Development Budget of the OPMC for 2019 to 2024 were validly appropriated in parliament for the purpose of the Pacific Games, how it was spent from the Sports Solomons Fund did not comply with sections 25, 57 and 60 of the PFMA 2013.

The ruling also stated that the Accountable Officer of NHA did not have the authority to expend funds from the Sports Solomons Funds for the Pacific Games 2023, including funds from the Advance Warrants made on 4 separate occasions. Expenditure approvals for the funds were without lawful authority.

The court also ruled that the Modification Policy (Resolution NHA 03-23-01) purported to authorise the Blanket Waiver of competitive tendering, were beyond the powers of NHA and so the Policy is null and void and that the expenditure made pursuant to the blanket waiver aspect of the modification policy was without lawful authority,

The ruling also clears the Auditor General's Office to complete its report and present that to Parliament, through the Speaker in accordance with section 108 (4) of the Constitution.

Auditor-General David Teika Dennis welcomed the High Court's ruling, and said they will now present the report to parliament, and added the report will also be given to the authorities for further investigation.

"I think it is really important that our audit reports into hosting one of the best ever Pacific Games 2023 have clear findings and learnings," he said.

"The ruling resolves the applicable legal framework governing the Sports Solomon Fund and how it should be expended and managed, and we very much welcome the rulings.

"In addition, this sets the precedence for the management and expenditure of all other special funds within Government Ministries and Agencies.

"The Court ruling makes it clear that Special Funds as public money, unless explicitly required otherwise by Parliament must comply with the Public Financial Management Act.

"It follows from this ruling that all accountable officers of special funds including for Sports Solomon Fund must have a valid warrant to be able to lawfully incur expenditure."

A number of serious weaknesses in procurement and financial management processes surrounding the Games were identified in the special audit report, done by KPMG Fiji.

Most contractors did not provide adequate financial information to support an assessment of their financial capacity, while contracts allowed between 30 and 50 percent of the contract value to be paid upon signing, before goods, services or works had been delivered.

One of the biggest cases identified in the report was the controversial procurement of toilet paper.

Dennis said the procurement for the supply and delivery of toilet paper initially involved a contract amount of SB$6.18 million (NZ$1.2m), despite being linked to an overall budget of only SB$300,000 (NZ$58,000).

The contract was later reduced to SB$1.89m (NZ$370,000), but the revised amount was still significantly above the available budget.

It was one of the five contracts for which competitive bidding was bypassed.

The audit includes detailed review of 16 procurement activities totalling $222.4m (US422.75m), selected from $502.16m (US$62.67m) in purchase orders.

"The Pacific Games were one of Solomon Islands' largest national events, requiring major investment in sporting venues, accommodation, transport, equipment, logistics and other infrastructure and services," Dennis told the media in Honiara.

World.title: Pedestrian dies after being hit by car in Auckland supermarket carpark
World.content:
A person has died in a crash at in a supermarket carpark on Auckland's North Shore.

Police were called to the intersection of Sunnynook Road and Sycamore Drive about 6.30pm, after the crash between a car and a pedestrian in a Woolworth's carpark.

Police said on Wednesday that despite best efforts the pedestrian died at the scene.

Woolworths Sunnynook said on Tuesday it was co-operating with emergency services at the scene.

It said its immediate focus was on supporting team members and their whānau.

World.title: Health system in intensive care and starting to flatline, experts say
World.content:
Experts and advocates discuss the health of our nation Morning Report Download MP3 3m

The health system is in intensive care and is starting to flatline.

That was the dire diagnosis delivered by a group of experts at a state of the health system address in Porirua on Monday night.

But the government says the public health workforce is growing, not shrinking.

Malcolm Mulholland from the advocacy group Patient Voice Aotearoa said this country now had a two tiered health system - one for the insured and one for the uninsured.

"The longer that this is allowed to continue, the worse it's going to become. Our big fear is that we're going to see more and more privatisation, so essential services that we would expect to be encountered as part of attending hospital or care in the community will be outsourced to a private provider."

Malcolm Mulholland. RNZ / Penny Smith

Doctor David Galler was a former intensive care specialist at Middlemore Hospital.

He said the underinvestment in New Zealand's health system was well documented - and it was driving away the workforce.

"We know that ongoing privatisation at the moment, and the setting of austerity and the setting of workforce shortages just simply weakens the public system. It removes more and more of the public workforce, who move into private as they become increasingly overwhelmed in the public sector," he said.

Doctor David Galler. RNZ / Penny Smith

The government said that outsourcing wasn't new - but it was doing it differently.

It said patients helped the most by outsourcing planned surgeries to private providers were those without insurance - who were on the public waitlist.

A spokesperson said there had also been record funding for general practice and a focus on growing that workforce.

General practitioner Lucy O'Hagan. RNZ / Penny Smith

General practitioner Lucy O'Hagan said the health workforce was suffering from a pandemic of burnout.

"The young GPs I teach, full of energy and enthusiasm, are choosing to do the job three days a week because the cognitive and emotional demand is so challenging. Older, passionate GPs are retiring early or reducing their hours simply to stay sane."

Others just weren't accessing healthcare.

The chair of the Tūwharetoa Iwi-Māori Partnership Board, Louisa Wall, said about a quarter of the Māori residents in her rohe were not enrolled with a GP.

"It means our people are waiting until it becomes extreme, that is, they're in so much pain it can't be ignored, before they choose to do something about it," she said.

Louisa Wall. RNZ / Penny Smith

A youth mental health advocate, Luca Zampese, said too many young people were struggling to get help when they needed it.

"New Zealand has been ranked last among comparable wealthy countries for child and youth mental well-being. UNICEF's latest international report also found that Aotearoa has the highest adolescent suicide rate among the countries studied, almost three times the average for high-income nations."

Youth mental health advocate Luca Zampese. RNZ / Penny Smith

The Minister for Mental Health Matt Doocey said a recent survey found more than a quarter of young people didn't know where to get help.

"Only 3.7 percent said they couldn't get an appointment. But, there are still barriers to break down, with 29.4 percent saying they did not know where to get help and more than 35 percent saying they were too embarrassed," he said.

Doocey said the government would start reporting how quickly young people were accessing mental health support.

Mental Health Minister Matt Doocey. RNZ / Mark Papalii

Among those at the meeting was long-time Cannons Creek resident Sandra Merediths.

She said that last year she waited in a lobby at Wellington Hospital for eight hours, before being seen by a nurse.

Her own assessment of the health system was blunt.

"It's bloody shocking. People can't get the service they need ... don't have enough good places where older people can be cared for when they have health issues. Services at home for some people that could live at home are limited," she said.

Long-time Cannons Creek resident Sandra Merediths. RNZ / Penny Smith

Also in the audience was a UK Doctor, who had been living and working in New Zealand for eight years.

Disillusioned by what he'd seen in this country, he was now considering returning to England - and his secondary career as a bus driver.

"Why would I stay around and watch another public health system be vandalised and destroyed in New Zealand, having seen that happen in the UK over the last three decades?"

Health Minister Simeon Brown. RNZ / Baz Macdonald

In a statement, the Health Minister Simeon Brown said that the health system was improving.

"More people are being treated, wait times for surgery are shorter, and patients are waiting less time in emergency departments. There is, however, much more work to do," he said.

World.title: New Caledonia’s President Tukumuli outlines a six-month recovery roadmap
World.content:
New Caledonia's President Milakulo Tukumuli on Monday outlined the urgent issues facing the French Pacific territory.

In a special address at New Caledonia's Congress, Tukumuli, who was elected president of the collegial multi-party government on 31 July following provincial elections, said he gave his government six months to tackle the most pressing issues facing New Caledonia.

After this, he said his government would start to focus on other issues.

He said there the most immediate urgencies included necessary efforts to salvage the French territory's pension and health insurance schemes, currently facing a short-term risk of total collapse.

He added, if nothing is done, over 40,000 New Caledonian pensioners could find themselves pensionless "within a few months".

New Caledonia's healthcare system was also under direct threat with a cumulated current deficit to the tune of US$420 million.

Another urgency was to examine the local political system's expenditures in order to reduce costs.

"The fall is now receding, but recovery has not started yet. When a canoe is taking water, it's not time to take stock of what is onboard. You begin by fixing the hull and restoring the course," he told local Congress members, as part of his general policy speech.

"I did not request this position just to manage impotency", he said, stressing that New Caledonia was still recovering from the damage caused by the 2024 civil unrest.

On the crucial nickel mining sector in New Caledonia, where most of the stakeholders and operators are still searching for new investors, Tukumuli said his government would support any "coherent" offer by "solid" and "durably engaged" stakeholders.

But he said New Caledonia's economy also needed to reduce its long-term dependency on nickel through other economic sectors such as tourism, agriculture, the blue economy or digital-based projects.

"Let's make sure that a future New Caledonia remembers us as those who have chosen to put it back on its feet".

He said economic recovery must include "social justice".

"These are the two sides of the same coin: wealth without justice does not hold. And justice without wealth cannot last", he told the Congress, saying one of his priorities was to bring New Caledonians a "dignified life".

New Caledonia’s President Milakulo Tukumuli delivers his general policy address at the Congress on 24 August 2026. Supplied / Gouvernement de la Nouvelle-Calédonie

Mending the multi-ethnic social fabric

Being the first New Caledonian government of Wallisian heritage, he also mentioned the need for all citizens of all ethnic heritages to "feel at home".

"Our country is made of all these components, the Kanak people, first inhabitants of New Caledonia. But also women and men who came from Europe, Tahiti, Wallis and Futuna, Asia, Vanuatu and elsewhere, and who, generation after generation, have also made this land theirs and know no other one".

"The events of May 2024 have reopened fractures that we knew were there, but preferred not to see".

He said New Caledonia's social cohesion cannot be dictated, but "is built also within our institutions, through the words we use and the way we speak to each other".

Reactions

Reactions from across the political chessboard were generally positive, including in the pro-independence ranks.

Pro-independence member for Kanaky-NC (mostly consisting of member of Union Calédonienne) Omaira Naisseline said the speech was "responsible", but that her political group remained "attentive".

On the pro-France side, Congress members (who have struck a coalition pact with Tukumuli's Eveil Océanien party), hailed Tukumuli's "truthful and responsible" roadmap.

"It's a make or break situation. We're up against a wall", Congress member for pro-France Les Loyalistes-Rassemblement told the media after the speech, saying his party would support Tukumuli's government reform efforts.

Congress President Virginie Ruffenach (pro-France) said the address was "very pragmatic" and "tough".

Bipartisan delegation in Paris next week

Tukumuli also confirmed he will lead a bipartisan delegation in Paris next week, with the main objective being to re-negotiate with the French government the terms of massive loans contracted in the past few years.

This included loans contracted a result of the Covid crisis, and later following the massive damages incurred during the May 2024 unrest, which resulted in 14 deaths, over €2.2 billion in material damages, thousands of jobless and a drop of some 13.5 percent in New Caledonia's Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Despite French assistance packages, New Caledonia was still short of over €100m just to finish the 2026 financial year.

The delegation (which will consist of Tukumuli, some of his government members, Congress members and New Caledonia's two MPs from the French National Assembly) mainly aims at convincing the French government to turn the massive loans into non-refundable grants.

"The loans have avoided total collapse, but they have also generated a debt course that we cannot sustain. Our debt has now reached a level New Caledonia has never seen before", Tukumuli said on Monday.

Speaking shortly after his election in July, he described the situation as a very real short-term risk of "shutdown".

"We're not asking for charity ... New Caledonia will not pass 2027 without fresh financial support from the French State", he said on Monday.

New Caledonia's Congress has to vote its 2027 budget before the end of 2026.

"This budget will have to be sincere and balanced. It will greatly depend on France's financial support. What we are proposing is a contract of responsibility with known amounts and reciprocal commitments. New Caledonia will pursue its reforms".

Even though the delegation's trip to Paris does not include further negotiations on New Caledonia's future political status, Tukumuli also called on politicians to remain mobilised in view of future institutional talks with France about the French territory's future political status.

"Uncertainty about tomorrow does not authorize us to remain motionless today".

World.title: 'This is a difficult task': PNG parliament to finally address Bougainville decision
World.content:
Papua New Guinea's prime minister has urged the nation to appreciate the gravity of the decision on Bougainville that parliament is to debate this week.

The PNG parliament resumed on Tuesday and from Thursday MPs will debate whether to ratify the 97.7 percent vote by Bougainvilleans for independence in their 2019 non-binding referendum.

PNG's national MPs have the final say, in adherence with the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement (BPA), which was signed following Bougainville's civil war and related crisis of the 1990s, and ultimately provided for the referendum.

"The Referendum was legitimate, peaceful and overwhelming in its result, and we respect the voice expressed by the people of Bougainville," Prime Minister James Marape said in a statement.

As the referendum result is finally to be tabled in parliament, Marape cautioned MPs and the public not to create division over the issue through threats, fear, regionalism or hostility.

"Every member of parliament will have the opportunity to speak. Every member will ultimately have to exercise his or her responsibility according to conscience, guided by the Constitution and the interests of our country."

'Not an ordinary debate'

"This is a difficult task but duty demands that we do this," Marape said, while also praying with other MPs for wisdom to guide their deliberations on the issue.

He said Papua New Guineans should appreciate the gravity of the matter because the decisions on Bougainville will have implications for future generations.

"This is not an ordinary parliamentary debate. It concerns our Constitution, our sovereignty, our national identity, the aspirations of the Bougainville people and, above all, the peace that our people have worked so hard to maintain."

It remains uncertain whether this week's debate will culminate in a vote on whether to ratify the refendum result as soon as the debate finishes, or whether it will be scheduled at a later point.

Earlier this year, the parliament set a three-quarter majority threshold requirement for ratification.

World.title: Crows captain makes tearful speech as All Australian team is named
World.content:
Max Gawn has claimed a record ninth All Australian blazer, while Nick Daicos was named player of the year by both the coaches and his fellow players, but a speech from Adelaide captain Jordan Dawson stole the show at the AFL Awards.

Dawson won Best Captain and Most Courageous Player, before being selected in and named vice captain of the All Australian team, and spoke openly about his mental health on stage.

Dawson's brother died at the age of 35 earlier this year, something he says he has struggled to deal with throughout the season.

"It's been a struggle. It's not easy. It's a range of emotions and they come at different times," Dawson said.

"For me it's about creating safe spaces in the footy club and at home, and understanding there will be times when it's hard to go to work and that it is OK to feel a certain type of way.

"It's still raw, it's always going to be hard to talk about. I'm so lucky I have such supportive people around me.

"The mental health space is something new to me, but something I want to learn more about.

"I want everyone to know who is struggling with their mental health that you are definitely loved and that the world is a better place with you in it. You are enough. We all love you, you have friends and family around you."

Nick Daicos was a multiple winner at the AFL Awards. (Getty Images: Michael Willson)

Gawn, who was named captain of the All Australian side, became the first man to earn nine blazers. Marcus Bontempelli earned selection for an eighth time.

Daicos, selected in the All Australian time for the fourth time in the first five years of his career, also swept the Coaches Association Champion Player of the Year and Leigh Matthews MVP awards.

Carlton's Jagga Smith was named the Rising Star for 2026.

World.title: Richmond denies players 'making light' of Swans scandal on Mad Monday
World.content:
The Richmond Football Club has denied its players were "referencing or making light of recent matters" in footage recorded during their post-season celebrations.

Tiger players were recorded during a drinking session at a Victorian country pub, with one player seen feigning shock after being spanked on his rear by a teammate.

Another teammate whips a fellow player on the back with a belt in footage captured by news outlets yesterday, leading to speculation they were referencing the ongoing Sydney Swans scandal.

The club denied that was the case.

"Richmond is aware of a video circulating from a player end-of-season gathering," a statement read.

"The club has spoken to the players who have expressed their embarrassment over their behaviour.

"The players are adamant they were in no way referencing or making light of recent matters."

Swans will not be invited to Brownlow ceremony AFL boss Andrew Dillon speaks to the media about the Sydney Swans scandal, saying "the actions of a few don't define the actions of the entire industry".

The Tigers finished second last this season with a 3-20 win-loss record.

The pub that hosted Richmond's drinks said the controversy had been blown out of proportion.

"In our view, this has been blown out of proportion," the Garfield Hotel, 80 kilometres east of Melbourne, said in a statement posted on social media.

The hotel said it "could not speak more highly" of how players behaved.

"For such a young group, they were extremely respectful and a fun group of boys to deal with," the statement read.

Nick Blakey (left) is one of the Swans suspended for breaching club standards. (AAP Image: Dean Lewins)

"They enjoyed a few quiet beers to unwind after a long season and we see nothing wrong with that.

"They had booked out the venue for the afternoon, so they were the only patrons on site.

"They enjoyed their afternoon and moved on."

The hotel noted media were waiting for the Tigers players "in the hope of capturing a misstep, which we consider disappointing".

The Richmond footage emerged hours after AFL chief executive Andrew Dillon fronted the media for the first time since the Swans scandal began.

"I have been asked a lot in recent days, what message football should be sending young people and what we should be saying to our kids," Dillon said.

"For me, the answer is straightforward: it doesn't matter who you are, it doesn't matter what you do, whether you're an AFL footballer — the way we treat women says a lot about who we are as people, as a community and as a game.

"Quite simply, respect for women is not negotiable."

Dillon said the actions of the five suspended Swans players had "fallen well short of the standards our game expects and community deserves".

"While there are players involved, we cannot lose sight of the bigger picture. More importantly, there are women who have made a report to police and they should be shown care and respect," he said.

World.title: NRL changes rules to allow Jai Arrow to 'play' 100 games for Souths
World.content:
Jai Arrow will make cameo appearances in the final two rounds of the regular season in order to reach 100 games for South Sydney.

In one of the feel-good stories of the NRL season, the forward who retired with motor neurone disease in May has been approved to start on the field in rounds 26 and 27.

Arrow will then be substituted out in the opening seconds before any active involvement in play.

Arrow, in jersey number 23, has been named co-captain with Cameron Murray, who is listed to come off the bench.

It came after the Rabbitohs made an appeal to the NRL to grant the former Queensland representative an on-field swansong while still able to walk and run.

The initiative gives Arrow two final chances to farewell an NRL career that featured a grand-final appearance in 2021 and 12 State of Origin caps.

The NRL has granted Souths special dispensation to name Arrow as an extra player on today's team list and an extra substitution in their rotation.

Arrow vows to help others fight MND Former NRL player Jai Arrow says he is determined to raise money and awareness for Motor Neurone Disease until a cure is found.

The matches, against Gold Coast and the Sydney Roosters, will bring Arrow's tally to 180 career games and 100 for the Rabbitohs.

Arrow will lead the team out on both occasions and sit on the interchange bench in Souths kit after being substituted out.

The Titans and Roosters have both approved the plan, as have the Rugby League Players Association.

"We are very grateful to Peter [V'landys] and the NRL, and Clint [Newton] at the RLPA, for supporting our proposal," Souths chief executive Blake Solly said.

"We believe this will provide great inspiration for everyone watching the game from the stadium or at home, showing that MND will not hold Jai, or anyone else, back from achieving what they want to achieve in life."

The NRL world has rallied around Arrow since his shock diagnosis and immediate retirement in May.

The league threw Arrow "the world's biggest birthday party" on the day Souths beat Newcastle in July, rolling out a birthday cake in the shape of the 31-year-old's jersey and presenting him with a commemorative jersey.

Fundraising efforts have already passed $1 million in support of Arrow, who is the father of a young daughter.

Players from all clubs have shown their support by marking tries with arrow celebrations throughout the month of July.

World.title: McVeigh to canvass Hird return as icon urges Bombers fans to unite
World.content:
New Essendon coach Mark McVeigh says he will speak to James Hird about returning to the club in a different capacity after a second failed bid to be coach.

McVeigh was unveiled on Tuesday in a press conference that was also attended by a number of Essendon's current players.

Both he and club president Andrew Welsh indicated their desire to have Hird involved.

"I'd love to see James as a part of the club going forward. He's such a fantastic football person," Welsh said.

"I feel there's significant value James can bring, not just tokenistic, but real value to our club and our playing group.

"Certainly, part of my messaging was that Mark and I would want to catch up with him when the time is appropriate."

While Welsh said a pair of calls to Hird had gone unanswered on Monday night, McVeigh said he had shared a conversation with his former captain.

"I love James Hird, he's one of my best mates. It was difficult to go through the process against a good friend," he said.

McVeigh (right) called Hird (left) one of his "best mates" after beating him to the Essendon job. (Getty Images: Ryan Pierse)

"I don't fear those people [Hird's supporters], I actually embrace how they feel, and I understand it, to be fair.

"He's been a constant in my life since I was 17 years of age. We spoke this morning, and the way he spoke of how proud he was of this moment for me, it hasn't broken us, we're still together, but I understand and embrace the feelings of the people that love James Hird, because I do too."

McVeigh, Welsh and club CEO Tim Roberts called for unity at the club amid rumours of a potential board challenge from unimpressed Hird fans.

"I don't ask for your patience, I ask for your re-alignment to our club," McVeigh said.

"I sit here year after year, and we get people coming out of the shadows that want to challenge the board," added Welsh.

"I can tell you since I've been here that this club has never been more united.

"These people want to keep living in the shadows and keep on trying to destabilise our club, we don't jump at shadows.

"We're a strong club and we'll continue to make sure that we make the right decisions on behalf of our members and our teams and our staff to get this club moving forward again."

Tim Watson (pictured) has called for unity at Essendon after Mark McVeigh's signing. (Getty Images: Michael Willson)

The plea for unity came as Essendon legend Tim Watson has the club's passionate supporters to "put [their] weapons down".

"There's got to be a unification of the club now," he told SEN on Tuesday morning.

"People have to put down their weapons and get behind this appointment of a former player — somebody who has been passionate about the football club.

"This is part of the healing process that needs to take place. Ultimately, it's a much bigger thing than the emotion that might be associated with it now. There is an enormous amount of work to do.

Live Moment Look back at Mark McVeigh's first press conference as Essendon's new senior coach. McVeigh says Bombers 'won't live in the past' Pretty good way to end the press conference from the new Essendon coach. He receives another round of applause from those in attendance before walking off the podium. Welsh with another clue on Hird returning I reckon it's going to be a full-court press on the Dons trying to get Hird to say yes to some kind of role within the club. "We have great people that we want to get back involved with the club in meaningful ways," Welsh says. "I look at this as a point that we can re-align that passion." McVeigh with an insight into his game plan McVeigh explains what areas he's going to try and fix on-field. "In the phases of the game, we can't focus on one. If you look at the numbers, we're the bottom of the table in a lot of areas. "I do want them to be brave, I do want them to play with flare, but we do need to fix up our defence. "They [the players] need to come back prepared physically and ready to learn. "The system we'll put in place, you need to understand, otherwise you'll get found out. "When we get all three phases going in the right direction, Essendon will fly." Show more

"Congratulations to him. He's been an Essendon man all his life. He's loved this football club, that was clear in the days that he played.

"He's had a great development profile if you look at where he's been and what he's been doing. He's been part of elite coaching departments [at GWS and Sydney]."

McVeigh has signed a three-year contract with Essendon and was the unanimous choice of the Essendon board.

World.title: Piastri searching for answers as teammate re-enters F1 title picture
World.content:
Oscar Piastri's "disappointing" end to the Dutch Grand Prix has left the Australian and his McLaren team searching for answers, while his teammate has roared back into the Formula 1 title picture.

Last weekend in Zandvoort was shaping to be a good weekend for Piastri.

The Australian was matching the pace at the front through qualifying, and after a terrific second start in the grand prix following Max Verstappen's heavy crash, Piastri was on course for a first podium finish since Miami in May.

Piastri struggles after slow pit stop, Norris wins as Verstappen crashes Reigning world champion Lando Norris has doubled his grand prix win tally in 2026, producing a pair of brilliant overtakes to win the Dutch Grand Prix.

Piastri had performed a breathtaking overtake on Mercedes driver George Russell to move into third and was not far off the pace set by leaders Kimi Antonelli and teammate Lando Norris, despite being on a harder compound tyre.

But a slow first pit stop knocked Piastri back behind Russell and out of third place, and it only got worse from there.

Piastri, who won the Dutch Grand Prix in 2025, fell right off the pace and finished a distant sixth as Norris surged to victory.

Piastri was running third until a slow pit stop knocked him out of the podium position at Zandvoort. (Reuters: Benoit Tessier)

The sudden pace drop-off has left Piastri with plenty of questions that he and the team will want answers to.

"The first stint felt reasonable, but from the second stint onwards, the pace was simply not there, and it became a real struggle," he said.

"We will review the entire weekend and analyse to understand why we experienced such a significant performance drop-off.

"A slow pit stop didn't help, but the fundamental issue was the lack of pace, which is something we'll work on ahead of Monza.

"That's the priority now, to dig into the data with the team to find the root cause and ensure we can move forward in a more positive direction for the upcoming races."

Piastri's situation is a far cry from where he was at the conclusion of last year's Dutch Grand Prix, when he claimed his seventh grand prix win of the season and was the championship leader.

But while Piastri is seeking answers to get back to the front of the grid, Norris is threatening to stay there.

'The fight's still on': Norris re-enters the F1 title picture

McLaren entered the 2026 season having won the previous two constructors' championships, and with Lando Norris as reigning drivers' champion.

Reigning Formula 1 drivers' champion Lando Norris has won the past two grands prix. (Reuters: Benoit Tessier)

But with a new era of regulations, McLaren's 2026 season started poorly.

Piastri crashed on his way to the grid in Melbourne and he and Norris did not start in Shanghai due to car issues.

Norris then had back-to-back retirements in Montreal and Monaco, meaning he failed to finish three of the opening six grands prix.

But the reigning world champion has returned to winning ways, triumphing in Hungary before the mid-year break and then again last weekend in the Netherlands.

With back-to-back wins and growing confidence in his season, Norris has re-emerged as a drivers' championship contender.

F1 drivers' championship standings after Dutch Grand Prix 242 — Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes

183 — George Russell, Mercedes

183 — Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

159 — Lando Norris, McLaren

155 — Charles Leclerc, Ferrari

With 10 or 11 rounds remaining this season, depending on conflict in the Middle East, Norris is sitting fourth in the standings, 83 points behind leader Kimi Antonelli.

It is a huge gap, but recent history shows it is not an impossible feat.

At the conclusion of last year's Dutch Grand Prix, Max Verstappen was 104 points behind then-leader Piastri with nine rounds remaining.

Verstappen surged towards the end of the season while Piastri slumped. Verstappen fell two points shy of Norris in the standings, but finished a stunning 11 points ahead of Piastri.

Having seen what is possible, Norris has made this year's title fight a four-way race with Antonelli, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton.

Norris's message to his team over the radio after taking the chequered flag on Sunday certainly sounded like the Briton believed his championship hopes are far from over.

"Let's keep pushing. Thank you for the hard work. Let's keep bringing upgrades, let's keep bringing performance, please," he said.

"The fight's still on."

Out of the car, Norris was quick to point out that there is a long season still ahead of the drivers and that he was not getting ahead of himself with an 83-point deficit.

"One race at a time. A lot of people say it now, but it is the truth of it. There's no point in thinking that far ahead," he said after winning on Sunday.

"There are plenty of things we can do better, and we need to do better if we want to fight for a championship.

"We have to keep working hard. There's still plenty of races, plenty of opportunity for everyone."

Norris's deficit to Antonelli was 101 points prior to the weekend in Hungary, but the McLaren champion has reduced that by 18 with two tremendous weekends.

However, the 83-point gap is significant and Antonelli has extended his overall championship lead.

Entering the Dutch Grand Prix weekend, the young Italian's lead over Hamilton was 50 points, and 59 over Russell.

After the weekend, his lead is 59 points over both Hamilton and Russell.

F1 heads to Monza for the Italian Grand Prix in two weeks, one of the fastest tracks on the calendar and vastly different to the tight and twisting circuits in Hungary and the Netherlands where Norris has won this year.

World.title: 'A dangerous individual': Ex-snooker champ convicted of child sex abuse
World.content:
Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been convicted of sexually abusing two primary school children in Scotland in the 1990s and early 2000s.

Dott, 49, was found guilty of abusing a girl from 1993-96 and a boy from 2006-10 after a five-day trial at the High Court in Glasgow. The judge ordered Dott to be held in custody ahead of his sentencing on September 29.

The woman, now in her 40s, testified that Dott sexually abused her on multiple occasions, "caressing" her bottom over her clothing, exposing himself and touching her with parts of his body, including his penis.

The man, now in his late 20s, said he was abused on multiple occasions, with Dott touching him inappropriately, kissing him and performing sexual acts.

Dott with his wife Elaine after winning the snooker world championship in 2006. (Getty Images: Rui Vieira)

"Dott is a dangerous individual, and I hope this conviction provides some measure of comfort to those impacted by his crimes," Detective Inspector Gary Smillie from Police Scotland said.

Snooker's governing body suspended Dott in April 2025 after he was charged in the case. The Scot was ranked number 56 in the world at the time and dropped from the rankings after the season.

On Monday, the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association revoked Dott's membership following an emergency board meeting. The WPBSA also said it wrote to the World Snooker Tour to request his immediate removal from the WST Hall of Fame.

Dott won the World Snooker Championship in 2006 and was a runner-up twice.

AP/Reuters

World.title: Zak Butters trade rumours dominate Port Adelaide's turbulent season
World.content:
It's been a tumultuous year for Port Adelaide.

Its newly-appointed coach Josh Carr had to navigate a new system with an injury riddled list; using 39 of its 44-listed players and finishing the season with 15 unavailable.

He also had to build chemistry and belief despite a contract decision overshadowing his campaign.

Its vice-captain and dual All-Australian Zak Butters has dominated headlines all season as one of the biggest free-agents available this off-season; and has now confirmed the worst-kept secret in football that he has requested a trade to Victoria.

"I've made a decision to head home. It's obviously been one that I've wrestled with for a while now. It's been a tough decision and one that I haven't taken lightly," Butters said on Monday.

"Although I've loved my time in Adelaide … I'm probably at a stage in my life where I'd like to get back around some family and friends and enjoy some more time with them."

Butters denied reports in June that he had begun telling those close to him he was eager to move east after a trip back home during the round 12 bye; another chapter in a compendium of updates on the dual Showdown medallist's future.

So why was the club so protective of Butters when he had a foot out the door?

There are two key foundations of any negotiation in any industry. Value and relationships.

Growing speculation

As the weeks progressed and the speculation grew, the four-horse race between Richmond, Geelong, Collingwood and the Western Bulldogs intensified as the coverage evolved into a public bidding war; increasing Butters' contract terms and giving the Power fuel for higher trade demands.

Every story has a source … and every source has an agenda.

Zak Butters to leave Port Adelaide Star Port Adelaide midfielder Zak Butters has informed the Power he wants to return to Victoria.

Player agents are looking to maximise demand and clubs want their outgoing stars to leave at a high price.

Relationships between the two parties are also incredibly important in future dealings. Clubs are constantly trying to find the balance between fair compensation and long-term favours.

For Port Adelaide this was the case two years ago when Dan Houston was desperate to move to Collingwood but the Magpies didn't have the capital for a reasonable return.

The Power settled for Picks 13, 29 and 36 plus forwards Jack Lukosius and Joe Richards in exchange for its dual All-Australian defender and a future first round pick.

It was a move that was widely panned at the time but hasn't done much damage given rising key forward Jack Whitlock was taken at 29 and Joe Richards is developing into a handy midfield option.

But Dan Houston and Zak Butters are different cases.

The Power is hoping to maximise its draft haul in moving its triple best-and-fairest winner given it has rarely had early selections in recent years leading to a gulf in young talent depth.

It also has a litany of upcoming academy and father-son draftees it will need to match bids on, such as expected number one pick Dougie Cochrane and Zemes Pilot.

Matthew Richardson spoke about the Butters trade rumous in May. (ABC News: Marco Catalano)

Back in May, Port chief executive Matthew Richardson flagged on ABC Sport that the club would match any bid on Butters to force a trade given the star is a restricted free agent.

"There will be offers that we can match and we will match. It does give the club a fair bit of control in what happens," he said.

The issue is Butters current suitors have a diverse availability of picks at their disposal and the Power's best option Richmond doesn't quite align with the values Butters claimed he was eyeing when I asked him back in March what would dictate his decision.

"I think you're stupid if you don't want to win premierships," he said.

"I want to win. Family is important as well … but you can't look too far ahead."

THE CONTENDERS (As of current ladder position, all four clubs have all future picks available) Geelong: 17, 35, 53, 71

Western Bulldogs: 10, 28, 46

Collingwood: 16, 34, 63, 66, 70

Richmond: 2, 20, 38, 56

While Port navigates its way through the 20 out-of-contract players it has held fire on due to the Butters decision, there will be time for Josh Carr to reflect on his inaugural season at the helm.

Season highlights

Despite double ups with four sides who missed finals; the Power managed seven wins in 2026 and had a clear narrative throughout; it could match it with the best but could rarely beat them.

Its campaign ended with an equal league record five losses by five-points or less and eight by as much as 14-points.

A Showdown win over Adelaide in June was the highlight, plus its April upset over Geelong; but its only road wins were against fellow bottom four sides West Coast and Richmond.

It finished 16th for ball movement from D50 to F50 but defensively was a powerhouse until the final month where 10-goal losses to the Lions, Swans and Demons blew out the team's average points against to 89, dropping it down from a Top 4 side into 10th.

The other positive was its clearance work. Despite missing Connor Rozee for the majority of the campaign, and Zak Butters for the final month, the side finished second for clearance differential, blooding future stars in Jase Burgoyne, Joe Richards and Miles Bergman on ball.

Port Adelaide won seven games in the 2026 season. (ABC Riverland: Catherine Heuzenroeder)

From a list perspective it was the only side not to have a player named in the AFL's 22-under-22 squad and some of the long-term signings from the Hinkley era like Todd Marshall and Brandon Zerk-Thatcher barely featured.

Former Port midfielder and four times Showdown medallist Josh Francou believes 2026 was a free hit for Josh Carr.

"It has been a difficult campaign … the way they're defending the ground is a real plus for them but they struggle to move the ball," he said.

"Next year things start to ramp up on Josh Carr and he's got to get it right."

Despite all the adversities, it feels like Josh Carr has laid the foundation for success but a critical off-season awaits as he looks to reshape the list and keep his stars healthy for the 2027 campaign.

World.title: Cyclists run for cover as hailstorm forces La Vuelta stage cancellation
World.content:
A torrential hailstorm in the French Pyrenees forced the abandonment of the third stage of the Vuelta a España on Monday.

With 15 kilometres remaining of the 174-km route from Gruissan to Font-Romeu, the skies darkened as the peloton neared the top of the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began bouncing off the tarmac and pelting the riders.

Mats Wenzel (Kern Pharma) and Lorenzo Fortunato (XDS Astana) were 25 seconds ahead of the peloton when the elements intervened, as race leader and favourite Tadej Pogacar was seen indicating to the peloton to pull off the course.

Bedraggled riders were then seen getting off their bikes and shuffling into a hotel for shelter.

Shortly afterwards, race organisers, ASO, announced the stage would not resume, leaving fans frustrated at the finish where thick layers of hail blanketed the road.

Slovenia's Pogacar (UAE Emirates-XRG) retained his overall lead of nine seconds from Belgium's Wout van Aert (Dutch Visma-Lease a Bike) with Britain's Matt Brennan 10 seconds back.

Earlier it had been warm and sunny on the flat approaches to the mountainous finish with no sign of the chaos to come as a five-man breakaway group stayed out ahead.

Pogacar, bidding to complete his Grand Tour collection by winning the Vuelta for the first time, was always near the front of the pack with his team setting the pace.

Sadly, his expected challenge for the stage victory fell foul of the weather in an anticlimactic finish.

He will get his chance to underline his superiority again on Tuesday, though with stage four featuring three first-category climbs as the race starts and finishes in Andorra la Vella.

Reuters

Tech.title: Dreame’s dream of a rocket-powered car is dead
Tech.content:
is transportation editor with 10+ years of experience who covers EVs, public transportation, and aviation. His work has appeared in The New York Daily News and City & State.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Dreame, the Chinese vacuum company that aspires to be a global technology giant, is reportedly shutting down its automotive project after funding from the government dried up.

According to CarNewsChina, the company’s automotive division called “Project Starry Sky” once employed over 1,000 people, but now only a handful legal and HR staffers remain, charged with winding down the operation. In a statement, Dreame said it “recently adjusted certain operations that were in the exploratory phase,” and that going forward, it would focus on four key business areas: “smart home, outdoor/garden, smart mobility, and embodied AI.” (A spokesperson for the company didn’t respond to a request for comment.)

The news comes after China’s government issued new rules aimed at tightening oversight of the $3.4 trillion private fund industry, singling out Dreame in the process. After becoming one of the world’s largest manufacturer of vacuums, the company quickly moved into a variety of new businesses, spawning nearly a thousand affiliated ventures related to smartphones, robotics, and cars. But much of that expansion was funded by China’s government — and the government is now starting to take a closer look at how Dreame spends that money, according to CNBC.

The NEXT 01 JET Edition Car at the Dreame NEXT event during the Silicon Valley Summit at the Palace of Fine Arts on April 29, 2026 in San Francisco, CA. Photo by Kelsey McClellan / The Verge

Dreame wowed audiences at a San Francisco expo earlier this year with “Nebula Next 01 Jet Edition,” a sleek looking concept car equipped with a pair of rocket engines that theoretically can accelerate from 0 to 60 mph in 0.9 seconds. The vehicle was allegedly equipped with a sulfide-based solid-state battery with a record-breaking energy density exceeding 450 Wh/kg and a purported range of over 550 km (341.7 miles). The company claimed its boosters would deliver 100 kilo-Newtons of force.

But the concept raised a lot of questions, including some basic ones about how Dreame could make a car accelerate so quickly without breaking the laws of physics. Apparently Dreame didn’t have any answers to these questions, as the car itself was fully vaporware. Former employees told China Economy that the concept that was shown off in San Francisco lacked an actual chassis and was driven via remote control. (Concept cars are rarely “real” cars, in the technical sense — but even this is a little shocking in its level of deception.)

The news that Dreame’s vaporware car was totally vaporware will come as little shock to those familiar with the showy, boastful promises of companies that have never actually built a car suddenly deciding to build a car. Faraday Future, another Chinese companies with ambitions to build all manner of electric, autonomous vehicles, ran into this exact problem nearly a decade ago. And it also faced accusations of operating self-driving cars for public demos via offstage remote control.

Tech.title: Bose’s smallest Bluetooth speaker is a great deal at 35 percent off
Tech.content:
Bose may be best known for its QuietComfort headphones , but the brand’s Bluetooth speakers have earned a great reputation for featuring great sound and build quality. The compact Bose SoundLink Micro — its most compact Bluetooth speaker — is currently discounted to $79.99 at Amazon , a pretty great discount from its usual $129 price tag.

The rounded-off square speaker is almost pocketable, and easily slides into a purse or backpack; it’s just over four inches wide, 1.54 inches deep, and weighs less than a pound. It’s dustproof and waterproof, with an IP67 rating that matches the larger Bose Bluetooth speakers, and should last a full day at the beach or by the pool. The speaker will run for up to 12 hours on a single charge, and has convenient nylon strap for attaching it to your backpack or to your bike’s handlebars.

Tech.title: Instagram’s ‘First Draft’ trims your Reels clips for you
Tech.content:
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Instagram is launching a new Reels-editing feature that automatically trims your video clips to focus on the highlights. The feature, called First Draft, is rolling out to Instagram’s iPhone app and provides a “starting point” that you can build upon with other edits, according to an announcement on Tuesday.

An example shared by Instagram shows a user selecting multiple clips for a reel and then tapping the “First Draft” button. From there, Instagram analyzes the clips — each of which is more than a minute long — before trimming them down to eliminate pauses and showcase the most important parts. Instagram then combines the snippets into a reel that’s ready to edit and share.

It sounds similar to Adobe’s AI-powered Quick Cut feature, which automatically combines clips based on a prompt. But unlike Adobe’s feature, Instagram’s First Draft tool doesn’t use AI, according to Nicole Rechtszaid, the head of communications at Instagram.

Instagram says First Draft works with “multi-clip montages, talking-head videos, and day-in-the-life content.” You can find the feature by opening the camera app in Instagram, filming your video, and tapping the First Draft Button. You can also find it in your Reels gallery after selecting more than one clip.

Update, August 25th: Added confirmation that First Draft doesn’t use AI.

Tech.title: Nothing OS 5.0 brings a new Glyph Interface app and a more customizable homescreen
Tech.content:
is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

With the new design of Nothing OS 5.0, app icons and widgets can use adaptive color to get color tints pulled from your wallpaper, which update whenever your wallpaper changes. Alongside Android’s built-in Dynamic Colors, the company says it allows you to have specific elements change to match your wallpaper “while Nothing’s predominantly monochrome character stays underneath.”

While I like Nothing’s simplified, monochrome app icons, it’s nice to get an option for adding some limited areas of color to the homescreen. Nothing’s launching it as “an additional theme,” so you can keep using the old design if you like.

The Android 17-based update is launching in open beta on August 26th, starting with the Nothing Phone 3. It will eventually also roll out to most of Nothing’s other phones, but a few older devices aren’t getting this update, including the Phone 1, Phone 2, and CMF Phone 1 — the last of which I’ve been using, so unfortunately I won’t get to try out these new features myself.

Most Nothing phones will get the update by January 2027. Image: Nothing

The latest version of Nothing OS also adds a slew of new homescreen customization options and quality-of-life tweaks that will let you track how long you spend away from your phone, or make better use of its Essential AI features. And if you have a Nothing phone with its glyph interface lighting, a new dedicated app pulls all the features and controls into one spot.

You can control Nothing’s glyph lights from a dedicated app now. Photo: Dominic Preston / The Verge

Lockscreen clockfaces can also use colors from your wallpaper now. There are also a couple of new lockscreen clockfaces in Nothing OS 5.0, including a bubbly “Gooey” design and an information-dense “Micrographics” one.

Since Nothing OS 5.0 is built on Android 17, it also includes platform updates like enhanced quick share, Android’s new Noto 3D emojis, and expanded dark theme support. Other new highlights include:

“Geist” system typeface

Away Time widget that tracks how long you haven’t been using your phone, and Collector widget that turns pictures of items into home or lock screen icons

Select multiple homescreen app icons to move them all at once

Status bar icons with animations to signify things like turning airplane mode on or off

Single-tap Bluetooth controls in Quick Settings

Essential AI updates including support for Model Context Protocol (MCP), cleaner transcriptions from Essential Voice, a Smart Collections feature for organizing Essential Space captures, and support for building Essential Apps on-device

Tech.title: GeForce Now is getting support for the Steam Controller
Tech.content:
is a senior reporter covering technology, gaming, and more. He joined The Verge in 2019 after nearly two years at Techmeme.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Nvidia’s GeForce Now cloud gaming service will officially support Valve’s Steam Controller and Steam Machine starting later this year. With Steam Controller support, you’ll be able to play games with Valve’s great new gamepad when using the GeForce Now app on your Steam Deck or Steam Machine. If you’re using GeForce Now on Windows or macOS, support for the Steam Controller is coming “later,” Nvidia says.

GeForce Now is getting a few other upgrades, too. Nvidia will soon add new DLSS 4.5 controls for DLSS Super Resolution, Dynamic Frame Generation, and Ray Reconstruction. (Ray Reconstruction is also officially launching for RTX GPUs in early access.) The previously-announced GOG single sign on is now available. The service will come to more of Amazon’s Fire TV Sticks “later this year,” and you’ll be able to buy a subscription through Amazon. And as of last week, you can officially use GeForce Now on Firefox.

Nvidia’s Gamescom announcements also include news for its upcoming RTX Spark chip family: EA, Embark, and Ubisoft are planning to support the chip, which is set to launch this fall, with games like EA Sports F1 25, Apex Legends, Arc Raiders, and Anno 117: Pax Romana. EA is also working on native support for its Javelin Anticheat technology for the company’s “biggest multiplayer games.”

Nvidia also shared details about 007 First Light’s path tracing update launching in September, upgrades to RTX Remix, and more, and you can read about everything that’s new in the company’s blog post.

Tech.title: Polestar claims it was blindsided by sales ban
Tech.content:
is transportation editor with 10+ years of experience who covers EVs, public transportation, and aviation. His work has appeared in The New York Daily News and City & State.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

Polestar said the Trump administration strung it along for months before finally rejecting its request to continue selling its electric vehicles in the US under a rule outlawing vehicles with connected software from China.

In an August 18th letter sent to dealers and obtained by The Verge, Polestar said it doesn’t have a clear answer as to why its application to continue selling its EVs in the US was denied, considering its sister company Volvo was authorized to sell its vehicles despite similar corporate ownership. (The letter was first reported by The Wall Street Journal.)

The US Department of Commerce approved Volvo in May 2026 to continue importing and selling its vehicles in the US, despite restrictions tied to its majority Chinese owner, Geely. But one month later, the department rejected Polestar’s similar request, leading to the company to announce it would stop selling its vehicles in the US starting with the 2027 model year. The rule, which originated under the Biden administration, bans the import and sale of vehicles with connected software from hostile countries, including China.

In the letter to dealers, Polestar’s head of product Peter Wexler lays out the timeline of the company’s communications with the Trump administration, starting with a May 29, 2025 application to the

Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) under the Commerce Department. In subsequent meetings, Wexler says Polestar was given the impression that Polestar would be approved, considering its vehicles are functionally similar to Volvo’s.

Jeffrey Kessler, Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security, said during an in-person meeting with Polestar’s representatives “that it would be reasonable for Polestar to expect approval of its applications if Volvo Cars was approved to sell its cars under effectively the same shareholding and ownership structure and with the same hardware and software in the Polestar 3 as the Volvo EX90,” Wexler writes.

Polestar told the administration it open to a variety of “mitigation measures” to ensure its vehicles were compliant with the ban on Chinese software, including regular audits, geographic restrictions on data storage and management, and limitations on digital keys and remote access. But the administration declined all such offers, Wexler said.

“BIS never engaged in any such discussions with Polestar,” he writes. “Instead, BIS communicated that it had all the information it required to render a decision.”

Wexler said that Polestar is continuing to press the administration for an explanation on why it was denied approval. The company was sued recently by Polestar dealer Prestige Imports in New Jersey, which accuses the company of engineering its own exit from the US by failing to do enough to satisfy regulators at the Commerce Department.

Tech.title: Stability AI, maker of image generator Stable Diffusion, raises $76 million in fresh funding
Tech.content:
Stability AI, the startup behind AI image generation model Stable Diffusion, has raised $76 million in Series B funding. The new haul brings the company’s fundraising total to $232 million.

The company announced the round Tuesday, saying the new capital comes partly from a number of prominent entertainment industry organizations, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music Group, and Warner Music Group, and gaming giant Electronic Arts (EA). Two investment firms, AMD Ventures and Pacific Alliance Ventures, also took part.

It’s an unusual roster and less a typical venture round than a lineup of the companies Stability now depends on for content licensing and distribution deals.

Stability AI CEO Prem Akkaraju, who joined the company in 2024, called the funding “an affirmation of our vision where generative AI empowers every producer, musician, and storyteller.” Akkaraju joined the company in 2024.

The company says it plans to use the money from its latest funding round to continue building out its “creative production” product suite while also expanding its professional services arm. Currently, Stability offers a variety of AI models that are designed for the purposes of AI music, video, and image generation.

Stability, founded in 2019, has spent the past year signing deals to weave generative AI into entertainment companies’ creative workflows. It struck partnerships with Universal Music and EA last October and with Warner Music last November, each giving those companies a hand in co-developing Stability’s AI tools rather than just licensing the output..

Stability has also had a mostly winning stretch in court. The company largely prevailed in a copyright lawsuit brought by Getty Images in the United Kingdom, which had accused the company of infringing upon IP rights by using the company’s images in the training of its image generation model. A judge ruled largely in Stability’s favor in that case, but a similar lawsuit from Getty in the U.S. is still working its way through the courts.

Stability was also sued in 2023 by the company’s co-founder, Cyrus Hodes, who claimed that he was tricked by the other co-founder, Emad Mostaque, into selling his share in the company.

Tech.title: SpaceX will build a second, $100B ‘Starbase’ spaceport in Louisiana
Tech.content:
SpaceX has announced it will build a second spaceport for future launches of its Starship mega-rocket at a former Exxon property in Louisiana, ending what the company says was a seven-year search for a suitable location.

The new launch site will sit along the Gulf Coast in Vermilion Parish, west of New Orleans and roughly 10 hours from the company’s existing Starbase complex in South Texas. SpaceX says it is investing $100 billion, with construction starting in 2027. SpaceX claims the first Starship launch will take place in 2029.

Louisiana Economic Development (LED), the state agency that oversees business development, offers a slightly more conservative timeline. It says construction will start by the end of 2027 with “initial operations expected to come online in 2030.”

Before any of that happens, SpaceX is still trying to prove that it can fly Starship into low-Earth orbit and make the rocket reusable, like its existing Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets. SpaceX has performed 13 test flights of Starship since 2023, and while the company has ticked off a lot of development boxes, it still has a lot of work to do.

An upcoming 14th test flight could see SpaceX send Starship’s upper stage to orbit for the first time. But the company has yet to return both the booster and the upper stage to the launch pad on a single flight, a basic necessity if Starship is to become truly reusable. Even then, SpaceX must show that it can bring the vehicle back and refurbish it quickly enough to reach its own aggressive goal of sending up multiple Starships per week.

That isn’t stopping SpaceX from betting almost everything on Starship. This past week, SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said he will retire the Falcon rockets once Starship is flying multiple times per week. His comments confirmed earlier reporting from Bloomberg News that the company was already telling prospective customers about the impending end of the Falcon program.

SpaceX has spent more than $8 billion developing Starship, according to filings submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The rocket — which is the largest and most powerful ever built — is crucial to maintaining and growing the only profitable part of SpaceX’s business, its Starlink satellite internet service. SpaceX is also planning to build an entire network of satellites dedicated to AI processing, which it needs Starship to launch.

The new Starbase site will create 3,000 direct new jobs over 10 years, with an average annual salary of $92,600, according to LED. More than 30,000 construction jobs are expected at the peak of the buildout.

It’s not immediately clear if SpaceX intends to create a company town around the new Starbase site, like the one it has architected in Texas. The Texas municipality, once called Boca Chica and renamed Starbase, has its own ZIP code and volunteer fire station, and is building its own police force and community library. It is run by a local government filled with SpaceX employees (or family members of SpaceX employees).

SpaceX did say in its announcement that it wants to make the new site a “self-sustaining spaceport” with “propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle processing facilities, and an airport.”

As a mix of a launch complex and active construction zone, the Starbase site in Texas has also seen extremely high injury rates over the last decade. It’s the most dangerous site SpaceX operates and the company has reported hundreds of injuries to the Occupational Health and Safety Administration. In May, a construction worker employed by a third-party contractor fell to his death at Starbase.

“We are very excited to be in this position to receive one of the best opportunities of a lifetime which will bring not only a variety of jobs to our Parish but will offer opportunities to our grandchildren allowing them to stay home for employment,” Vermilion Parish Police Jury President Chad Vallo said in a statement.

SpaceX, which has for years faced criticism for — and fought legal battles over — how it treats the local ecosystem around its Texas site, has “already engaged the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority and other appropriate state agencies to proactively address potential impacts to wildlife, fisheries and their supporting habitats,” according to LED.

The company also says it is “partnering with state and federal agencies to expand Louisiana’s Coastal Master Plan and Coastal Wetlands Planning, Protection and Restoration Act projects, including Gulf shoreline protection breakwaters designed to reduce wave energy” and reduce shoreline erosion in the area.

Tech.title: Your vote matters! Decide which Audience Choice sessions will make it to TechCrunch Founder Summit
Tech.content:
Each year, we get a huge influx of applicants to speak at TechCrunch’s events, and this year’s Founder Summit in Boston on November 4 will be no different! We want to thank everyone who applied to take part in our programming and to help share their expertise with the startup community.

After careful review, we have 11 finalists who are vying for four slots within this year’s event agenda, and each one showcases the kind of practical, essential insights that can only be delivered by those who have built, iterated, and succeeded.

You can vote via this link to weigh in on which sessions ultimately make the cut. Submissions will close on September 4. If you’re voting and haven’t already gotten your Founder Summit tickets this year, what are you waiting for?

On November 4 in Boston, you’ll get the chance to learn directly from the experts in intimate, exclusive sessions that can put you ahead of the competition or set you up to play a pivotal role in developing the next era of innovators. We still have discounts running on tickets that can save you up to $100 right here!

With that said, let’s dive into our Disrupt Audience Choice nominees, and remember: The voting takes place via this form, so take a look and then submit your vote!

How to Build Events Strategy Before You Can Afford a Full-Time Events Team

Alexandra Ames: Founder and Chief Event Strategist, Blueprint Lab

Early-stage founders approach events one of two ways: say yes to every opportunity, or avoid them entirely because the ROI feels impossible to justify. Neither is smart. Events can build your audience and credibility before product-market fit but only if you’re strategic about which ones deserve your time and budget. We’ll discuss how to think strategically when resources are tight, including how to maximize ROI from founder events like this one. You’ll leave with frameworks for prioritizing stage-appropriate event investments, tactics for proving value without complex tools, and clarity on when events make sense and when they don’t.

How to Build a “Made in the USA” Hardware Company and Actually Scale It

Hannan Happi: CEO and Co-Founder, Exowatt

Domestic manufacturing is back in the spotlight, but building hardware in the U.S. is still widely seen as too expensive to scale. This session explores how founders can design hardware companies that make “Made in the USA” economically viable from day one. We’ll break down supply chain strategy, cost structure, factory partnerships, and how policy tailwinds like the IRA and CHIPS Act change the equation. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for evaluating when domestic manufacturing can become a competitive advantage — not just a branding decision.

Build Something We Don’t Have a Word for Yet

Andy Tang: Partner, Draper Associates

Pitches that change industries rarely fit existing categories — and most investors will pass on them for exactly that reason. This talk explores why the most fundable startups are often the hardest ones to describe, and what that means for how you build and position yours. Founders will leave with a clearer sense of the difference between a market insight and a market-creating idea, and what it actually takes to get a pattern-matching investor to bet on something genuinely new — before the rest of the world has a name for it.

GraphRAG in Action: Stop Hallucinations with Knowledge Graphs

Shishir Tewar: Head of Enterprise Data Engineering, Procore Technologies

Are messy data sources causing your LLMs to hallucinate? Relational databases struggle to bridge the semantic gap for AI. Learn to build a production-ready GraphRAG pipeline that turns chaotic data into actionable insights. Actionable takeaways: Build an offline pipeline to resolve disjointed datasets into “golden records.” Translate flat records into an interconnected Neo4j knowledge graph. Deploy a secure, local LLM (Ollama) to translate natural language into validated Cypher queries. Give your AI the foundational data structure it needs!

The Enterprise AI Playbook: How to Close L’Oreal and Vodafone Before You Raise a Series A

Merve Kitapci: Managing Partner and CGO, ADIN.AI

Most founders chase product-market fit before landing enterprise clients. We did the opposite. This roundtable covers the exact motion for closing global enterprise accounts at pre-Series A: how to structure the first conversation with a Fortune 500 CMO; why agency partnerships accelerate enterprise sales; how to price with no brand recognition; and what zero organic churn means for your fundraising story. Attendees leave with a repeatable enterprise sales framework, an early-stage AI pricing model, and the three things that make a CMO say yes before legal sees the contract.

Lessons from 20 Years of Bootstrapping an Open Source Business to $50M+

Peter Farkas: CEO, Percona

Building a successful open source company without venture capital is rare — scaling it past $50 million in revenue is even rarer. This talk shares two decades of lessons from growing a commercial open source business from zero to global scale. We’ll cover product-market fit, monetizing open source while keeping the core free, building distributed teams before remote work was mainstream, and creating a repeatable go-to-market engine without outside funding. We’ll also discuss failures, hard lessons, and how to compete against well-funded alternatives while staying bootstrapped. Attendees will leave with practical strategies for scaling sustainably.

Small but Mighty: How AI Lets Lean Teams Outship the Giants

Linden Tibbets: CEO and Co-Founder, IFTTT

The playbook has flipped, and we have lived it firsthand. A five-person team can now outbuild, outship, and outmaneuver companies with 500 engineers. This roundtable gets into the tactical reality of running a lean, AI-powered team: which tools are actually worth your time, how to build workflows that compound instead of bloat, and where most teams are burning cycles on AI that goes nowhere. Walk away knowing how to audit your current stack for speed gaps, which AI-driven growth motions are converting right now, and how to use your small size as an advantage, not an excuse.

The Demo Trap: Why Impressive AI Doesn’t Always Build Real Companies

Jeff Mahler: Co-Founder and CTO, Ambi Robotics

In today’s AI boom, impressive demos can generate headlines, funding, and early excitement, but they rarely prove a real business by themselves. This session explores the gap between prototype performance and real-world deployment, and why many promising AI startups stall before reaching scale. Founders and investors will learn how to evaluate whether AI systems are truly ready for production, the operational and reliability metrics that matter most, and how to build companies that can move beyond hype to durable, real-world impact.

From CentOS to Rocky Linux: Building Movements That Outlast You

Gregory Kurtzer: CEO and Founder, CIQ

Greg Kurtzer helped create CentOS, one of the world’s most widely used operating systems, then founded CIQ and launched Rocky Linux when Red Hat discontinued CentOS. In this session, he shares hard-won lessons from building open source movements and a startup from scratch: why founders must leave ego at the door, then navigate the transition from hiring versatile generalists early, then moving to a team of specialists as you scale. He explains the mistake he almost made by dismissing the value of culture and core values, and what it really takes to build something durable.

The Healthcare AI Companies That Will Actually Matter

Vikram Chaudhery, PhD: CEO and Founder, Genoa Ventures

Most AI healthcare demos look incredible and ship nothing. The companies that will matter in 2026 aren’t the ones with the best models. They’re the ones that get decisions to clinicians in an actionable window and change what doctors actually do for the patient in real clinical workflows. This roundtable digs into what separates investable healthcare AI from expensive science fairs, where agentic systems are creating real value beyond copilots, what founders consistently get wrong before their Series A, and the bar that anyone funding, founding, or joining a healthcare AI company should apply.

How Technical AI Founders Get Into YC, a16z Speedrun, and Raise from Top-Tier VCs

George Bandarian: Founder and General Partner, Untapped Ventures

The best technical founders building in AI and robotics aren’t failing because of their product — they’re failing because they don’t understand what top investors are actually looking for. In this roundtable, early-stage technical founders will work through what YC, a16z speedrun, and top-tier VCs evaluate beyond the deck: founder-market fit signals, why most technical founders need a business counterpart earlier than they think, how to position an autonomous economy company for a lead investor, and what the fundraising process actually looks like before you have traction.
